meta.source: Souter, A Pocket Lexicon to the Greek New Testament (1916), proofread against the 1917 printing

words.s: ἄβυσσος (ἡ), the abyss, the unfathomable depth, an especially Jewish conception, the home of the dead and of evil spirits.

words.g: Adam, the first man, the first parent of the human race
words.s: Ἀδάμ (Hebr.), Adam, the first man, the first parent of the human race: ὁ ἔσχατος Ἀδάμ, its latest ideal representative, who inaugurates the new age, Jesus the Messiah (1 Cor. xv 45).

ἄζυμος, unleavened, especially in the neut. plur. τὰ ἄζυμα, the unleavened bread, a festival of the Hebrews, held from 15 to 21 Nisan, in commemoration of their deliverance from Egypt: in a moral sense, 1 Cor. v 7–8.
αἵρεσις (originally, choosing, choice), a self-chosen opinion: a religious or philosophical sect.
ἀλείφω, I anoint.
ἄμπελος, a vine.
ἀναγκάζω, I compel, I constrain.
ἀνατέλλω, (a) I make to rise, Mt. v 45; (b) I rise, shine (generally of the sun, and hence metaphorically).
ἄνω (adv.), up, above; ἕως ἄνω, up to the top, up to the brim, John ii 7; τὰ ἄνω, things above, heaven, the heavenly region: see ἀνώτερον.
ἀποστρέφω (seems mostly literary) (trans.), (a) I turn away (from); (b) (mid.) I turn myself away from; (c) (metaph.) I pervert, Lk. xxiii 14.
ἄρσην (ἄρρην), male.
ἀστραπή, a flash of lightning.
βόσκω, I feed.
γαστήρ, belly: often ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχειν, of a woman, to be pregnant (lit. to have [a child] in the belly).
γεμίζω, I fill, load.
γωνία, a corner.
δεῦρο, (originally hither, hence) (a) exclamatory, come; (b) temporal, now, the present, Rom. i 13.
διασκορπίζω, I scatter.
ἕβδομος, seventh.
εἰδωλόθυτος (of meat), sacrificed to an image (of a god).

words.g: I turn to confusion, put to shame
words.s: ἐντρέπω, (a) I turn to confusion, put to shame, e.g. 1 Cor. iv 14, 2 Thess. iii 14, Tit. ii 8; (b) mid. c. acc., meaning I reverence, e. g. Mk. xii 6, Heb. xii 9.
ἑξήκοντα, sixty.

words.g: I long for, strain after, desire greatly
words.s: ἐπιποθέω, I long for, strain after, desire greatly.
ἔρις, strife.

ἔσω, (adv.) within, inside, with verbs either of rest or of motion: ὁ ἔσω ἄνθρωπος, that part of man which is spiritual; οἱ ἔσω, those within (the church), members of the church, 1 Cor. v 12; (prep.) within, to within, inside, Mk. xv 16.
εὐάρεστος, well-pleasing (especially to God).
εὐώνυμος (lit. well-named, to avoid the evil omen attaching to the left), on the left-hand side, left: ἐξ εὐωνύμων, on the left.

words.g: an Israelite, one of the chosen people Israel
words.s: Ἰσραηλείτης (Ἰστραηλείτης), an Israelite, one of the chosen people Israel, a Jew.
Ἰωνᾶς (Hebr.), Jonah, the Old Testament prophet.
καθαιρέω, (a) I take down, pull down; (b) I depose, Lk. i 52, cf. 2 Cor. x 4, c. gen. I diminish aught from, Ac. xix 27; (c) I destroy, Ac. xiii 19.
Καϊάφας (Καϊαφᾶς) (Old Latin and Sahidic Καίφας), Caiaphas, Jewish high priest.

words.g: I lead down, I bring down
words.s: κατάγω, I lead down, I bring down, either from a high place on land to a lower (or actually to the sea-coast), or from the high seas to land.
κατάπαυσις (in O.T. of the rest attained by the settlement in Canaan), resting, rest.

words.g: Cephas, the new name given to Simon, the disciple
words.s: Κηφᾶς, Cephas (Aram. for rock), the new name given to Simon, the disciple.
κίνδυνος, danger, peril, risk.
κλάσμα, a fragment.
κλαυθμός, weeping.
κλίνη, a couch, a bed, alike a mere mat (e.g. Mt. ix 2, 6), and a more elaborate structure (e.g. Mk. iv 21); possibly a bier in Rev. ii 22.
κραυγάζω, I cry aloud, shout.

words.g: I beat a door with a stick, to gain admittance
words.s: κρούω (pulso), I beat a door with a stick, to gain admittance.
λαμπάς, a lamp, a lantern.
λαμπρός, shining, glossy, bright.
λεπρός, a leprous person, a leper.
λέων, a lion: ἐκ τῆς φυλῆς Ἰούδα applied to Jesus, Rev. v 5 (after Gen. xlix 9): in 2 Tim. iv 17 used proverbially for very great danger.
μαργαρίτης (margarita), a pearl.
μεστός, full; met. (cf. πλήρης) almost tainted, diseased with, Mt. xxiii 28, Rom. i 29.

μεταξύ, (prep.) between: μεταξὺ σοῦ καὶ αὐτοῦ μόνου (Aramaic idiom), privately, Mt. xviii 15, μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων, in their mutual intercourse, Rom. ii 15; (adv.) with ὁ in the sense the next, the next after (because between the present and the one after that), Ac. xiii 42, ἐν τῷ μεταξύ (sc. χρόνῳ), meantime, meanwhile, John iv 31.
μεταπέμπομαι, I send for, summon.

words.g: a mina, a Greek money unit
words.s: μνᾶ (a Semitic word), a mina, a Greek money unit = 100 δραχμαί, or about £4.
νῆσος, an island.
ὀργίζομαι, I am angry.

words.g: in heaven, belonging to heaven, heavenly, from heaven
words.s: οὐράνιος, in heaven, belonging to heaven, heavenly, from heaven.
περίχωρος, neighbouring; ἡ περίχωρος (sc. γῆ), the neighbouring country, the neighbourhood, surroundings.

words.g: I send in front (forth, forward), set forward
words.s: προπέμπω, (a) I send in front (forth, forward), set forward, start on their way (in Tit. iii 13, of being provided with necessaries for the journey); (b) (prosequor), I convey, I escort on (his, &c.) way, as a mark of affection and respect, Ac. xv 3, xx 38, xxi 5, Rom. xv 24, 3 John 6.

words.g: a Samaritan, an inhabitant of Samaria
words.s: Σαμαρείτης, a Samaritan, an inhabitant of Samaria.

words.g: Saul, the first king of Israel
words.s: Σαούλ, (a) Saul, the first king of Israel, Ac. xiii 21; (b) Saul, the Hebrew name of the Apostle to the Gentiles (see Σαῦλος).
σελήνη, the moon.
σιγάω, I am silent.

words.g: Sidon, a great coast city of Phoenicia
words.s: Σιδών, Sidon, a great coast city of Phoenicia: in Mk. vii 31 perhaps an error for Saidan = Bethsaida.

words.g: Sodom, a city submerged by the Dead Sea
words.s: Σόδομα, Sodom, a city submerged by the Dead Sea.

words.g: Solomon, son of David, King of Israel
words.s: Σολομών (oldest form Σαλωμών, next oldest Σαλομών), Solomon, son of David, King of Israel, and Bathsheba.
τεῖχος, a wall, especially the wall of a city.
τρέφω, I nourish, feed; I bring up, Lk. iv 16: met., James v 5.
ὑστέρημα, (a) that which is lacking, of things or persons; (b) want, poverty, Lk. xxi 4, 2 Cor. viii 14, ix 12, xi 9.
ὕστερος, (a) comparative, latter; (b) superlative, last, latest.

words.g: Felix, third name of (Marcus) Antonius Felix
words.s: Φῆλιξ (Latin), Felix, third name of (Marcus) Antonius Felix, procurator of the Roman province Judaea from an uncertain date (before A.D. 52?) till A.D. 59.
φθείρω, (a) lit. I destroy, I waste; I damage, injure (in being); (b) usually met. I corrupt morally, I deprave, injure (in character); I seduce, 2 Cor. xi 3.
φθόνος, envy, grudge; plur. where related to various advantages.
φθορά, rottenness, perishableness, corruption, decay, decomposition.
φόνος, murder.
αἰνέω, I praise.

ἄμωμος (cf. ἀμώμητος), (a) blameless, the original sense, which may be that in Eph. i 4, v 27, &c.; (b) without blemish, unblemished, a sense almost invariable in the LXX, of sacrificial animals, and possibly the only sense intended in N.T.
ἀναγκαῖος (necessarius), (a) necessary, essential; (b) intimate, Ac. x 24.
ἀρκέω, (a) act. I am sufficient, I suffice; impers. John xiv 8; (b) mid. c. dat. I am content, satisfied (with).
ἄφθαρτος, indestructible, imperishable, incorruptible; hence immortal.
βάθος (a) depth; (b) a depth, a deep (also met.).
Βηθλεέμ, Bethlehem, a town of Judaea.

words.g: I come to the rescue of, come to help, help
words.s: βοηθέω, I come to the rescue of, come to help, help.
βοῦς, an ox.

words.g: infant, babe, bantling, child in arms
words.s: βρέφος, infant, babe, bantling, child in arms: ἀπὸ βρέφους, from babyhood (cf. a pueris).
γογγύζω, I whisper, murmur, grumble (generally of smouldering discontent).
διακόσιοι, two hundred.
διανοίγω, I open up.
διηγέομαι, I relate, narrate.
δρέπανον, a sickle.
ἐκτός, (a) adv. (1) without, outside; (2) except; (3) τὸ ἐκτός, substantivally, the outside; (b) prep. c. gen. outside, apart from.

words.g: I flee out, away, I escape
words.s: ἐκφεύγω, I flee out, away, I escape: with an acc. I escape something.
ἕλκω, I drag, draw, pull.
ἐναντίος, opposite, opposed, contrary: ἐξ ἐναντίας (adv.), opposite; ὁ ἐξ ἐναντίας, the adversary.
ἔνδυμα, a garment, dress.

words.g: working, action productive of ἔργον (concrete work)
words.s: ἐνέργεια, working, action productive of ἔργον (concrete work), activity: in the N.T. confined to superhuman activity.
ἐνθάδε, here, in this place.
ἐξαιρέω, I take out, remove; sometimes (mid.) I choose, sometimes I rescue.
ἐσθής, clothing.

words.g: a chamberlain, keeper of the bed-chamber
words.s: εὐνοῦχος, (a) a chamberlain, keeper of the bed-chamber of an Eastern potentate, eunuch, Ac. viii: hence, as such were castrated, (b) a eunuch, a castrated person.
ζιζάνιον (lolium); in plur. darnel.
ζώνη, a girdle, belt, waistband; because the purse was kept there, also a purse.
ἡλικία, age, term of life; full age, ἡλικίαν ἔχει, he has come to maturity, John ix 21, 23, cf. Eph. iv 13; stature, only in Lk. xix 3.
Ἰσκαριώτης, the graecized form of Ἰσκαριώθ, Iscariot (v. l. in John vi 71, xii 4, xiv 22 ἀπὸ Καρυώτου, from Karyotes).
ἴσος (ἶσος), equal, equivalent, identical: τὰ ἴσα, the equivalent, Lk. vi 34; ἴσα, adverbially, on an equality, Phil. ii 6 (if text be sound).
καλύπτω, I veil, hide, conceal, envelop.
κατέναντι, adv. and prep. c. gen. opposite, in front (of).
κατηχέω, I instruct orally.
κήρυγμα, a proclamation.
Κιλικία, Cilicia, a Roman province between the Taurus range of mountains and the coast in the SE. corner of Asia Minor, linked up with the province of Syria.
κινέω, tr. I move; I stir, excite.

words.g: a little girl, a young girl
words.s: κοράσιον (colloquial), a little girl, a young girl; a girl.

words.g: Cornelius, a centurion of the Roman army
words.s: Κορνήλιος, Cornelius, a centurion of the Roman army, stationed at Caesarea (b).
λιθάζω, I stone.
Μᾶρκος, Marcus, Mark, who also had the Hebrew name John, son of Mary [(c) above], nephew of Barnabas, coadjutor of Barnabas, Saul (Paul), and Peter.
μεγαλύνω, (a) I enlarge, lengthen, Mt. xxiii 5; (b) I increase, magnify.

words.g: I translate (from one language into another)
words.s: μεθερμηνεύω, I translate (from one language into another).

words.g: Melchisedek, king and priest of Salem
words.s: Μελχισεδέκ (Hebr.), Melchisedek, king and priest of Salem (Gen. xiv 18–20).
μέντοι (originally a strengthened μέν), (a) indeed, really, James ii 8; (b) yet, however, nevertheless.

words.g: a group of ten thousand, a ten thousand
words.s: μυριάς, a group of ten thousand, a ten thousand.
νύμφη, νύνφη, (a) a bride; hence, in the symbolism of Rev., the New Jerusalem, the Lamb's Bride; (b) a daughter-in-law, Mt. x 35, Lk. xii 53.
Νῶε (Hebr.), Noah.
ξηρός, dry: ἡ ξηρά (arida), dry land, as opposed to sea, &c.; dried up, withered, parched; in generalizing neuter, Lk. xxiii 31.
ὀκτώ, eight.
ὀξύς, (a) sharp; (b) swift, express, Rom. iii 15.
ὁρίζω, (lit. I bound, fix a limit; hence) I fix, determine, define; I fix upon, appoint, designate.

ὅσιος, (a) holy, pious (implying the right relation to God); τὰ ὅσια, the pieties, the pious deeds, Ac. xiii 34: (b) (Hebrew Chāsīd means not only godly, pious, but also beloved of Yahweh), ὁ ὅσιος, the Holy One (i. e. the Messiah).

ὀσφύς, sing. and plur., the loins, the middle, mentioned in two connexions, first as the quarter from which comes the male seed (Hebraism Ac. ii 30, &c.), and second as the part of the body round which the girdle is placed, when the flowing robes are girt higher with a view to travel or work (cf. Lk. xii 35); hence also met., 1 Pet. i 13 (the negation of mental slackness is referred to).

words.g: native city, native town, native place
words.s: πατρίς (patria), native city, native town, native place.

words.g: the official residence of the procurator
words.s: πραιτώριον (Latin praetorium, meaning originally, the quarters (residence) of the general), (a) the official residence of the procurator, which in Jerusalem was the palace of Herod on the west side of the city; (b) personally, the imperial guard, the praetorian guard, or perhaps, the law officers of the Crown, Phil. i 13.
πρωτότοκος, first-born, earliest born, eldest.
ῥίπτω (iacio), ῥιπτέω (iacto), I throw, cast; I shake, toss: ἐριμμένοι, sunk powerless, Mt. ix 36: in Ac. xxii 23, I toss about, a sign of excitement and uncontrollable rage.

words.g: Rome, the famous city on the Tiber
words.s: Ῥώμη, Rome, the famous city on the Tiber, the capital of the Roman Empire.
σαπρός (puter), crumbling, decayed, decaying, rotten; hence, old and worn out, stale, worthless: met. corrupt, Eph. iv 29.

words.g: Silas, a Jewish prophet and evangelist
words.s: Σίλας (Western documents spell Σιλέας), Silas, a Jewish prophet and evangelist, a Roman citizen and a helper of St. Paul. The name is generally regarded as a pet-form (used in Ac. only) of Σιλουανός, and Silas is in consequence identified with him.

words.g: an army, a body of soldiers
words.s: στράτευμα, an army, a body of soldiers.
συλλέγω, I collect, gather together.

words.g: a body of advisers (assessors) in a court, a council
words.s: συμβούλιον (consilium), (a) a body of advisers (assessors) in a court, a council, Ac. xxv 12; (b) abstr., consultation, counsel, advice; resolution, decree: διδόναι (Aramaism) Mk. iii 6.

words.g: Syria, a great Roman imperial province, united with Cilicia
words.s: Συρία, Syria, a great Roman imperial province, united with Cilicia.
σχίσμα, a cleavage, cleft, split, rent: so met. a division in a crowd, due to difference of opinion, a party division.
ταπεινός, of low estate, poor (and thus despised by the mass of mankind); also poor in spirit, meek, a notion often combined by the Jews with the previous.
τάχος, quickness; ἐν τάχει, adverbially, speedily, quickly.
τεκνίον (a diminutive form, suggesting affection, applied to grown up persons), little child.
χάραγμα, an engraved work, Ac. xvii 29; an inscription engraved, a stamp.

words.g: I am angry, I am incensed
words.s: ἀγανακτέω, I am angry, I am incensed.
ἀγέλη, a herd.

words.g: I am struggling (as in an athletic contest or warfare)
words.s: ἀγωνίζομαι, I am struggling (as in an athletic contest or warfare); sometimes with the object ἀγῶνα expressed.
ἀεί (rare in colloquial Greek), always.

words.g: air, the lower air we breathe
words.s: ἀήρ, air, the lower air we breathe.
ἄκαρπος, fruitless, profitless.
ἅλας (neut.), salt.
ἀπάτη (deceit, deception, or more probably, according to a Hellenistic sense), pleasure in Mk. iv 19 (= Mt. xiii 22, cf. Lk. viii 14), 2 Pet. ii 13.
ἁπλότης (simplicitas, sinceritas), singleness of mind, sincerity.
ἀπολείπω, I leave behind: in Heb. iv 6 ἀπολείπεται is impers. (= restat), it remains.
ἀφθαρσία, indestructibility, incorruptibility; hence immortality.
ἀφορμή (a) a starting, a start; (b) cause, occasion, opportunity.

Βεεζεβούλ, Βεελζεβούλ, Beezebul, Beelzebul, a name of uncertain derivation, the chief of evil spirits among the Jews. The form Beelzebub = god of Flies at Ekron (2 Kings i 2, 3): the better attested form perhaps = the Phoenician Sungod as lord of the heavenly dwelling.
βρέχω, (a) I wet; (b) I rain, having originally the raingod (Ζεύς, Jupiter) as subject (cf. Mt. v 45 and Latin pluo): thence, of a shower from the sky other than rain, Lk. xvii 29.
βρυγμός, gnashing, crunching.
γαμίζω, I give in marriage: this sense probably even in 1 Cor. vii 38, where the older view took it as equal to γαμέω.
δάκτυλος, a finger: the picturesque δακτύλῳ of Lk. xi 20 is represented by πνεύματι in Mt. xii 28.
δηλόω, I show, make clear, reveal.
διαστρέφω, I pervert.
δῶμα, the roof (of a house), the top of the house.

words.g: in the Hebrew, or rather, in the Aramaic dialect
words.s: Ἑβραϊστί, in the Hebrew, or rather, in the Aramaic dialect.
ἐλευθερόω, I free, set free, liberate.

words.g: on the earth, belonging to the earth
words.s: ἐπίγειος, (a) on the earth, belonging to the earth (as opposed to the sky); (b) in a spiritual sense, belonging to the earthly sphere, earthly (as opposed to heavenly) (opp. ἐπουράνιος in both senses).
ἐριθεία, (the seeking of followers and adherents by means of gifts, the seeking of followers, hence) ambition, rivalry.
εὔχομαι, I pray.

words.g: one who is eagerly devoted to a person or a thing, a zealot
words.s: ζηλωτής, one who is eagerly devoted to a person or a thing, a zealot.
ἡμέτερος, our.
θαρσέω, only in the imperative, be of good cheer, a by-form of θαρρέω.
θεῖον, brimstone, sulphur.
θόρυβος, (a) din, hubbub, confused noise, Ac. xxi 34, cf. Mk. v 38; (b) riot, disturbance.
ἰατρός, a physician.

words.g: Jericho, Hiericus, a city a little north of the Dead Sea
words.s: Ἰερειχώ (Ἱερειχώ), Jericho, Hiericus, a city a little north of the Dead Sea.

words.g: I am sitting, I sit, I am seated
words.s: καθέζομαι, I am sitting, I sit, I am seated.

κλίνω, (A) tr. (a) I rest, recline (even in John xix 30); I bend, incline; (b) (inclino) I cause to give ground, I make to yield, Heb. xi 34; (B) intr. of the day, declines, approaches its end, Lk. ix 12, xxiv 29.
κόκκος, a grain.
κρεμάννυμι (pendo), I hang, I suspend; mid. (pendeo) I am hanging, I hang.

words.g: I acquire, win, get, purchase, buy
words.s: κτάομαι, (a) I acquire, win, get, purchase, buy; (b) I possess, 1 Thess. iv 4.
κυριεύω, I rule; c. gen. I rule over, lord it over, master.
λάμπω, I shine.

Λευεί, Λευείς (Hebr.), Levi, (a) an ancestor of Jesus, Lk. iii 24; (b) another ancestor of Jesus, Lk. iii 29; (c) third son of Jacob, the patriarch, and founder of a tribe named after him, Heb. vii 5, 9, Rev. vii 7; (d) son of Alphaeus, and called also Matthew, a revenue officer and one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.
μαστιγόω (uerbero), I flog, scourge, the victim being strapped to a pole or frame, see μάστιξ.

words.g: I am intoxicated with wine, I am drunk
words.s: μεθύω, I am intoxicated with wine, I am drunk.
μοιχαλίς, (a) an adulteress (that is, a married woman who commits adultery), Rom. vii 3, 2 Pet. ii 14; (b) Hebraistically extended to those who worship any other than the true God (Yahweh).
νότος, the south wind; hence the south.
ὄπισθεν, adv. and prep., behind; in Rev. v 1 the reverse (outer) side of the papyrus roll, where the fibres are vertical, is referred to: this was seldom written on, and only from motives of economy.

words.g: a debtor, one who owes, one who is indebted
words.s: ὀφειλέτης, (a) a debtor, one who owes, one who is indebted; (b) one who has sinned against another (an Aramaism, see ὀφείλημα), a sinner, Lk. xiii 4.
πάλαι, long ago, almost weakened to already in Mk. xv 44.
πεντήκοντα, fifty.
πνέω, I blow: τῇ πνεούσῃ (sc. αὔρᾳ, breeze).
πολεμέω, I war, carry on war.

words.g: the active exercise of vicious propensity
words.s: πονηρία (malignitas), the active exercise of vicious propensity, malignity, wickedness: plur. iniquities, Mk. vii 22, Ac. iii 26.
ποταπός, (from what country?, in what country born?, and then) of what sort?, how fashioned? (hence, practically, how great?, 1 John iii 1).
πρέπω, I suit: generally impersonal, or with neuter pronoun as subject, πρέπει, πρέπον ἐστίν, it is becoming, it is fitting.
προστάσσω, (a) I instruct, command; (b) I appoint, Ac. xvii 26.
προσφωνέω, c. acc. I call, I summon: c. dat. I call (out) to; I address, I give a speech to, Ac. xxii 2, cf. absol. Ac. xxi 40.
ῥήγνυμι, ῥήσσω, (a) I break: I rend, tear: in Mk. ix 18, Lk. ix 42, it = either σπαράσσω, of convulsions, or I throw on the ground; (b) intr. I break forth into joy, Gal. iv 27.
ῥομφαία (properly a long Thracian sword), a sword, scimitar: met. in Lk. ii 35 of acute suffering.
σαρκικός (carnalis), generally ethical, belonging to σάρξ (which see), belonging to the natural life of man as a creature of flesh, with the characteristics of σάρξ, fleshly, unspiritual, carnal.
Σιών, Sion, Zion, the mountain on which the Davidic citadel of Jerusalem was built, and thus the centre of the life of the people Israel.

words.g: a cohort, that is about 600 infantry
words.s: σπεῖρα, a cohort, that is about 600 infantry, under the command of a tribune.

words.g: Stephen, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem
words.s: Στέφανος, Stephen, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem, and the first martyr.

στοιχεῖον (elementum), (a) plur. the heavenly bodies, 2 Pet. iii 10, 12; (b) a rudiment, an element, a rudimentary principle, an elementary rule; but in Gal. iv 3 there is much to be said for taking the word in the sense of spirit, demon (possibly also in (a)).

words.g: I serve in the army, I am in the army, I am a soldier
words.s: στρατεύομαι, I serve in the army, I am in the army, I am a soldier (whether on active service or not): hence met. I make war, I take up war, e.g. 1 Pet. ii 11.

Συμεών, Symeon, (a) the patriarch, son of Jacob and founder of a tribe, Rev. vii 7; (b) an ancestor of Jesus, Lk. iii 30; (c) an inhabitant of Jerusalem, who blessed the babe Jesus, Lk. ii 25, 34; (d) an Antiochian Christian, also called Niger, Ac. xiii 1; (e) a form of the Hebrew name of Peter the Apostle, Ac. xv 14, 2 Pet. i 1 (v.l.).

συνβιβάζω, (a) I bring together, join, unite, Eph. iv 16, Col. ii 19; (b) I put together, compare, examine closely, hence I consider, conclude, Ac. xvi 10; I deduce, prove, Ac. ix 22; (c) (a Biblical sense, translation Greek) I teach, instruct, Ac. xix 33 (v.l.), 1 Cor. ii 16, Col. ii 2.
συντρίβω, (a) I break; I bruise; (b) I trample upon, crush, Rom. xvi 20: I maul, Lk. ix 39; (c) met. pass. I am stunned, crushed, [Lk.] iv 18.
τάφος, a tomb; sepulchral monument.
τράχηλος, the neck: τὸν ἑαυτῶν τράχηλον ὑποθεῖναι, to lay down their own necks, i. e. to risk their own lives.
ὑποπόδιον, a footstool (of the conquering king placing his foot on the neck of the conquered).
φθάνω, (a) I anticipate, I precede, 1 Thess. iv 15; (b) I come, I arrive.
φίλημα, a kiss.
φιμόω, I muzzle; hence, probably originally a slang use, I silence, φιμώθητι, be quiet! Mk. i 25, &c.
φλόξ, a flame: πυρός (Hebraistic), a fiery flame: spiritualized, 2 Thess. i 8.
φονεύς, a murderer.
φρέαρ, a well; hence, transferred, Rev. ix 1, 2.
φυσιόω (lit. I inflate), met. I puff up, with anger, conceit, &c.
χαλάω, I slacken.
χεῖλος, a lip: hence the edge, Heb. xi 12.
ψαλμός, a psalm, that is a song of praise, &c., to God, with an accompaniment on the harp.
ᾠδή, a song.
αἰγιαλός, sea-coast, (sandy) beach; shore (of sea or lake), land.
αἰσχύνη, shame; shamefacedness.
ἄκρον (neut. of adj. ἄκρος), edge, tip.

words.g: the Greek way of writing the Latin Aquila
words.s: Ἀκύλας, the Greek way of writing the Latin Aquila, a male proper name; the husband of Priscilla (Prisca), and a Jew, of a family belonging to (Sinope in?) Pontus.

words.g: Alexander, a proper name of Greek origin
words.s: Ἀλέξανδρος, Alexander, a proper name of Greek origin, borne by four, possibly five, persons in the N. T., (a) an early Christian, son of Simon of Cyrene, who carried the Cross, Mk. xv 21; (b) a leading non-Christian Jew in Jerusalem, Ac. iv 6; (c) an Ephesian Jew, Ac. xix 33; (d) a renegade Christian at Rome (1 Tim. i 20), probably to be identified with Alexander the coppersmith (2 Tim. iv 14).
ἀνακλίνω, (a) I make to recline (especially at a dinner-table); (b) mid. and pass. I recline at a table.

ἀνόητος, senseless (in Gal. iii 1 pathos is behind the use of the word, according to Ramsay, Historical Commentary, pp. 308 ff., and it describes a state of culture unworthy of the Romanized Galatians).

words.g: I am away from my parish, I am away from home
words.s: ἀποδημέω (ἀπό from, δῆμος parish), I am away from my parish, I am away from home, I am absent.
ἀπωθέομαι, I push (thrust) away from myself.
ἀσέβεια, impiety, irreverence.

words.g: a foreigner, one who speaks neither Greek nor Latin
words.s: βάρβαρος, a foreigner, one who speaks neither Greek nor Latin: as adj. foreign.
βαρέω, I weight, load, burden, lit. and met.
βάρος, a weight, a burden, lit. or met.: in 1 Thess. ii 7 there may be a play on the derived sense, authority, dignity.
βαρύς, heavy, weighty, burdensome, lit. and met.
βασανισμός, torture.

words.g: a thorn-bush; a batus, a liquid measure among the Jews
words.s: βάτος, a thorn-bush: ἐπὶ τοῦ (Lk. τῆς) βάτου, in the passage about the thorn-bush, Mk. xii 26, Lk. xx 37. βάτος (Hebr.), a batus, a liquid measure among the Jews, containing 72 sextarii, that is, between eight and nine gallons.

words.g: an abominable thing, an accursed thing
words.s: βδέλυγμα, an abominable thing, an accursed thing.
βουλεύομαι, I deliberate, take counsel.
διαφθείρω, I destroy, waste; hence met. I corrupt.
διαφθορά, destruction, dissolution, corruption.
διεγείρω, I wake out of sleep; I arouse, in general.
διερμηνεύω, I translate, interpret, explain.
δίς, twice.
δοκός, a beam.
εἰκῆ, used both with reference to antecedent causes and purposes for the future, without a cause; purposelessly, in vain, for nothing.
ἐμπτύω, I spit upon.
ἕνδεκα, eleven.
ἔνι (ἐνί, Ionic form of ἐν), is in (among): οὐκ ἔνι, there is (or can be) no room for.
ἐνκακέω, ἐκκακέω (from κακός in the sense of cowardly) (very rare outside the Bible), I lose heart.
ἐνκεντρίζω, I graft.
ἐξαπατάω, I deceive.
ἐξαυτῆς (= ἐξ αὐτῆς τῆς ὥρας), immediately.
ἐξηγέομαι, (I interpret) I relate, expound, explain; make declaration (John i 18).
ἐπαινέω, I praise, commend.
ἐραυνάω (a form of ἐρευνάω not known before 1st cent. A.D.), I search: = ἐξεραυνάω, 1 Pet. i 11.
ἔχθρα, enmity, hostility.

words.g: I inflict loss (damage) upon, I fine, I punish
words.s: ζημιόω, I inflict loss (damage) upon, I fine, I punish, sometimes with the acc. of the penalty, even when the verb is passive.
ζυγός, a yoke; hence met. (a Jewish idea) of a heavy burden, comparable to the heavy yokes resting on the bullocks’ necks.

words.g: Herodias (died after A.D. 40), daughter of Aristobulus
words.s: Ἡρῳδιάς, Herodias (died after A.D. 40), daughter of Aristobulus and granddaughter of Herod I, wife, first, of her uncle Herod, second, of his half-brother, her uncle Herod Antipas.

words.g: I am courageous, I am of good cheer
words.s: θαρρέω, I am courageous, I am of good cheer, a by-form of θαρσέω.
θαυμαστός, to be wondered at, wonderful.
θερμαίνομαι, I warm myself.

words.g: Iconium, a Phrygian city of the Roman province Galatia
words.s: Ἰκόνιον, Iconium, a Phrygian city of the Roman province Galatia (mod. Konia).
καθότι (i. e. καθ’ ὅ, τι [neut. of ὅστις], cf. καθό, καθά), (a) in proportion as, according as, Ac. ii 45, iv 35; (b) because, Lk. i 7, xix 9, Ac. ii 24, xvii 31.
κακόω, I treat badly.
κάμηλος, includes both camel and dromedary.
κάρφος, a dry stalk; a chip of wood.
κατάρα, cursing; a curse.
καταφιλέω, I kiss affectionately.

words.g: the Ark, in which Noah sailed
words.s: κιβωτός, (properly a wooden box, hence) the Ark, in which Noah sailed.
κλείς, a key.
κόκκινος, crimson, dyed with Kermes (coccum), the female coccus of the Kermes oak.
κόλπος, (a) sing. and plur. bosom; (sinus) the overhanging fold of the garment used as a pocket, Lk. vi 38; (b) a bay, gulf, Ac. xxvii 39.
Κόρινθος, Corinth, in NE. Peloponnese, the capital of the Roman province Achaia.
κόφινος (cophinus), a stiff wicker basket.
κραυγή, (a) a shout, cry, clamour; (b) outcry, clamouring against another, Eph. iv 31.
Κυρηναῖος, belonging to Cyrene.

words.g: Laodicea, a city in the Lycos valley in the Roman province Asia
words.s: Λαοδίκεια, Laodicea, a city in the Lycos valley in the Roman province Asia, near Colossae and Hierapolis.

λείπω (earlier, I leave behind, abandon), (a) I am wanting; τὰ λείποντα, what is defective, Tit. i 5; (b) mid. e.g. c. gen. I come behind (in a race), I am left behind in, I fall short of (some standard), I am wanting in.

words.g: public service in the widest sense
words.s: λειτουργία, public service in the widest sense, 2 Cor. ix 12, Phil. ii 30: service as of priest or levite ritual, Lk. i 23, Phil. ii 17, Heb. viii 6, ix 21.

words.g: a wolf, or perhaps a jackal
words.s: λύκος, a wolf, or perhaps a jackal: often applied to persons of wolfish proclivities.
Λύστρα, Lystra, a Lycaonian city in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.

words.g: a sorcerer, a magician, a wizard
words.s: μάγος, a sorcerer, a magician, a wizard.
μάστιξ (flagrum), (a) a scourge, lash, of leathern thongs with pieces of metal sewn up in them, Ac. xxii 24, Heb. xi 36; (b) met. severe pains (sufferings) sent by God.
μάταιος, vain, unreal, ineffectual, unproductive: practically godless.
μέριμνα, care, worry, anxiety.
μεσίτης, (a) a mediator, intermediary, 1 Tim. ii 5; (b) a go-between, arbiter, agent of something good, Gal. iii 19, 20, Heb. viii 6, ix 15, xii 24.
μεταμέλομαι (lit. I change one care or interest for another), I change my mind (generally for a better).
μόλις (uix), with difficulty, hardly.
μόσχος, a calf.
Ναζαρηνός, of Nazareth, a Nazarene.
νήφω (lit. I am sober), I am calm (vigilant).
ὄναρ, a dream.
ὄξος (posca), vinegar of wine (Num. vi 3), vinegar, the drink of field-labourers and private soldiers.
ὅπλον; especially plur. ὅπλα (properly arma, also tela), defensive armour (Rom. xiii 12), but also offensive armour, weapons, arms (John xviii 3): sometimes met.
ὀσμή, odour; generally met. in connexion with εὐωδίας (from O.T.), originally of the sweet smelling odour of sacrifice, and then widely used.

words.g: the day of preparation, the day before the sabbath, Friday
words.s: παρασκευή, the day of preparation, the day before the sabbath, Friday.

words.g: I watch carefully, keep my eye on
words.s: παρατηρέω, act. and mid. (a) I watch carefully, keep my eye on (as a cat does a mouse); absol. I watch my opportunity, Lk. xx 20; (b) I observe, keep, Gal. iv 10.
πενθερά, a mother-in-law.
περιζώννυμι, I gird round: mid. I gird myself, generally for active work or travel.
πηλός, mud; clay.

words.g: a bag (to hold food, &c.), a wallet, a travelling bag
words.s: πήρα, a bag (to hold food, &c.), a wallet, a travelling bag, perhaps especially a collecting bag (such as beggar-priests of pagan cults carried).

words.g: I travel by sea, I sail, voyage
words.s: πλέω, I travel by sea, I sail, voyage.
ποιητής, (a) a ‘maker’, a poet, Ac. xvii 28 (the reference is to Epimenides’ Minos); (b) a doer, a carrier out.
πρᾶξις, (a) abstr., conduct; function, Rom. xii 4; (b) concrete, in plur. doings, deeds.
προκόπτω (originally of the pioneer cutting his way through brushwood), I advance, progress, make progress.
προορίζω, I foreordain (lit. I bound [limit] beforehand).
πυρετός, a fever: medical writers use the plural (Ac. xxviii 8), where we should use the singular, because of recurring attacks of fever.

πυρόω, (a) I equip with fire, Eph. vi 16 (of flaming darts), I refine by fire, Rev. i 15, iii 18, I burn with fire, I fire, 2 Pet. iii 12; (b) mid. or pass. met., of strong passion or feeling, I burn with fleshly lust, 1 Cor. vii 9; I blaze with anger, 2 Cor. xi 29.

words.g: ever yet, yet at any time
words.s: πώποτε, ever yet, yet at any time, only used after a negative word.
σβέννυμι, ζβέννυμι, I extinguish, put out: met. 1 Thess. v 19.
σημαίνω (a technical term for the speech of a communicator of an oracle), I indicate by a word; I point out in a letter (by letter), Ac. xxv 27.

words.g: a fine light dress worn over the underclothing
words.s: σινδών (Semitic), a fine light dress worn over the underclothing, or a nightgown, or a sheet hastily seized, Mk. xiv 51: of the grave-clothes of Jesus, probably a piece of unused linen, Mk. xv 46, &c.
σκληρύνω, I make unyielding.

words.g: I look upon, I gaze upon, watch
words.s: σκοπέω, I look upon, I gaze upon, watch.
σπεύδω, I hasten, hurry.
σπήλαιον, a cave (especially as inhabited).
σπόρος, seed.
στάδιος, στάδιον, a stade, a measurement of distance about twelve yards short of a furlong, or about 180–200 metres.
στενάζω, I groan.
στρώννυμι, στρωννύω (sterno), I spread out, strew; in Mk. xiv 15, Lk. xxii 12 of the dining couches with the cushions ready for diners, cf. Ac. ix 34 of making one’s bed.
συναντάω, I meet, encounter: in Ac. xx 22, with inanimate subject.
συνλαλέω, I speak together (with).

words.g: Troas, a harbour city of Mysia
words.s: Τρῳάς, Troas, a harbour city of Mysia.
τρώγω (originally I munch, I eat audibly), I eat. (This word was displacing ἐσθίω in ordinary use.)
ὕπνος, sleep.
φαῦλος, worthless, low, paltry, implying not so much what is evil as the limitations and paltrinesses belonging to a low order of things.
φθαρτός, perishable.

words.g: love of brothers for each other
words.s: φιλαδελφία, love of brothers for each other; hence, love of the brethren, love of fellow-Christians, all being sons of the same Father in a special sense.
χειμών (hiemps), (a) winter; (b) stormy weather, Mt. xvi 3, Ac. xxvii 20.
χειροποίητος, made by hand, hand-made.
ψυχικός (from ψυχή, in the sense ‘the principle of life and the basis of its emotional aspect, animating the present body of flesh, in contrast to the higher life’), emotional or sensuous.
ὡσαννά (Aramaic and Hebrew, originally a cry for help), a cry of happiness, hosanna!

words.g: Aaron, son of Amram and Jochebed, younger brother of Moses
words.s: Ἀαρών (Hebr.), Aaron, son of Amram and Jochebed, younger brother of Moses.

words.g: wild joy, ecstatic delight, exultation, exhilaration
words.s: ἀγαλλίασις, wild joy, ecstatic delight, exultation, exhilaration.
ᾄδω, I sing.
ἀετός, an eagle.
Αἰγύπτιος, Egyptian.
αἰσχύνομαι, I am ashamed.
ἀκριβῶς (diligenter), carefully, exactly, strictly.
Ἀλφαῖος, Alphaeus, apparently two persons, (a) father of Levi (Mk. ii 14); and (b) father of James (Mk. iii 18, &c.). (Some say = Aramaic Chalphai, and identify with Clopas, John xix 25.)
ἄμεμπτος, blameless.
ἄμμος, sand.
ἀνακράζω (colloquial), I shout (aloud).
ἀνάπαυσις, a resting, rest, especially a respite or temporary rest as a preparation for future toil.

words.g: I send up (to a higher tribunal)
words.s: ἀναπέμπω, (a) I send up (to a higher tribunal), Lk. xxiii 7, Ac. xxv 21, &c.; (b) I send back, Philem. 12, &c.

ἀνθύπατος (pro consule, proconsul), a proconsul, a title applied to the governor of a senatorial province under the Empire, such as Cyprus (Ac. xiii 7, 8, 12), Achaia (Ac. xviii 12), and Asia (Ac. xix 38, where the plural is general and does not mean that there were more than one at a time). The word means originally one with the rank and insignia of a consul (i. e. the chief Roman magistrate), but was later applied to those who had not yet held the office of consul as well as to those who had.

ἀντίχριστος, antichrist, either one who puts himself in the place of or the enemy (opponent) of the Messiah, a figure first appearing in the N.T., identified with various historical persons: the plur., of many such, in 1 John ii 18.
ἀόρατος, unseen, invisible.
ἀπέναντι, over against, opposite; in view of, in presence of.

words.g: I wrench away from, I drag away
words.s: ἀποσπάω, lit. I wrench away from, I drag away; but perhaps sometimes in the well-attested weakened sense, I withdraw.

words.g: I deprive one of something, I rob
words.s: ἀποστερέω, I deprive one of something, I rob; absol. in Mk. x 19 (1 Cor. vii 5).
ἄργυρος (rare in papyri), silver as a metal (except Mt. x 9, where silver used as money).

words.g: Aristarchus, a Christian, belonging to Thessalonica
words.s: Ἀρίσταρχος, Aristarchus, a Christian, belonging to Thessalonica in Macedonia.
ἅρπαξ, snatching, robbing, greedy: subst. swindler, extortioner, 1 Cor. v 10.
ἄρρωστος, infirm; sick, ill.

words.g: Artemis, a goddess, worshipped principally at Ephesus
words.s: Ἄρτεμις, Artemis, a goddess, worshipped principally at Ephesus, typifying fertility (she had no relation with the other Artemis, the maiden huntress, to whom corresponded the Latin Diana).
ἀσφαλής (lit. unfailing), safe, reliable, trustworthy.
Βηθσαϊδά, Bethsaida, a city of Galilee.
βραχύς, little: mostly in various adverbial phrases, indicating degree or time.
βύσσινος, of fine-linen, of lawn.
γαζοφυλάκιον, treasury.

Γάϊος, Gāïus, (a) a Corinthian, Rom. xvi 23, 1 Cor. i 14; (b) a Macedonian (?), Ac. xix 29; (c) a citizen of Derbe, Ac. xx 4; (d) an Ephesian (?), 3 John 1. It may be that (b) and (c) or even (b), (c), and (d) are identical.
γάλα, milk.
δαπανάω, I spend.
δεκτός, acceptable.
δή, (a) in a clause expressing demand: so, then, 1 Cor. vi 20; (b) indeed, Lk. ii 15, &c.; (c) truly, Mt. xiii 23.
διαρρήσσω, I tear asunder.
δυσμή, a setting (of the sun); hence the West: for the plur. cf. occasus.
ἑβδομήκοντα, seventy.
εἴσοδος, (abstr.) (act of) entering, entrance, entry: concrete, the entrance itself, Heb. x 19 (cf. 20), 2 Pet. i 11.

words.g: I put off, take off, strip off
words.s: ἐκδύω, I put off, take off, strip off, with acc. of person or garment or both.
ἐκμάσσω, I wipe (off) thoroughly.
ἐκτρέπω (lit. I turn out from): mid. and pass. I turn aside (from the right road), I wander, and with an obj. I remove from myself, 1 Tim. vi 20.
ἐλαύνω, (a) tr. I drive (on), propel: (b) intr. I row, Mk. vi 48, John vi 19.

ἐμβριμάομαι, I groan (with the notion of coercion springing out of displeasure, anger, indignation, antagonism), I express indignant displeasure, with dat. of person with whom it is felt, Mt. ix 30, Mk. i 43, xiv 5: absol. John xi 33, 38.
ἔμφοβος, full of fear, terrified.
ἐναντίον, before, in the presence of; in the eyes of: see also τοὐναντίον.
ἐννέα, nine.
ἐντυγχάνω, (a) I meet, encounter; hence, (b) I call (upon), I make a petition, I make suit, supplication, cf. ἔντευξις.
ἐξαίφνης (ἐξέφνης, colloquially), suddenly.
ἐξαλείφω, I wipe away, obliterate.
ἑξῆς (deinceps), next in order: ἡ ἑξῆς (sc. ἡμέρα), the next day, the following day: τῷ ἑξῆς (Lk. vii 11, v. l.), perhaps = τῷ ἑξῆς χρόνῳ, at the period immediately following.
ἔπειμι, in the participle ἐπιοῦσα, coming on, next: τῇ ἐπιούσῃ (understand ἡμέρᾳ), next day.
ἐπιεικής, forbearing, fair, reasonable.

ἐπίσκοπος (used as an official title in civil life), overseer, supervisor, ruler, especially used with reference to the supervising function exercised by an elder or presbyter of a church or congregation, and therefore (at first) practically synonymous with πρεσβύτερος.
ἐπιτυγχάνω, I attain, obtain.
ἐπιχορηγέω, I supply, provide (perhaps lavishly).
εὖ (bene), adv. well: as interj. well done! bravo!
ἐφάπαξ (ἐφ’ ἅπαξ), once, once for all.
Ἐφέσιος, Ephesian, of Ephesus.
ἔχιδνα, a serpent, snake: in Ac. xxviii 3 probably Coronella leopardinus, a constrictor snake like a viper without poison-fangs, which fixes its small teeth into the skin, but is harmless.
ζόφος, darkness, murkiness.

words.g: pleasure, a pleasure, especially sensuous pleasure
words.s: ἡδονή, pleasure, a pleasure, especially sensuous pleasure.
ἥμισυς (dimidius), half; (τὸ) ἥμισυ, τὰ ἡμίσια (ἡμίσεια, elsewhere unparalleled; usual form ἡμίση), the half.

words.g: I am quiet, I keep quiet, I rest
words.s: ἡσυχάζω, I am quiet, I keep quiet, I rest; I am silent.
Θεσσαλονίκη, Thessalonica (modern Saloniki), an important city of the Roman province Macedonia.
θηλάζω, (a) I give suck; (b) I suck.
θῆλυς, female.
θώραξ, a breastplate, corslet, cuirass.
Ἰάσων, Jason, a Christian of Thessalonica, perhaps the same as the ‘relative’ of St. Paul in Rom. xvi 21.

words.g: an amateur, an unprofessional man, a layman
words.s: ἰδιώτης, (priuatus, unofficial, hence) an amateur, an unprofessional man, a layman.

words.g: Jesse, son of Obed (Iobed), and father of King David
words.s: Ἰεσσαί (Hebr.), Jesse, son of Obed (Iobed), and father of King David.
ἱματισμός, a collective word, raiment, clothing.
καθεξῆς (deinceps), in order, in succession: ἐν τῷ καθεξῆς (sc. χρόνῳ), in the time immediately after, just after, Lk. viii 1; οἱ καθεξῆς, those who followed, Ac. iii 24.
καίπερ, although.
καταδικάζω, I condemn.

words.g: I cause to recline at table
words.s: κατακλίνω, I cause to recline at table; mid. (and pass.) I recline at table.
καταλαλέω, I speak evil of.
καταπατέω, lit. and met. I trample down.
καταράομαι, I curse; κατηραμένοι, having become the subjects of a curse, Mt. xxv 41.
κενόω, (a) I empty, Phil. ii 7; (b) I deprive of content; make unreal.
κῆπος, a garden.
κολαφίζω, I strike with the fist; hence, I maltreat violently.
κονιορτός, dust.
κράσπεδον, the fringe, the edge.
Κρήτη, Crete: see Κυρήνη.
Κύπρος, Cyprus.
κύων, a dog: universally despised in the East, and thus the name is applied contemptuously to persons, Phil. iii 2, Rev. xxii 15 (cf. Mt. xv 26).
λατρεία, service rendered to God, perhaps simply worship.
ληνός, a winepress: hence met. Rev. xiv 19, xix 15.
λούω (literally or merely ceremonially), I wash, bathe (the body): mid. of washing, bathing one’s self.
Μαθθαῖος, Matthaeus, Matthew, a revenue officer, then one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.

words.g: I am raving mad, I speak as a madman
words.s: μαίνομαι (furo), I am raving mad, I speak as a madman.

words.g: a Macedonian, an inhabitant of the Roman province Macedonia
words.s: Μακεδών, a Macedonian, an inhabitant of the Roman province Macedonia.

words.g: I testify, I protest, I asseverate
words.s: μαρτύρομαι, (properly, I call (summon) to witness, and then, absolutely) I testify, I protest, I asseverate; (obtestor) I conjure, solemnly charge, 1 Thess. ii 12, Eph. iv 17.

words.g: a part, division of a country
words.s: μερίς, (a) (a sense amply attested outside) a part, division of a country, Ac. xvi 12; (b) a share, portion.
μιαίνω, met. I stain, pollute, defile.
μοιχάομαι, I commit adultery, not only of a married woman but of a married man (see Mt. xix 9, v.l., Mk. x 11).

words.g: an idle tale, fable, fanciful story
words.s: μῦθος, an idle tale, fable, fanciful story.
μωρία, foolishness.
νηστεία, fasting.

words.g: Nicodemus, a rich Jewish follower of Jesus
words.s: Νικόδημος, Nicodemus, a rich Jewish follower of Jesus, and member of the Sanhedrin.
ὄγδοος, eighth.
ὁδηγέω, I lead, guide.
ὁδηγός, a guide.
ὀθόνιον, a bandage, a wrapping (see ὀθόνη).
οἰκτιρμός, pity, mercy: the frequency of the plural is due to Hebraic influence (the corresponding Hebrew word has the same meaning in the plural).
ὀνειδισμός, a reproaching, a reproach.
ὄνος, an ass.
ὁποῖος (qualis), corresponding to τοιοῦτος (talis), rel. and indirect interrog., of which kind; of what kind, what sort of. This word was dying out in N.T. times.
ὁρμάω, I rush.
οὐρά, a tail.
ὀψάριον, (conversational diminutive of ὄψον, seasoning [especially fish] taken as a relish with bread: hence) a relish; then especially, a fish.
παγίς, a snare (especially for catching birds: perhaps a net thrown over one): hence, met., of moral snares.
παίω, I strike.

words.g: Pamphylia, a Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor
words.s: Παμφυλία, Pamphylia, a Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.

words.g: I stretch forward the head to catch a glimpse
words.s: παρακύπτω, I stretch forward the head to catch a glimpse (especially through a window or door, sometimes inwards, oftener outwards: fig. it implies a rapid, hasty, and cursory glance), I look, peep, peer in (at); I look down.

words.g: a veiled speech in which particularly high thoughts are concealed
words.s: παροιμία (from παρά and οἶμος, beside the common way), a veiled speech in which particularly high thoughts are concealed, a cryptic saying, an allegory; a proverb (2 Pet. ii 22).
πατέω, tr. and intr. I tread; I trample upon.
πένθος, mourning, sorrow.

words.g: I strip off, I strip from, I take away
words.s: περιαιρέω, (a) I strip off, I strip from, I take away; (b) I cast off, cut adrift, Ac. xxvii 40; in Ac. xxviii 13, if the text be right, the word must be rendered in the same way, I cast off, I cast loose.
περιποίησις, acquiring, obtaining, possessing, possession, ownership.
περίσσευμα, what is in excess; overflow, superabundance, superfluity.
πίναξ, a flat dish.
πλάνος, adj., misleading, deceiving: as subst. a deceiver.

words.g: a side of a human being
words.s: πλευρά, a side of a human being.
πλοιάριον, (a little boat, hence) a boat.
ποίμνη, a flock; herd (of goats perhaps, in 1 Cor. ix 7).
ποίμνιον, a little flock: hence, of men.
πρωτοκλισία, the chief (most honourable) reclining-place on the dining couches at a dinner table.
πταίω, of incipient falling, I trip, stumble, lit. or met.

πωρόω (from πῶρος, a kind of marble, then, a bony formation on the joints, and a callus or ossification uniting two portions of a fractured bone: thus πωρόω, I petrify, and I cover with a callus, and I deaden, I dull), I make (render) obtuse (dull, dead); I blind (intellectually or morally).
σείω, I shake.
σίναπι, mustard.
σκληρός (properly hard), (a) strong, James iii 4; (b) met. harsh, rough; almost = dangerous, Ac. xxvi 14.
σκορπίζω, I scatter.
σκορπίος, a scorpion.
στάχυς, an ear (spike) of corn.
στῆθος, the breast.
στοιχέω, I walk (properly, in a straight line, in rank).
συνεσθίω, I eat in company with.
συνπνίγω, met. I choke utterly: in Lk. viii 42 by exaggeration (possibly slang), of pressing very hard upon, hustling, in a crowd (cf. the more correct συνθλίβω).
συνχέω (cf. συνχύννω), I confound.
σύρω, I drag, pull, draw.
σωτήριος, bringing salvation, fraught with salvation.
ταχύς, quick.
τρόμος, trembling.

words.g: Tychicus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia
words.s: Τυχικός (or Τύχικος), Tychicus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia.
ὑβρίζω, I treat insolently (outrageously), I insult.
ὑετός (imber), a shower of rain; rain.
υἱοθεσία, adoption.

Φαραώ, properly a dynastic title (cf. Decebalus in Dacia, Candace in Ethiopia), but, though sometimes preceded by the definite article, probably everywhere understood as a proper name, Pharaoh, a king of Egypt.
φόρος (tributum), tribute, war-tax.
φύραμα, a mixture; hence a lump, a mass, lit. or met.
χαλκός, copper or bronze; hence, a copper coin; copper money, Mk. vi 8 (Mt. x 9), Mk. xii 41.
χρίω, I anoint, to the kingly office, used generally with regard to dedication to Messiahship, &c.
χρονίζω, I delay.

words.g: I play on the harp (or other stringed instrument)
words.s: ψάλλω, I play on the harp (or other stringed instrument).

words.g: Abel, second son of Adam and Eve, brother of Cain
words.s: Ἅβελ (Hebr.), Abel, second son of Adam and Eve, brother of Cain.
ἀγαθωσύνη, (intrinsic) goodness (especially as a personal quality), with stress on the kindly (rather than the righteous) side of goodness.
ἄγαμος, unmarried, not married, of a person not in a state of wedlock, whether he or she has formerly been married or not.
ἄγκυρα, an anchor.
ἄγνοια, ignorance, inadvertence; sometimes with the idea of wilful blindness (Eph. iv 18).

words.g: I am not asleep, I am awake
words.s: ἀγρυπνέω, I am not asleep, I am awake; especially I am watchful, careful.
ἀδιαλείπτως, unceasingly, without remission.

words.g: Athens, the intellectual capital of Greece
words.s: Ἀθῆναι, Athens, the intellectual capital of Greece.
αἰσχρός, base, disgraceful.

words.g: the cause of, the originator of
words.s: αἴτιος (adj.), the cause of, the originator of; responsible for.

words.g: I take captive (in war), I subdue, I ensnare
words.s: αἰχμαλωτίζω, I take captive (in war), I subdue, I ensnare.
ἀκρίς, a locust.

words.g: a hearer of, a listener to
words.s: ἀκροατής, a hearer of, a listener to.
ἁλληλουιά (Hebr.), Hallelujah, Praise the Lord.
ἀμελέω, I neglect.
ἀμίαντος, undefiled, untainted.
ἀμνός (agnus), a lamb (as a type of innocence, and with sacrificial connotation).
ἀναθεματίζω, I curse, I invoke curses.
ἀνακάμπτω, I return.
ἀνάμνησις, a recalling, remembrance, memory.
ἄνθος, bloom, possibly a reference to the bright flowers, such as poppies (among the grass).

words.g: I let go, loosen, release, give up
words.s: ἀνίημι, I let go, loosen, release, give up.
ἀντέχομαι, I hold fast (firmly) to.
ἀντιλογία, contradiction, dispute.
ἀντλέω, I draw (generally water from a deep well in the ground); perhaps, I draw out, John ii 9.
ἄνυδρος, waterless.
ἀνυπότακτος, unsubjected, unruly.
ἀποβαίνω (I go away), (a) I disembark; (b) ἀποβαίνειν εἰς, to result in, to end in.
ἀπογράφομαι, I enrol myself (for the census); hence Heb. xii 23, in another connexion.

ἀποδείκνυμι, (a) I show off, display, exhibit, 1 Cor. iv 9; (b) I make good, demonstrate, Ac. xxv 7; (c) I make out (to be so and so), proclaim (to be), 2 Thess. ii 4; (d) I designate, nominate, appoint, Ac. ii 22.

words.g: I take a tenth part from
words.s: ἀποδεκατόω, (a) as ἀποδεκατεύω; (b) c. acc. pers. I take a tenth part from.

words.g: I have been put away, I am stored
words.s: ἀπόκειμαι, I have been put away, I am stored.
ἀποκεφαλίζω, I behead.
ἀπόκρισις (rare in N.T. times), answering, answer.
ἀποκρύπτω, I hide away, conceal.
ἀποκυλίω, I roll (trans.) away from.
ἀποπλέω, I sail away.
ἀποστολή, commission, duty of ἀπόστολος (apostle), apostleship.
ἀρεστός, pleasing, satisfactory, acceptable.
Ἀριμαθαία, Arimathaea, a place in Palestine, identical with Ramathaim, the birthplace of Samuel. Originally part of Samaria, it with its surrounding district was united to Judaea under the Maccabees.
ἀριστερός, on the left hand: ἡ ἀριστερά (understand χείρ), Mt. vi 3; ἐξ ἀριστερῶν, on the left hand.
ἅρμα, a chariot.
ἀρχηγός (auctor), originator, author, founder.
ἄρωμα, spice.
ἄσπιλος, unstained, undefiled.
ἄστρον, a star.
ἀσφαλίζω, I make safe (secure, fast).
ἄτιμος, unhonoured, without honour, unesteemed.
ἄτοπος (lit. out of place, unusual, unbecoming), improper, unrighteous, perverse, froward: almost = evil, Ac. xxviii 6.
ἀφόβως (literary), fearlessly.
ἀφροσύνη, want of sense, foolishness.
ἄφωνος, soundless, voiceless, speechless, dumb.
βαθύς, deep (lit. and met.); ὄρθρου βαθέως, in the depths of the early morning, while still very early.
βαλλάντιον, a purse.
βαπτισμός, dipping, washing (of a ceremonial character).
βάπτω, (a) I dip; (b) I dye; Rev. xix 13, cf. δίβαφα, twice-dyed garments.

words.g: Bartholomew, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus
words.s: Βαρθολομαῖος (Aram.)(son of Tholmai [=Ptolomaeus]), Bartholomew, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus.
βασίλισσα, a queen.
Βενιαμείν (Hebr.), Benjamin, youngest son of Jacob, founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
βλαστάνω, βλαστάω, intr. I sprout: tr. I cause to sprout, make to grow up, James v 18.
βλάσφημος, abusive, scurrilous.

words.g: Galatia, a large Roman province in central Asia Minor
words.s: Γαλατία, Galatia, a large Roman province in central Asia Minor, comprising the districts of Paphlagonia, Pontus Galaticus, Galatia (in the narrower sense, which some still think is intended in the N.T.), Phrygia Galatica, Lycaonia Galatica, Pisidia and Isaurica. In 2 Tim. iv 10 the reference may be to Gaul, even if we read Γαλατίαν.
γείτων, a neighbour.
γέννημα (from γεννάω), of animal, never of vegetable, products (contrast γένημα), offspring, child.
γλυκύς, sweet.
γνήσιος (lit. born), hence real, true, genuine; τὸ γνήσιον, the true, genuine element.
γογγυσμός, murmuring, grumbling.

words.g: Gomorrha, one of the destroyed cities on the Dead Sea
words.s: Γόμορρα, Gomorrha, one of the destroyed cities on the Dead Sea.

words.g: I fall on my knees before
words.s: γονυπετέω, I fall on my knees before (in supplication), supplicate, entreat.
γυμνάζω, I train by physical exercise: hence, train in widest sense; with gen. of sphere, 2 Pet. ii 14.
δαμάζω, I tame, subdue, involving obedience and restraint.
δανείζω (δανίζω), I lend; mid. δανείζομαι, I borrow.
δειπνέω, I dine.
δεκάτη, a tenth part, a tithe.
δεσμωτήριον, a prison, gaol.
δῆμος (populus), properly the people, especially the citizens of a Greek city in popular assembly (ἐκκλησία), but in N. T. = multitude, rabble.
δημόσιος (publicus), public: δημοσίᾳ, adv. (publice) publicly.

words.g: I offer here and there, distribute
words.s: διαδίδωμι, I offer here and there, distribute.

words.g: I am in trouble, doubt, difficulty
words.s: διαπορέω, I am in trouble, doubt, difficulty.
διάφορος, differing, different; hence excellent.
διηνεκής, continuous: εἰς τὸ διηνεκες, in perpetuum.
διορύσσω, I dig through, break through.
διπλόος, double.
δόμα, a gift.

words.g: a Hebrew, particularly one who speaks Hebrew (Aramaic)
words.s: Ἑβραῖος, a Hebrew, particularly one who speaks Hebrew (Aramaic), cf. Ac. vi 1; Ἑβραῖος ἐξ Ἑβραίων, a Hebrew descended from Hebrews (Phil. iii 5).
ἐγκράτεια, self-mastery, self-restraint, self-control, continence.
ἐθνικός (represents a word which in Biblical Hebrew means nation, but in Rabbinic Hebrew = non-Jew) (gentilis), a Gentile, a non-Jew.
εἰδωλολατρεία, service (worship) of an image (of a god).

words.g: I am peaceful, I keep the peace, I am at peace
words.s: εἰρηνεύω, I am peaceful, I keep the peace, I am at peace.
εἴσειμι, I go in, enter (originally, I shall go in).
εἴωθα, I am accustomed; τὸ εἰωθός, custom, what was customary.
ἐκδίδωμι, I give out, let: middle, I let out for my own advantage, Mk. xii 1.
ἐκθαμβέομαι, I am greatly astonished.
ἐκλείπω, intr. I fail utterly: I am in a state of eclipse (of the sun) Lk. xxiii 45.

words.g: I put to a thorough test
words.s: ἐκπειράζω, I put to a thorough test.
ἐκριζόω, I root out, root up.
ἐκτίθημι, (a) (expono) I expose a child; (b) mid. I set forth, expound, explain.
ἐκτινάσσω, I shake off; mid. I shake off from myself.
ἐλάσσων (less correct ἐλάττων), less, smaller: poorer, inferior, John ii 10: ἔλαττον (adv.), less.
ἐμμένω, I remain (abide) in, Ac. xxviii 30: hence met. Heb. viii 9: with plain dative, I abide by, maintain, Ac. xiv 22, Gal. iii 10.
ἔνδειξις, a showing, proof, demonstration.
ἔνδοξος, glorious.
ἐνενήκοντα, ninety.
ἐνθύμησις, inward thought, meditation; plur. thoughts.

words.g: I buy out, buy away from, ransom
words.s: ἐξαγοράζω, I buy out, buy away from, ransom: mid. I purchase out, buy, redeem.
ἔξειμι (originally, I shall go out), I go out (away), depart.
ἐξουσιάζω, I exercise (wield) power (authority), c. gen., over: pass. 1 Cor. vi 12, I am ruled.

words.g: I follow close after, I accompany, dog
words.s: ἐπακολουθέω, I follow close after, I accompany, dog; I promote, 1 Tim. v 10; hence I endorse [Mk.] xvi 20.
ἐπίβλημα, something put on, a patch.
ἐπιβουλή, a plot.
ἐπίθεσις, laying on.
ἐπισκοπή, (a) visitation (of judgement), Lk. xix 44, 1 Pet. ii 12; (b) oversight, supervision, overseership.
ἐπιφαίνω, I appear (as of a light in the heavens [cf. Ac. xxvii 20] or from the heavens).
ἐπιφωνέω, I call out, shout; c. dat. against, Ac. xxii 24.
ἑπτάκις, seven times: ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας; seven times in the day.
ἐρημία, a desert place, a desert.

words.g: a creeping creature, reptile, especially a serpent
words.s: ἑρπετόν, a creeping creature, reptile, especially a serpent.
εὐλαβής, (lit. handling well, hence) cautious, circumspect; hence God-fearing, pious.
εὐοδόομαι, I have a happy (successful) journey: hence I prosper, with the acc. in 1 Cor. xvi 2 expressing the concrete sign of prosperity.
ζημία, loss.
ζυμόω, I leaven.
ἡσυχία, quietness; silence.
ἦχος, (a) a sound; (b) a rumour, Lk. iv 37.
Θεσσαλονικεύς, a man of Thessalonica.

words.g: I disturb greatly, I terrify, I strike with panic
words.s: θορυβέω, I disturb greatly, I terrify, I strike with panic.
θρηνέω, I lament.

words.g: worship as expressed in ritual acts, religion
words.s: θρησκεία (underlying sense, reverence or worship of the gods), worship as expressed in ritual acts, religion.

words.g: Thyatira, a city of the old district Lydia
words.s: Θυάτειρα, Thyatira, a city of the old district Lydia, in the Roman province Asia.
θυρωρός (ostiarius), door-keeper, porter.
ἴασπις, jasper.
ἱμάς, a thong, strap, (a) for binding a man who is to be flogged, Ac. xxii 25; (b) for fastening a sandal or shoe.
Ἰταλία, Italy.
καθίημι, I let down.
καθό (i. e. καθ’ ὅ, according to which thing), as, according as.
κακολογέω, I speak evil of (not so strong a word as βλασφημέω).
κακοποιέω, I do evil.
κακοῦργος (lit. an evil-worker), a criminal.

words.g: a covering, especially a covering of head and face, a veil
words.s: κάλυμμα, a covering, especially a covering of head and face, a veil.
κάμινος, a furnace.
κάμπτω, I bend.
Κανᾶ, Cana, a town in Galilee.
κανών (lit. a level, ruler), (a) rule, regulation, Gal. vi 16; (b) a measured (defined) area, province.
κατάγνυμι, I break.
κατακαυχάομαι, I boast against.
κατακλυσμός, a flood.

words.g: I exercise lordship over, I overpower
words.s: κατακυριεύω, I exercise lordship over, I overpower.
καταλλαγή, reconciliation.

words.g: I cause to rest, bring to rest
words.s: καταπαύω, (a) tr. I cause to rest, bring to rest; c. gen. I cause to refrain, Ac. xiv 18; (b) intr. I rest, Heb. iv 4, 10.

words.g: I shake (the hand) up and down, I wave
words.s: κατασείω, I shake (the hand) up and down, I wave; intr. I beckon for silence.

words.g: I encamp, take up my quarters, tabernacle, dwell
words.s: κατασκηνόω, I encamp, take up my quarters, tabernacle, dwell.

καταφέρω, (a) I bring down, ψῆφον, the pebble into the urn, i.e. I give my vote; αἰτίωμα, I bring a charge against; (b) I oppress; καταφερόμενος, being gradually oppressed, becoming oppressed, Ac. xx 9, κατενεχθείς, being borne down, overcome, Ac. xx 9.
κατήγορος, a prosecutor, an accuser.
καυματίζω, tr. I burn, I scorch.

words.g: I shear, I cut the hair of
words.s: κείρω, I shear, I cut the hair of; mid: I cut my own hair, I have my hair cut.
κέντρον, a goad.
κῆνσος (Latin census), poll-tax.
κιθάρα, a harp.
κινδυνεύω, I am in danger, sometimes c. infin. of . . .
κλῆμα, a branch.
κοίτη, (a) a bed, Lk. xi 7; (b) a marriage bed, Heb. xiii 4; κοίτην ἔχειν ἐκ, to conceive seed from, Rom. ix 10: κοῖται plur. repeated (immoral) sexual intercourse, Rom. xiii 13.
κολοβόω (lit. I maim, mutilate), I cut short, shorten, abbreviate.
κρανίον, the skull.
κραταιόομαι, I become strong.
κράτιστος (egregius), most excellent, an official epithet, used in addressing a Roman of high rank, and in the second century one of equestrian (as distinguished from senatorial) rank.

words.g: a piece of landed property, a field
words.s: κτῆμα, a piece of landed property, a field, Ac. v 1; plur. possessions, property, possibly landed property, property in land in Mk. x 22, Mt. xix 22, as it is in Ac. ii 45.
κτῆνος, a beast of burden (generally, a horse or mule), either for riding or for carrying loads on its back, or for yoking to a cart or carriage.
κτίσμα, a created thing, a creature, of God.
κυκλόω, I encircle, invest, surround.
κυλλός (debilis), maimed.
κῦμα, a wave.
κυνάριον, a house dog, possibly with a touch of contempt.
κυριότης, (a) abstr., lordship, 2 Pet. ii 10; (b) concr., divine or angelic lordship, domination, dignity, Eph. i 21, Col. i 16, Jude 8, usually with reference to a celestial hierarchy.

words.g: I obtain (receive) by lot, my lot (turn) is
words.s: λαγχάνω, (a) I obtain (receive) by lot, my lot (turn) is; (b) I cast lots, John xix 24.
λάθρα (λάθρᾳ), secretly.
λαλιά, (in classical Greek babble, chattering) speech, talk; manner of speech.
λάχανον, a vegetable.

words.g: properly a division of the Roman army
words.s: λεγιών (Latin, = legio), properly a division of the Roman army, numbering about 6,000 infantry with additional cavalry (cf. Mt. xxvi 53): hence, a very large number.
λέπρα, leprosy.

λόγιον, plur. oracles, divine responses or utterances (it can include the entire O. T. scriptures); in Rom. iii 2 mainly of the promises in the Old Testament; in Heb. v 12 probably of Jesus’ teaching.

words.g: I revile a person to his face, I abuse insultingly
words.s: λοιδορέω, I revile a person to his face, I abuse insultingly.
Λώτ (Λώθ) (Hebr.), Lot, nephew of Abraham.

words.g: I make disciples, I make into disciples
words.s: μαθητεύω, I make disciples, I make into disciples: followed by dat. of instrument, Mt. xiii 52.
μαλακός (mollis), (a) soft, (τὰ) μαλακά, as substantive, soft material; (b) of persons, soft, voluptuous, effeminate (really = cinaedus, pathicus).
μαμωνᾶς (Aramaic, with cognate words in Hebrew and Punic), riches, money, possessions, property.

words.g: manna, the supernatural food eaten by the Israelites
words.s: μάννα (Hebrew), manna, the supernatural food eaten by the Israelites in the desert: of spiritual food, Rev. ii 17.
μάχη, (earlier, a battle, conflict, perhaps in James iv 1; hence) in the sphere of words, &c., strife, contention, quarrel.

words.g: I engage in battle, I fight
words.s: μάχομαι, I engage in battle, I fight: hence I strive, John vi 52.
μέλι, honey.
μεσονύκτιον, midnight, the middle of the period between sunset and sunrise.

words.g: I summon to myself, I send for
words.s: μετακαλέω: mid. I summon to myself, I send for.
μεταμορφόω, I change a form (involving a change of inmost nature; contrast the creatures described in Ovid's Metamorphoses); mid. c. acc. I assume something through a change, 2 Cor. iii 18.
μετοικεσία, transportation, deportation, followed by genitive of reference, Βαβυλῶνος.
μηνύω, (a) I reveal, make known: in a law-court, I lay information, I inform, John xi 57, Ac. xxiii 30; (b) I make known, I point out, Lk. xx 37, 1 Cor. x 28.
μίγνυμι, I mix.
μιμέομαι, I imitate.
μύλος, a mill.

words.g: I make foolish, I turn to foolishness
words.s: μωραίνω (from μωρός) (infatuo): (a) I make foolish, I turn to foolishness; (b) I taint, and thus make useless, Mt. v 13, Lk. xiv 34.

words.g: a young man, a man in his prime
words.s: νεανίας (iuuenis), a young man, a man in his prime (used even of a man of 40).
νεότης, youth, youthfulness.
νῖκος (a later variety of νίκη, dating from about the middle of first century B.C.), victory.

words.g: I suffer acute pain, physical or mental
words.s: ὀδυνάομαι, I suffer acute pain, physical or mental.
οἰκέτης (famulus), a household slave, a slave.
ὄλεθρος, ruin, doom, destruction.
ὅλως (omnino), (a) entirely, altogether, at all; (b) actually, 1 Cor. v 1; absolutely, 1 Cor. vi 7, xv 29.

words.g: I consort with, associate with, commune with
words.s: ὁμιλέω, I consort with, associate with, commune with; particularly, I talk (converse) with, Ac. xx 11.
ὁμοῦ (simul), together.
ὀπτασία, a vision; an appearance.
ὅρασις, a sight, a vision: ὁράσει (specie), in appearance, Rev. iv 3.
ὀρθῶς, rightly.

words.g: the swearing of an oath, the taking of an oath
words.s: ὁρκωμοσία, the swearing of an oath, the taking of an oath.
ὀρχέομαι, I dance.
ὀστέον, a bone.

words.g: not yet either, not yet, not as yet, never before
words.s: οὐδέπω, not yet either, not yet, not as yet, never before.
ὄφελον (in origin an aorist of ὀφείλω, with augment dropped), I would that.
ὀψέ, late: sometimes c. gen. either late on or after.
ὀψώνιον, especially plur. ὀψώνια, (rations: then) soldier's pay, Lk. iii 14, cf. 1 Cor. ix 7: pay, wages, salary, reward in general, Rom. vi 23, 2 Cor. xi 8; charges, 1 Cor. ix 7.
παλαιόω, I make old, I antiquate; I wear out; I treat as past, Heb. viii 13; pass. I fall to the past, Heb. viii 13.

words.g: I make jealous, I provoke to jealousy
words.s: παραζηλόω, I make jealous, I provoke to jealousy.
παρακολουθέω, I accompany, follow closely, both lit. and met., I investigate; I result [Mk.] xvi 17 (v. l).

words.g: I remain beside, I stand by
words.s: παραμένω, I remain beside, I stand by; hence equivalent to, I serve (as a free man), cf. perhaps Phil. i 25, James i 25; I remain in office, Heb. vii 23; I persevere in the law, James i 25.
παραμυθέομαι, I encourage, comfort, console.
παρασκευάζω, I prepare; mid. I prepare, make preparations, 1 Cor. xiv 8.

words.g: I turn aside, I cause (suffer) to pass by
words.s: παραφέρω, I turn aside, I cause (suffer) to pass by, Mk. xiv 36, Lk. xxii 42; I carry away, remove, lit. or met.

words.g: I spend the winter, I winter
words.s: παραχειμάζω (hiberno), I spend the winter, I winter.

words.g: a stranger, sojourner, in a land not his own
words.s: πάροικος (adj. and noun) (= μέτοικος), a stranger, sojourner, in a land not his own, a non-citizen, with limited rights: so, metaphorically, of the Christian resident on the earth, whose real home is in heaven, Eph. ii 19, 1 Pet. ii 11.

words.g: a ruler of a family (or tribe)
words.s: πατριάρχης, a ruler of a family (or tribe), given as an honorary title to David (Ac. ii 29) as ancestor of the race of Jewish kings.
πειθαρχέω, I obey one in authority.
πέμπτος, fifth.
πέρας, (a) a boundary, limit; (b) an end, Heb. vi 16.
περιίστημι: in intr. tenses, I surround; I stand clear of, 2 Tim. ii 16, Tit. iii 9.
περίλυπος, deeply pained (grieved).
περισσεία, excrescence; superabundance, superfluity.
περισσῶς, exceedingly, so perhaps Ac. xxvi 11; but usually more (cf. περισσός), with reference to what precedes.
πετρώδης, rocky.
πῆχυς, the fore-arm; hence, a cubit, about a foot and a half: used as a measurement of time in Mt. vi 27 (Lk. xii 25), to indicate any extension.
πικραίνω, I make bitter (tart, sour): mid. I am embittered, I show quick temper.
πικρία, bitterness, sourness; hence met., an embittered (resentful) spirit, which refuses reconciliation, Eph. iv 31.
πλάτος, breadth.

words.g: a greedy, covetous, rapacious, acquisitive, self-aggrandizing person
words.s: πλεονέκτης, a greedy, covetous, rapacious, acquisitive, self-aggrandizing person; a defrauder, one who tramples on the rights of others.
πληροφορία, full assurance, conviction (confidence).
πλουσίως, richly; lavishly.
πολίτης (ciuis), a citizen: a fellow-citizen, Lk. xix 14, Heb. viii 11.
πόνος, labour, toil; trouble.
πορφύρα, a purple robe, purple; a red-coloured cloak, such as common soldiers wore, Mk. xv 17, 20.
πραΰς, meek, gentle.
προγράφω, (a) I write previously (aforetime), Rom. xv 4, Jude 4; I write above (already), Eph. iii 3: (b) I evidently pourtray or I placard, advertise, Gal. iii 1.

words.g: I see beforehand, I foresee, I see previously
words.s: προοράω, I see beforehand, I foresee, I see previously, Ac. xxi 29: mid. I pay regard to, set before me, Ac. ii 25.

words.g: I lead to, I bring to
words.s: προσάγω, (a) (adduco), I lead to, I bring to; characteristically, I bring a subject into the presence of a king), I present to, I introduce, 1 Pet. iii 18; (b) intr. I approach, Ac. xxvii 27 (v. l.).
προσήλυτος (lit. that has come to), a proselyte, that is a non-Jew, who has been circumcised and has adopted the Jews' religion.
πρόσκαιρος, for an occasion, transitory.
προσωπολημψία (a Hebraistic expression, later than LXX), favouritism, partiality.
πρωτοκαθεδρία, the chief (most honourable) seat (chair, stall).
πύργος, a tower.
ῥαντίζω, (a) I sprinkle and thus purify; (b) mid. I sprinkle (purify) myself, Mk. vii 4.

words.g: a street or lane in a town or city
words.s: ῥύμη, a street or lane in a town or city.
σάκκος (a Semitic word), sackcloth, sacking, a rough mourning dress held together by string, and hanging on the bare body.

words.g: material, made of flesh, consisting of flesh
words.s: σάρκινος (carneus), material, made of flesh, consisting of flesh.
Σάρρα (Hebr.), Sarah, wife of Abraham.
σεμνός (grauis), grave, worthy of respect.
Σιλουανός (Latin, Siluanus) Silvanus: see Σίλας.

Σινά, Sinai, a mountain in Arabia: according to Hebrew allegorical methods of interpretation identified with Hagar, concubine of Abraham, Gal. iv 25 (Arabic hadjar = rock, stone, and thus comes the equation Hagar = Sinai).
σκολιός, crooked: hence met. perverse, of turning off from the truth, crooked in nature.
σκύλλω (originally, I flay, skin), (a) I tire out by hunting; I distress, Mt. ix 36; (b) (a slang usage in origin) I worry, trouble.
σουδάριον (Latin, borrowed by Greek, and thence by Aramaic), a handkerchief.
σπουδαίως, eagerly, zealously; earnestly.
στέγω, (a) I roof over, cover: hence, I conceal, hide, but not in N.T.; (b) I keep out (weather): hence, I keep close, put up with, endure patiently, bear up under.
στεῖρα, a barren (childless) woman.
στενοχωρία (lit. confinement in a narrow space), restriction, restraint; anguish, great trouble.
στερεός, solid; firm, lit. or met.
στρουθίον, a sparrow, the cheapest of all birds for food.

words.g: a pillar for supporting an entablature or other structure
words.s: στύλος, a pillar for supporting an entablature or other structure; hence metaph.
σῦκον, a fig.
συμβουλεύω, act. I advise: mid. συμβουλευόμεθα, we counsel one another.

words.g: I keep a firm grip of
words.s: συναρπάζω, I keep a firm grip of.

words.g: a binding together, a means of holding together, a bond
words.s: σύνδεσμος, a binding together, a means of holding together, a bond, lit. and met.: in Ac. viii 23 the man is in (εἰς = ἐν) the grip of ἀδικία.
συνετός (lit. one who can put things together, from συνίημι), intelligent; in Mt. xi 25, Lk. x. 21 it doubtless refers to Pharisees learned in the law.
συνκλείω, I shut together; I enclose, I shut in on all sides, e.g. Rom. xi 32.

words.g: a joint heir, a fellow heir
words.s: συνκληρονόμος, a joint heir, a fellow heir.

words.g: a fellow sharer (in), a joint partaker (of)
words.s: συνκοινωνός, a fellow sharer (in), a joint partaker (of).

words.g: I take along with me (as helper)
words.s: συνπαραλαμβάνω, I take along with me (as helper).

words.g: I journey with, I go with
words.s: συνπορεύομαι, I journey with, I go with; I go together.
σώφρων (from σῶς, safe, sound, and φρήν, the mind), soberminded, prudent.
ταμεῖον (syncopated from ταμιεῖον, and first appearing in syncopated form in first cent. after Christ), an office, a private room: also a store, Lk. xii 24 (being derived from ταμίας, ‘a steward’).
ταπείνωσις, a being brought low, Ac. viii 33, James i 10: meekness; humility (ταπείνωσις et humilitas uirtutis dicitur et humilitas adflictionis, Ambrose, expos. ps. cxviii 20 10 § 2).
ταῦρος, a bull; an ox.
τετραάρχης, a tetrarch, that is, the ruler of a fourth part of a territory divided into four parts for efficient government, a division sometimes found in the Roman East.
τετρακόσιοι, four hundred.
τεχνίτης, a craftsman, an artisan: c. gen. a designer, Heb. xi 10.
τηλικοῦτος, so large, so great.
ὑμνέω, (a) intr. I sing a hymn; (b) tr. I praise in a hymn.

words.g: an upper room, an upstairs room
words.s: ὑπερῷον, an upper room, an upstairs room.

words.g: I receive under my roof, I welcome to my house
words.s: ὑποδέχομαι, I receive under my roof, I welcome to my house, I entertain hospitably.
ὑποστέλλω, act. tr. I withdraw, Gal. ii 12; mid. tr. I keep back, Ac. xx 20; intr. I withdraw, Heb. x 38; I shrink from, I shun (c. infin. and answering negative), Ac. xx 27.
ὑποταγή, subordination, subjection, submission.
φάτνη, a manger, a feeding-trough.

words.g: Philippi, a great city of the Roman province Macedonia
words.s: Φίλιπποι, Philippi, a great city of the Roman province Macedonia.

words.g: a hedge, a fence, a partition
words.s: φραγμός, a hedge, a fence, a partition; hence, a path bounded by hedges or fences, Lk. xiv 23.
φρόνημα, an object of thought (or endeavour).

words.g: I guard, or rather I garrison
words.s: φρουρέω, I guard, or rather I garrison, lit. and met.
χάλαζα, hail.

words.g: of the colour of grass, green or yellow
words.s: χλωρός (from χλόη), of the colour of grass, green or yellow, as the case may be.
χοϊκός (from χοῦς), made of earth (dust) and with the quality attaching to this origin.
ψηλαφάω, I touch: in Heb. xii 18 perhaps corrupt; πεφεψαλωμένῳ has been suggested, burnt to ashes, calcined, volcanic.
ψυχρός, (a) lit. cold, neut. cold water, Mt. x 42; (b) met. cold, frigid, indifferent, phlegmatic.

words.g: a little bit, morsel, or crumb of food
words.s: ψωμίον, a little bit, morsel, or crumb of food.
ὠδίν, pangs of childbirth, birth-pangs, 1 Thess. v 3; in Ac. ii 24 Death is regarded as in labour and his pains as relieved by the birth of the child; hence, of any sharp sudden pain.
ὡραῖος (lit. in season), beautiful.
ὠφέλιμος, beneficial, useful, serviceable.
ἀββά (ἀββᾶ) (Aramaic) (voc.), Father!

words.g: Abijah, founder of the eighth class of priests
words.s: Ἀβιά (Hebr.), Abijah, founder of the eighth class of priests (1 Chron. xxiv 10).

words.g: I impress (into my service), I send (on an errand)
words.s: ἀγγαρεύω (from a Persian word, meaning to impress for the postal service), I impress (into my service), I send (on an errand).

words.g: the resulting state of the ἅγιος, holy or sanctified state
words.s: ἁγιωσύνη, the resulting state of the ἅγιος, holy or sanctified state.
ἄγριος, wild.

words.g: I feel fear, I lack courage
words.s: ἀδημονέω (originally, I am bewildered, from δήμων, knowing, prudent), I feel fear, I lack courage; I am distressed.
ἀδίκημα, (a) a legal wrong, a crime (with which one is charged), a misdeed; (b) a crime against God, a sin (Rev. xviii 5).
ἀθανασία, immortality, imperishability, freedom from death.
αἱρέομαι, I choose.
αἴτημα, a request.
αἰχμαλωσία, captivity: Hebraistically = captives, Eph. iv 8.
ἀκέραιος, (lit. unmixed) simple, unsophisticated.

words.g: I annul, make of no effect, cancel
words.s: ακυρόω, I annul, make of no effect, cancel.
ἄλαλος, dumb.
ἅλλομαι, I leap, leap up.
ἀλοάω, I thresh (corn).
ἄλογος, without (devoid of) human reason; unreasonable, senseless.

words.g: alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet
words.s: ἄλφα, alpha, the first letter of the Greek alphabet, cf. Α.
ἀλώπηξ, a fox.

words.g: Aminadab, son of Aram and father of Naasson
words.s: Ἀμιναδάβ (Hebr.), Aminadab, son of Aram and father of Naasson, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
ἀμφιέννυμι (a survival of literary language), I clothe.

words.g: Amos, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah
words.s: Ἀμώς (Hebr. = Amon, O.T.), Amos, son of Manasseh and father of Josiah, an ancestor of Jesus.
ἀνάγνωσις, public reading (of the law and prophets in synagogue or church).
ἀναζητέω, I seek out, search for (implying the difficulty of the task).

words.g: I turn upside down, upset, unsettle
words.s: ἀναστατόω (perhaps a political metaphor), I turn upside down, upset, unsettle.
ἀνατρέφω, I rear, bring up (in Lk. iv 16 text is doubtful).
ἀνεπίλημπτος, giving no cause for accusation.
ἀνέρχομαι, I go up (to the capital).

words.g: without, without the co-operation (or knowledge) of
words.s: ἄνευ, without, without the co-operation (or knowledge) of (Mt. x 29).
ἀνήκω, in third person, especially of imperfect (cf. Eng. ought = owed), is due, becoming, suitable, proper.
ἀνθρωποκτόνος (homicida) (borrowed from poetry), a murderer.

words.g: I make upright (straight) again, I rear again, restore
words.s: ἀνορθόω, I make upright (straight) again, I rear again, restore.

words.g: I lay hold of (in order to help), I aid (succour)
words.s: ἀντιλαμβάνομαι, I lay hold of (in order to help), I aid (succour); I take in hand (lit. and met.), I undertake; I partake of, enjoy, 1 Tim. vi 2.
ἀπαίρω, I take away, remove.
ἀπαλλάσσω, I free (a person) from (anything); oftener in the middle voice, I am released from, I am rid of (a person or thing).
ἀπαλλοτριόομαι, lit. I am being alienated from: the perf. pcpl. pass. is practically a noun = aliens.
ἀπάντησις, the act of meeting; εἰς ἀπάντησιν, to meet (a phrase seemingly almost technical for the reception of a newly arrived official).
ἀπατάω (becoming obsolete in most countries), I deceive, cheat.
ἀπειλή, threatening, a threat.

words.g: I cast away, I cast off
words.s: ἀποβάλλω, I cast away, I cast off: I lose, Heb. x 35.
ἀποκαταλλάσσω, I reconcile.
ἀπόκρυφος, hidden away, secret.
ἀποστάσιον, divorce.

words.g: away from the synagogue, expelled the synagogue
words.s: ἀποσυνάγωγος, away from the synagogue, expelled the synagogue, excommunicated.
ἀποφεύγω, I flee from.
ἀποφθέγγομαι, I utter forth, speak out.
ἀποχωρέω, I go away, depart.

words.g: not offending, not causing offence, blameless
words.s: ἀπρόσκοπος, (free from hurt or harm, hence) not offending, not causing offence, blameless.
ἀριθμέω, I number, count.
ἀριστάω, I breakfast.
ἄριστον, breakfast.
ἀρκετός (rare), sufficient.
ἀροτριάω, I plough.
ἁρπαγή, robbery, robbing.
ἀρραβών (ἀραβών, a word of Semitic origin) (arra), an earnest, earnest-money, a large part of the payment, given in advance as a security that the whole will be paid afterwards.
ἀρτύω, I season.

words.g: master of ceremonies at a dinner, master of the feast
words.s: ἀρχιτρίκλινος (arbiter bibendi), master of ceremonies at a dinner, master of the feast.
ἄσβεστος, inextinguishable, unquenchable.

words.g: I miss the mark, miss my aim, make a false aim
words.s: ἀστοχέω, I miss the mark, miss my aim, make a false aim.
ἀσφάλεια, safety; security, reliability, Lk. i 4.
ἀσφαλῶς, securely.
ἀσωτία, wantonness, profligacy.
αὐλέω, I play the flute.
ἄφνω, suddenly.

words.g: not made by hand, not handmade
words.s: ἀχειροποίητος (unknown outside N.T.), not made by hand, not handmade.

words.g: Balaam, son of Beor of Pethor on the Euphrates
words.s: Βαλαάμ (Hebr.) (Balaham), Balaam, son of Beor of Pethor on the Euphrates, a soothsayer in the Old Testament.
βάσανος, torture.
Βερνίκη, Berenice (Lat.), (born A.D. 29) daughter of Agrippa I and Kypros, and sister of M. Iulius Agrippa II, in whose company she appears, Ac. xxv, xxvi.

words.g: Bethphage, a village in the neighbourhood of Jerusalem
words.s: Βηθφαγή, Bethphage, a village in the neighbourhood of Jerusalem, on the Mt. of Olives.
βία, force.
βιβλαρίδιον, a little papyrus roll.
βιωτικός, belonging to ordinary life, with somewhat contemptuous attitude.

words.g: a hole in the earth, ditch
words.s: βόθυνος, a hole in the earth, ditch.
βούλημα, will, desire.
βραδύς, slow.
βραχίων, arm.
βυρσεύς, a tanner.
γαλήνη, a calm.

Γαλλίων, Gallio, Lucius Iunius Gallio, who received this name by adoption into another family, but was born brother of the philosopher Seneca and originally named L. Annaeus Nouatus; proconsul of the Roman province Achaia from spring A.D. 52 to spring 53.

words.g: Gennesaret, a fertile district by the lake of Tiberias
words.s: Γεννησαρέτ, Gennesaret, a fertile district by the lake of Tiberias, which was in consequence sometimes called the Lake of Gennesaret.
Γερασηνός, Gerasene, of Gerasa, a town on the E. of the Lake of Tiberias. Wherever this people is mentioned, the variants Γαδαρηνός and Γεργεσηνός occur.

words.g: Golgotha, a knoll outside the wall of Jerusalem
words.s: Γολγοθά, Golgotha, a knoll outside the wall of Jerusalem.
γόμος, a cargo, freight.
γυμνότης, nakedness, cf. γυμνός, γυμνιτεύω.
δειλός, cowardly, timid.
δεκάπεντε, fifteen.

words.g: Decapolis, meaning a group or district of ten cities
words.s: Δεκάπολις, Decapolis, meaning a group or district of ten cities (of the Greek type) in Palestine, mostly SE. of the Lake of Tiberias. The names and number vary in ancient authorities.
δέκατος, tenth.
δελεάζω, I allure (by a bait).
Δέρβη, Derbe, a town in Lycaonia and in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.
δεσμεύω, I bind.
δεσμοφύλαξ, a prison governor, gaoler.
δῆλος, clear, manifest.

words.g: Demas, a helper of St. Paul in Rome
words.s: Δημᾶς (a pet form, probably of Δημήτριος), Demas, a helper of St. Paul in Rome.
Δημήτριος, Demetrius, a silversmith of Ephesus.
διαβαίνω, I cross.
διαβλέπω, I see thoroughly.
διαγγέλλω, I announce throughout the world, I spread the news of.
διαγίνομαι, I pass (of time).
διάδημα, a chaplet, crown.
διαζώννυμι, I gird myself, by pulling up the tunic and allowing a fold to fall over the belt (ζώνη).
διαίρεσις, division, distribution.
διάκρισις, distinguishing; hence, deciding, passing sentence on (Rom. xiv 1).
διαρπάζω, I plunder, rob thoroughly.
διασπείρω, I scatter (like seed).

words.g: scattering abroad of seed by the sower
words.s: διασπορά, lit. scattering abroad of seed by the sower: hence dispersion, used especially of the Jews who had migrated and were scattered over the ancient world. In James i 1 and 1 Pet. i 1 the reference may be to the New Israel, the Christians.
διαστολή, distinction, separation.

words.g: I spread about (by word of mouth)
words.s: διαφημίζω, I spread about (by word of mouth).
διδακτός, taught.
Δίδυμος, the Twin.
διίστημι: διαστήσαντες (Ac. xxvii 28) tr. with τὸ πλοῖον understood, having moved (the ship) some distance; διαστῆναι, intr. to be distant from, to be separated from; to pass away.

δίκη, (a) (originally custom, usage: hence) right, justice, Ac. xxviii 4, where rather Justice (the goddess); (b) process of law, judicial hearing; (c) execution of sentence, punishment, penalty, 2 Thess. i 9, Jude 7.
