δίστομος (lit. twain-mouthed; hence of a sword, as a drinker of blood), two-edged.
δούλη, a female slave.

words.g: a drachma, a Greek silver coin
words.s: δραχμή, a drachma, a Greek silver coin, corresponding nearly to the modern franc.
δρόμος, a run, a course (in running).
δυνάστης (a man who rules by force, lit.), a ruler, potentate: Ac. viii 27 in appos., seems = courtier, member of the court.

words.g: I am powerful, I have power, I am able
words.s: δυνατέω, I am powerful, I have power, I am able.
δυσκόλως, with difficulty.
δωρέομαι, I give, grant, donate.
Ἑβραΐς, Hebrew, or rather Aramaic.
ἑδραῖος (stabilis) (lit. seated), firm, stedfast.
εἰλικρίνεια, purity.
ἑκατονταπλασίων, a hundredfold.

words.g: I am away from the δῆμος, from my parish, from home
words.s: ἐκδημέω, I am away from the δῆμος, from my parish, from home.
ἐκκλάω, I break off.

words.g: I fall away from, I turn away (from)
words.s: ἐκκλίνω (I bend away from, literally), I fall away from, I turn away (from).

words.g: I sail out (of harbour), I sail away
words.s: ἐκπλέω, I sail out (of harbour), I sail away.

words.g: I breathe my last, I expire
words.s: ἐκπνέω (lit. I breathe out), I breathe my last, I expire.

words.g: I breathe my last, I die
words.s: ἐκψύχω, I breathe my last, I die.
ἐλαττόω, I make less (inferior).

words.g: Eliakim, son of Abiud and father of Azor
words.s: Ἐλιακείμ (Hebr.), Eliakim, son of Abiud and father of Azor (Mt. i 13), son of Melea and father of Jonam (Lk. iii 30).
ἕλκος (ulcus), a (festering) sore.

words.g: a Hellenist, Grecian Jew, a Greek-speaking Jew
words.s: Ἑλληνιστής, a Hellenist, Grecian Jew, a Greek-speaking Jew, that is one who can speak Greek only and not Hebrew (or Aramaic).
ἑνδέκατος, eleventh.

words.g: I am in my δῆμος (parish), I am at home
words.s: ἐνδημέω, I am in my δῆμος (parish), I am at home.
ἐνεργής, effective, productive of due result.

words.g: I have a grudge against, I am angry (with)
words.s: ἐνέχω, (a) I have a grudge against, I am angry (with): in Mk. vi 19 the Sahidic translates ‘I am angry with’, the Vulgate ‘insidior’; in Lk. xi 53 δεινῶς ἐνέχειν is translated by the Sahidic ‘to provoke him’, by the Vulgate ‘grauiter insistere’; (b) pass. or mid. I am entangled, entangle myself (in 2 Thess. i 4 text doubtful).
ἔνταλμα, an injunction, ordinance.
ἔντρομος, trembling.

words.g: I wrap up, roll round, envelop
words.s: ἐντυλίσσω, I wrap up, roll round, envelop.

words.g: Enoch, son of Jaret and father of Mathusala
words.s: Ἐνώχ, Ἐνώκ (Hebr.), Enoch, son of Jaret and father of Mathusala: Jude 14 refers to the apocryphal Book of Enoch.
ἐξακολουθέω, I follow closely, adhere to.

words.g: I raise up, cause to grow
words.s: ἐξανίστημι, (a) in tr. tenses, I raise up, cause to grow; (b) in intr. tenses, I rise up.
ἐξετάζω (indicates precise and careful inquiry), I examine, question, inquire at.

words.g: going out, departure from a place
words.s: ἔξοδος, (a) going out, departure from a place; (b) (excessus) death, Lk. ix 31, 2 Pet. i 15.
ἐξώτερος, outmost.
ἐπάγω, I bring upon.
ἐπάν, whensoever.
ἐπανάγω, (a) nautical, I put out (from the shore), (lit. I take up a ship on to the high seas); (b) I go up, possibly I go up again, return.
ἐπαρκέω, I do service, render help.
Ἐπαφρᾶς (the pet form of Ἐπαφρόδιτος), Epaphras, Epaphroditus, a Colossian Christian, in captivity with Paul in Rome.

words.g: I put a burden on, burden
words.s: ἐπιβαρέω, I put a burden on, burden.
ἐπιβιβάζω, I place upon (a horse, mule).
ἐπιβλέπω, I look with favour on.
ἐπιμελέομαι, I care for, attend to.

words.g: I prop up, uphold, support, confirm
words.s: ἐπιστηρίζω, I prop up, uphold, support, confirm.
ἐπίτροπος, (a) (procurator) a steward; (b) (tutor) a guardian (appointed for an ‘infant’ [under 14 perhaps] by the father or by a magistrate), Gal. iv 2.

words.g: I take in hand, I attempt
words.s: ἐπιχειρέω, I take in hand, I attempt.

words.g: Erastus, steward of Corinth, a Christian
words.s: Ἔραστος, Erastus, steward of Corinth, a Christian.

words.g: making into a desert, wasting, desolating, desolation
words.s: ἐρήμωσις, making into a desert, wasting, desolating, desolation.
ἑρμηνεύω, (a) I translate; (b) I interpret the meaning of, Lk. xxiv 27 (v.l.).
ἑσπέρα, evening.

words.g: Hesrom, Hesron, son of Phares, father of Aram
words.s: Ἑσρώμ, Ἑσρών (Hebr.), Hesrom, Hesron, son of Phares, father of Aram (Arnei).
ἑταῖρος, companion, comrade.
ἑτοίμως, readily: ἑτοίμως ἔχειν, to be ready.
εὐαγγελιστής, a missionary (an occurrence on a pagan inscription = priest of Εὐάγγελος, that is, of Ἑρμῆς, is found).

words.g: I give pleasure to, I please
words.s: εὐαρεστέω, I give pleasure to, I please (perhaps with the added idea of rendering good service to, cf. ἀρέσκω).

words.g: of noble birth, of high birth
words.s: εὐγενής (generosus), (a) of noble birth, of high birth; (b) noble in nature, Ac. xvii 11.
εὔθετος, fitted, suitable: absol. Heb. vi 7.

words.g: I keep up spirit, am of good courage
words.s: εὐθυμέω, I keep up spirit, am of good courage.

words.g: I have a good (favourable) opportunity, I have leisure
words.s: εὐκαιρέω, I have a good (favourable) opportunity, I have leisure.
εὐσεβής, pious, God-fearing.
εὐσχημόνως, becomingly, decorously.

words.g: a prayer comprising a vow, as was usual
words.s: εὐχή (uotum), a prayer comprising a vow, as was usual; a prayer; a vow.
εὔχρηστος, useful, serviceable.
εὐωδία, a sweet smell.
ἐχθές, yesterday.

words.g: Zebulon, one of the sons of Jacob
words.s: Ζαβουλών (Hebr.), Zebulon, one of the sons of Jacob, and founder of one of the twelve tribes.
Ζακχαῖος, Zacchaeus, a Jewish tax-gatherer.
ζεστός, boiling hot.

words.g: Zerubbabel (flourished 6th cent. B.C.), son of Salathiel
words.s: Ζοροβάβελ (Hebr.), Zerubbabel (flourished 6th cent. B.C.), son of Salathiel, according to one of three traditions, all of which agree on Davidic descent, and father of Abiud and Resa.

words.g: I gird, I put on the girdle
words.s: ζώννυμι, I gird, I put on the girdle, especially as preparatory to active work; in John xxi 18 there is a double entendre, the second occurrence referring to binding by another.
ζωογονέω, I preserve alive (lit. bring to birth).
ἡδέως, gladly, pleasantly.

words.g: of which size, of what size
words.s: ἡλίκος (quantus), rel. and interrog. of which size, of what size, e.g. in James iii 5 ἡλίκον means how small, ἡλίκην, how much, just as quantus sometimes = quantulus. Context determines the sense in each case.

words.g: the Herodians, the partisans of Herod
words.s: Ἡρῳδιανοί, the Herodians, the partisans of Herod (Antipas).

words.g: Esau, elder son of Isaac the patriarch
words.s: Ἠσαῦ (Hebr.), Esau, elder son of Isaac the patriarch, brother of Jacob.

words.g: I am defeated, I am worsted, I am made inferior
words.s: ἡττάομαι, I am defeated, I am worsted, I am made inferior.
θαμβέω, pass. I am amazed (almost terrified).
θάμβος, astonishment, amazement (allied to terror or awe).

words.g: a theatre, a semi-circular stone building
words.s: θέατρον, (a) a theatre, a semi-circular stone building, generally open to the sky; (b) a spectacle, 1 Cor. iv 9.
θεῖος, divine; τὸ θεῖον, the divine, the divine nature, Ac. xvii 29.

θεραπεία, care, attention (Lk. xii 42), especially medical attention (treatment) (Lk. ix 11); hence almost healing (Rev. xxii 2). In Lk. xii 42 may, however, be taken as abstr. for concr. (cf. seruitia), the slaves.
θέρος, summer.
θιγγάνω, I touch.
θροέω, I disturb, agitate.
ἴαμα, a healing, a curing.
ἴασις, healing.
Ἱερεμίας (Hebr.), Jeremiah, Old Testament prophet (wrote about 603-586 B.C.).

words.g: the abstract notion of the priestly office
words.s: ἱερωσύνη (earlier ἱερεωσύνη, from ἱερεύς), the abstract notion of the priestly office.
ἰός (cognate with Latin uirus), poison; hence rust, James v 3.

Ἰοῦστος, Justus, (a) a surname of Joseph Barsabbas, one of the two nominated to fill Judas’ place as apostle, Ac. i 23; (b) Titius Justus, a Corinthian Christian, Ac. xviii 7; (c) surname of Jesus, a Christian with St. Paul in Rome.

words.g: Iscariot, the surname of Judas the Betrayer
words.s: Ἰσκαριώθ, Iscariot, the surname of Judas the Betrayer, which would seem to indicate the place from which he came (v. l. Σκαριώθ).
ἰσότης, equality; equality of treatment, fairness.
ἴχνος (uestigium), a track, footstep.

words.g: Joses, son of Mary, sister of Mary, the mother of Jesus
words.s: Ἰωσῆς (Hebr.), Joses, son of Mary, sister of Mary, the mother of Jesus; see Ἰωσήφ (d).
καθαίρεσις (destructio), taking down, razing, destroying.
καθέδρα, a seat, chair.

words.g: Cain, son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel
words.s: Καΐν (Hebr.), Cain, son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel.
κακοπαθέω, I am ill-treated.
κακοποιός, an evil-doer: in 1 Pet. iv 15 probably = maleficus, a sorcerer, magician, or poisoner.
καταγελάω, I laugh at, ridicule.
καταγινώσκω, I condemn; κατεγνωσμένος, reprehensible, Gal. ii 11.

words.g: I veil myself, I cover my head
words.s: κατακαλύπτομαι, I veil myself, I cover my head.
κατάκριμα, punishment following condemnation, penal servitude.
κατάλυμα, an inn, lodging.
καταμαρτυρέω, I give evidence against.
καταναρκάω, (properly a medical term, I stupefy; hence) I burden, encumber.
καταξιόω, I deem (count) worthy.
καταπίπτω, I fall down.
κατενώπιον, prep. before the face of.
κατευθύνω, (a) I make straight, 1 Thess. iii 11; (b) met. I put in the right way, I direct.
κατηγορία, a charge, an accusation.

words.g: I have strength against, I prevail against
words.s: κατισχύω, (a) I have strength against, I prevail against, Mt. xvi 18; (b) I prevail, Lk. xxiii 23; (c) I have strength, I am able, c. infin., Lk. xxi 36.

words.g: the East wind of Palestine, the Simoom
words.s: καύσων, the East wind of Palestine, the Simoom, which blows from February to June.
κεντυρίων (Lat., = Gk. ἑκατοντάρχης), a centurion, an officer commanding about a hundred infantry in the Roman army.
κεραμεύς, a potter.
κεράννυμι, I mix.
κέρδος, gain.
κῆρυξ, a herald, proclaimer.

words.g: Claudius, the fourth of the Roman Emperors
words.s: Κλαύδιος, (a) Claudius, the fourth of the Roman Emperors, Tiberius Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus, who ruled A.D. 41–54; (b) Claudius Lysias, a tribune at Jerusalem.

words.g: a small geographical division, district, or territory
words.s: κλίμα, a small geographical division, district, or territory, a portion of a χώρα (which see).
κολλυβιστής (from κόλλυβος, a commission paid on exchange), a money-changer, who changed heathen into Jewish money, for payment into the Temple treasury.
κολυμβήθρα (lit. a diving or swimming place), a pool.
κοπάζω, I cease, drop.
κουστωδία (Latin, = custodia), concr., a guard.
κρημνός, a crag, precipice.
κριτήριον, (a) a law-court, James ii 6; (b) a law-case before an arbiter.

words.g: in a circle round, round about
words.s: κυκλόθεν, in a circle round, round about.
Κύπριος, Cypriote, belonging to Cyprus.
κῶμος (comissatio), a revel, a revelling, such as took place at the gathering of the grapes.
λαῖλαψ, a sudden storm, a squall.

words.g: I act in the public service, I render service, I minister
words.s: λειτουργέω, I act in the public service, I render service, I minister, in the widest sense, Rom. xv 27, of some special public religious service, Ac. xiii 2: but also of the service of priests and levites, Heb. x 11.
λεπτόν, a small piece of money, probably the smallest piece of money = ½ quadrans (κοδράντης, which see).

words.g: a levite, properly a man of the tribe of Levi
words.s: λευείτης, a levite, properly a man of the tribe of Levi; hence, a priest’s assistant, an under priest, as the members of that tribe were charged with this duty.
λίθινος, made of stone.
λοιδορία, reviling, abuse.

Λουκᾶς, Lucas, Luke, an abbreviated pet-form either of Λουκανός, as the Old Latin Bible gave in the title of the Third Gospel, or of Λούκιος, as some moderns have thought, Christian physician and writer of the Third Gospel and Acts.
Λύδδα, Lydda, Diospolis, Lod (modern Ludd), a city on the way to Joppa within a day’s journey of Jerusalem.
λυτρόω (originally, I deliver captives from robbers or enemies in war by payment, I manumit or liberate a slave from slavery), I ransom, liberate, deliver.
λύτρωσις (in O. T. ransoming from imprisonment for debt, or from slavery, release from national misfortune, &c.), liberation, deliverance, release (cf. λυτρόω).

words.g: felicitation, regarding as happy or enviable
words.s: μακαρισμός, felicitation, regarding as happy or enviable.
μαλακία (malacia), weakness, illness.
Μανασσῆς (Hebr.), Manasseh, (a) son of Joseph, founder of a tribe of Israel, Rev. vii 6; (b) son of Hezekiah and father of Amon (Amos).
μαστός, a breast, especially a nipple of a woman’s breast.
ματαιότης, vanity, emptiness, unreality, purposelessness, ineffectiveness, instability.
μεγαλειότης, (divine) majesty or magnificence.
μεγαλωσύνη, (divine) majesty; in Heb. i 3, viii 1, a sort of substitute for the divine Name.

words.g: a great one, a lord, a courtier, a satrap
words.s: μεγιστάν (megistan), a great one, a lord, a courtier, a satrap. (The word has an oriental flavour and belongs to late Greek.)
μέθη, deep drinking, drunkenness.

words.g: I become intoxicated with wine, I become drunk
words.s: μεθύσκομαι, I become intoxicated with wine, I become drunk.
μέλας, black: τὸ μέλαν (atramentum), ink, 2 Cor. iii 3, 2 John 12, 3 John 13.
μεσουράνημα, mid-heaven, the middle of heaven.
μετάθεσις, (a) change, transformation, Heb. vii 12, xii 27; (b) removal, Heb. xi 5.
μῆκος, length.

words.g: Miletus, a city on the coast of the Roman province Asia
words.s: Μίλητος, Miletus, a city on the coast of the Roman province Asia.
μισθαποδοσία (lit. repayment of price or payment of price due), reward, Heb. x 35, xi 26: in the sense, due punishment, Heb. ii 2.
μισθωτός, hired, engaged for wages.
μνημόσυνον, reminder, memorial; a remembrance offering, Ac. x 4.
μνηστεύω, I betroth.

words.g: a dry measure, the chief corn unit
words.s: μόδιος (Latin, = modius), a dry measure, the chief corn unit, nearly two English gallons.
μοιχός, an adulterer, that is, a man who is guilty with a married woman.
μολύνω, I soil, stain, pollute, literally and morally.

μορφή, form, implying essential character as well as outline. It suggests unchangeableness, as contrasted with σχῆμα (= figure, fashion). In Phil. ii 6 the reference is to the pre-incarnate Christ with divine attributes.
μόχθος, struggle, hardship, involved in continued labour.
μυρίοι, ten thousand: also used for a very large number.

words.g: Naasson, son of Aminadab and father of Salmon (Sala)
words.s: Ναασσών (Hebr.), Naasson, son of Aminadab and father of Salmon (Sala), and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
ναύτης, a sailor.
νεκρόω, lit. and met. I make (cause) to be dead; I make as dead.

words.g: Naphthali, son of Jacob, founder of a tribe
words.s: Νεφθαλείμ, Naphthali, son of Jacob, founder of a tribe which occupied territory.
νηφάλιος, sober, not intoxicated (with wine).

words.g: a Ninevite, an inhabitant of Nineveh or Ninus
words.s: Νινευείτης, a Ninevite, an inhabitant of Nineveh or Ninus, a city on the Tigris in Assyria.

words.g: a teacher of the Law, one learned in the Law
words.s: νομοδιδάσκαλος, (a) a teacher of the Law, one learned in the Law (i. e. the Old Testament), = γραμματεύς, νομικός; (b) a teacher of laws, probably with reference to heretics of ascetic tendency, 1 Tim. i 7.
νουθεσία, a warning, admonition.
νυμφών, a wedding chamber; οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος (a Semitism), the wedding guests, the Messiah being spoken of as bridegroom, Mk. ii 19 and parallels, cf. νυμφίος.
ξυράομαι, I shave my head.
οἰκεῖος (from οἶκος, household, family), of one's family, intimate, 1 Tim. v 8; hence met.
οἰκτίρμων, pitiful, merciful.
οἶμαι, οἴομαι, I think: c. infin. the underlying idea is that of purpose, Phil. i 17.
ὀκνηρός, timid; slothful: ἐμοὶ οὐκ ὀκνηρόν, a kind of epistolary formula, I do not hesitate.
ὁλοκαύτωμα, a burnt offering.
ὅμως, nevertheless.

words.g: I hanker after, I seek (long) for
words.s: ὀρέγομαι, I hanker after, I seek (long) for, I am eager for, I aspire to.
ὄρνεον (originally, a little bird), a bird.
ὀρύσσω, I dig.

words.g: as often as, as many times as
words.s: ὁσάκις, always with ἐάν and subjunctive, as often as, as many times as.
ὀφειλή, a debt, what is owing (due): the mutual obligation of married life, 1 Cor. vii 3.
ὄφελος, advantage, gain.
ὄψις, (a) the face; (b) the features, the outward appearance, John vii 24.
πάθος, (properly experience, feeling; hence) passion, lustfulness, lust (as a state or condition).
παιδαγωγός (pedagogus), a boy-leader, a slave or freedman who attends and guards a boy to and from (sometimes also in) school, and looks after his moral character especially, a tutor.
πανοπλία, armour.

words.g: from all sides, from all quarters
words.s: πάντοθεν (undique), from all sides, from all quarters; on all sides.

words.g: I fall away, take a false step
words.s: παραβαίνω, (a) I fall away, take a false step, Ac. i 25; (b) I overstep, transgress.
παράδεισος, a quarter of heaven conceived by the later Jews to be in or just above the ‘third heaven’, paradise (lit. an enclosed orchard or garden with fruit trees).
παραθήκη (depositum), a deposit (properly of money or valuables deposited with a friend for safe-keeping, while the owner is abroad).
παρακοή, disobedience.
παρακούω, (a) I hear carelessly or incidentally, or I pretend not to hear, Mk. v 36; (b) I refuse to hear; I disobey.
παρεκτός, (a) adv. used as adj., outside, without, left over; (b) prep., apart from.

παρεπίδημος, a stranger settled in a town or region for a time without making it his permanent residence, a sojourner: so in a spiritual sense of those who are on the earth for a time, whose real home is heaven.
πατριά, a group of persons united by descent from a common father or ancestor, a family, a tribe.
πατρῷος, belonging to ancestors, ancestral.
πέδη, a fetter.

words.g: Pentecost, a Feast of the Jews, Whitsuntide
words.s: πεντηκοστή (originally sc. ἡμέρα; lit. the fiftieth day from 14th Nisan, the date of the Passover Feast), Pentecost, a Feast of the Jews, Whitsuntide.

words.g: Perga, a city on the river Cestrus in the Roman province Pamphylia
words.s: Πέργη, Perga, a city on the river Cestrus in the Roman province Pamphylia.

words.g: I go round, I move about
words.s: περιέρχομαι, intr. and tr., I go round, I move about (περιερχόμενοι, strolling, Ac. xix 13); I make a circuit, tack, Ac. xxviii 13 (v.l.).

words.g: I veil round, I cover over
words.s: περικαλύπτω, I veil round, I cover over; I conceal.

words.g: I fall into, I fall in with, I meet with
words.s: περιπίπτω, I fall into, I fall in with, I meet with, I come upon accidentally, I chance upon, I light upon.

words.g: I make my own, I acquire (get) for myself
words.s: περιποιέομαι, I make my own, I acquire (get) for myself, I gain for myself; in Lk. xvii 33 perhaps, I preserve alive.
περιφέρω, I carry around (about); I swing round, Eph. iv 14.
πλάξ, a tablet.
πλατύνω, I broaden, I make broad: met., of the growth of tenderness and love, 2 Cor. vi 11, 13.
πλατύς, broad.
πλέκω, I plait.
πλόος, a voyage.
πλουτίζω, I enrich.
πλύνω, I wash.
πνίγω, I choke, throttle, strangle; hence I drown, Mk. v 13.

words.g: strangled (i.e. killed without letting out the blood)
words.s: πνικτός, strangled (i.e. killed without letting out the blood).
πολυτελής, expensive, costly: hence precious, valuable, 1 Pet. iii 4.
πολύτιμος, costly, expensive: hence valuable, precious, 1 Pet. i 7.

words.g: Pontius, the second or gentile name of Pilate
words.s: Πόντιος, Pontius, the second or gentile name of Pilate.
πορθέω, I devastate, lay waste: hence, I bring destruction upon, I destroy.
πόρρω (procul), far, at a distance.
ποσάκις, how many times?, how often?
πόσις, drinking: hence, concrete, drink, as perhaps in all N.T. passages (certainly in John vi 55).

πρεσβυτέριον, (a) amongst the Jews, a college of elders, who supervised the worship, &c., of the synagogue; hence, the Sanhedrin at Jerusalem; (b) the Christian analogue, a college of elders of a particular church.
πρεσβύτης, an old man.

Πρῖσκα, Πρίσκιλλα, Prisca, Priscilla, the former being the more correct and formal name, the latter a diminutive and more familiar; a Roman lady, probably of good birth, wife of the Jewish Christian Aquila.
πρόδηλος, perfectly clear (evident).
προδότης, (a) a betrayer; (b) traitorous, treacherous, 2 Tim. iii 4.
πρόθυμος, eager: in Rom. i 15 τὸ κατ᾽ ἐμὲ πρόθυμον may be = ἡ ἐμὴ προθυμία, my good will, but perhaps it is better to read πρόθυμος (sc. εἰμί) with some authorities.
προκοπή, progress, advance.

προλαμβάνω, (a) I take before another (perhaps); I am in a hurry to take, I take eagerly, I seize, 1 Cor. xi 21; (b) προέλαβεν μυρίσαι, has by anticipation anointed (perhaps an Aramaism), Mk. xiv 8; (c) (deprehendo) I catch, capture, overtake (before he can escape).

words.g: I take thought for beforehand, I provide for
words.s: προνοέω, act. and mid., I take thought for beforehand, I provide for.
προσαγωγή, access, entrée, or perhaps a metaphor from the concrete sense landing-stage.

words.g: I run (run up) to a person
words.s: προστρεχω, I run (run up) to a person.

words.g: I set before myself, I purpose openly
words.s: προτίθεμαι, I set before myself, I purpose openly: but perhaps, I offer, I provide.

words.g: I appoint, elect (for an important duty)
words.s: προχειρίζομαι, I appoint, elect (for an important duty).
πρύμνα, the stern of a ship.
πτύω, I spit.
πτωχεία, (strictly beggary, but rather merely) poverty.
πύρωσις, (a) burning; (b) met. trial as it were by fire, fiery test, 1 Pet. iv 12.

πώρωσις (originally petrifaction, hardness: then the result of this, as metaphorically applied to organs of feeling), insensibility, numbness, obtuseness, dulling of the faculty of perception, deadness; intellectual (moral) blindness.

words.g: a slap, a blow on the cheek with the open hand
words.s: ῥάπισμα (colaphus), a slap, a blow on the cheek with the open hand.
ῥύσις, flowing; ῥύσις αἵματος, hemorrhage.
Σαλαθιήλ (Hebr.), Salathiel, son of Jechonias and father (according to one tradition) of Zerubbabel.

words.g: Samuhel, Samuel, an Old Testament prophet
words.s: Σαμουήλ (Hebr.), Samuhel, Samuel, an Old Testament prophet.

words.g: Sardis, an ancient city of Lydia in the province of Asia
words.s: Σάρδεις, Sardis, an ancient city of Lydia in the province of Asia.
σαρόω, I sweep.

Σεβαστός (official Greek equivalent of Augustus), Augustus, the name meaning ‘worthy to be reverenced (worshipped)’, given to Octavian by the Senate in Jan. 27 B.C., and retained by most of his successors, e.g. by Nero, to whom it refers in Ac. xxv 21, 25, where it is of course used by non-Christians: in Ac. xxvii 1 σπεῖρα Σεβαστή is the official equivalent of a cohors Augusta (a cohors I Augusta had its headquarters in Batanaea in NE. Palestine).
σεμνότης (grauitas), gravity, dignified behaviour.
σής, a moth.

words.g: Siloam, Shiloah, a spring (the only spring) within the walls
words.s: Σιλωάμ, Siloam, Shiloah, a spring (the only spring) within the walls, in the SE. corner of Jerusalem. The name is Aramaic and really a substantive (= discharge or gushing forth of water).
σιτευτός (altilis), fed up (with grain), fattened.
σκάπτω, I dig.
σκάφη, a small boat, towed behind.
σκέλος, a leg.
σκήνωμα, a tent, really a humble word for the permanent building aimed at, Ac. vii 46: of the body as the temporary abode of the soul.
σκιρτάω, I leap, bound, jump.
σκληροκαρδία (Hebraistic, from σκληρός and καρδία, as the seat of the will), stiffness, stubbornness, unyieldingness, obduracy.
σκοτεινός, dark.
σκοτόω, I darken, lit. or met.
σπαράσσω, I throw on the ground.
σπόγγος, a sponge.
σποδός, ashes.
σπόριμος, sown: hence τὰ σπόριμα, the crops.
σπουδαῖος, eager, zealous; earnest.
σταφυλή, a grape.
στέγη (originally poetical), a roof; in Mk. ii 4 perhaps of thatch.
στενός, narrow.
στενοχωρέω (στενός and χῶρος, cf. English colloquial, I keep some one in a tight place), I press upon, cramp, restrain.
στερεόω, I make firm, or solid: met., Ac. xvi 5.
Στεφανᾶς (a pet form of Στεφανηφόρος), Stephanas, a Corinthian Christian.
στεφανόω, I wreathe, crown as victor, 2 Tim. ii 5, hence met.
στοά, a portico, colonnade, porch: that ‘of Solomon’ was on the East side of the Temple.
συγγένεια, collective, all the συγγενεῖς, kindred, kin, relations.

words.g: I compare (settle) accounts, make a reckoning
words.s: συναίρω; with λόγον, I compare (settle) accounts, make a reckoning.

words.g: a fellow-captive, a fellow-prisoner, a companion in chains
words.s: συναιχμάλωτος, a fellow-captive, a fellow-prisoner, a companion in chains.
συνακολουθέω, I accompany.
συναναμίγνυμι, mid. I associate intimately with.

words.g: I die along with, I die together (with others)
words.s: συναποθνήσκω, I die along with, I die together (with others).

words.g: I raise along with the Messiah
words.s: συνεγείρω, I raise along with the Messiah (from the dead, or from a dead spiritual state).

words.g: I go with, I accompany; I am with, I am in company with, I company with
words.s: σύνειμι, I go with, I accompany, Lk. viii 4. σύνειμι, I am with, I am in company with, I company with.
συνήθεια, custom, habit: c. gen. habituation to, intercourse with, familiarity with, 1 Cor. viii 7.

words.g: I have partnership in, I share in
words.s: συνκοινωνέω, I have partnership in, I share in (with others).
συνκρίνω, I compare.

words.g: I join in giving evidence (bearing witness) with
words.s: συνμαρτυρέω, I join in giving evidence (bearing witness) with.

συνπληρόω, (a) I fill up, hence pass., by an idiom analogous to English, συνεπληροῦντο, Lk. viii 23, they were filling up (where it was really the ship that was filling up); (b) (Hebraistic) I complete, of the coming to an end of an interval of days before some event (in Ac. ii 1 the day of the event may be partly included).
συντάσσω, I direct, instruct, command.
συντηρέω, I keep safe.
συντίθημι, mid. and pass. I make a compact (agreement) with (together), I covenant with, I agree.
συντρέχω, I run (rush) together, lit. or met.
σφαγή, slaughter, sacrifice (of an animal); πρόβατον σφαγῆς (Hebraism), a sheep destined for sacrifice.
σωφροσύνη, sound sense, sobermindedness.

words.g: Tarsus, the capital of the Roman province Cilicia
words.s: Ταρσός, Tarsus, the capital of the Roman province Cilicia.
τελώνιον, a revenue office; a custom-house.
τετρααρχέω, I rule as tetrarch.
τετράπους (quadrupes), four-footed; a quadruped.
τέχνη, art, handicraft, trade.
τήρησις, (a) a keeping, an observance, 1 Cor. vii 19; (b) a place of custody.
Τιβεριάς, Tiberias, a town in Galilee on the western border of the sea called after it.
τοίνυν, so.
τοὐναντίον (syncopated from τὸ ἐναντίον, the opposite), as adv. on the contrary.
τράγος, a goat.
τρέμω, I tremble.
τρίβος, a path, track.

words.g: Trophimus, a Christian of Ephesus in Asia
words.s: Τρόφιμος, Trophimus, a Christian of Ephesus in Asia.
τρυγάω, I gather (always of grapes, τρύξ).
τυφλόω, I blind, make blind, lit. or met.

words.g: I am puffed up, I am haughty
words.s: τυφόω: pass. I am puffed up, I am haughty.
ὑάλινος, glassy, transparent as glass.
ὕβρις, (a) wanton insult, outrage, 2 Cor. xii 10; (b) injury, loss, due to the sea.
ὑδρία, a waterpot (hence, of any pot).
ὑπάντησις, meeting, act of meeting.
ὑπεραίρω, lit. I raise beyond: pass. met. I am exceedingly uplifted.
ὑπεράνω, far above.
ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ, most exceedingly.
ὑπήκοος, obedient.
ὑπηρετέω, I serve, minister to.
ὑπόμνησις, remembrance, recollection.
ὑπονοέω, I suppose.
ὑποφέρω, I endure, suffer.
φανερῶς, openly, overtly.

words.g: Phares, son of Judah and one of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Φαρές (Hebr.), Phares, son of Judah and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
φάσκω, I say, either I say frequently, or I allege.
φέγγος, a light, ray, beam.

words.g: I utter (a word), I open the mouth in speech
words.s: φθέγγομαι, I utter (a word), I open the mouth in speech.
φιλόξενος, friendly to foreigners; hospitable.

words.g: I am zealous, I strive eagerly
words.s: φιλοτιμέομαι, (earlier, I am ambitious; then, I act with public spirit; now,) I am zealous, I strive eagerly.
φοβερός, fearful, terrible.
Φοινίκη, Phoenice, Phoenicia, a northern coast strip of the Roman province Syria.
φράσσω, I stop, close.

words.g: Phrygia, an ethnic district in Asia Minor
words.s: Φρυγία, Phrygia, an ethnic district in Asia Minor, the north-western part of which was in the Roman province Asia, and the south-eastern part in the Roman province Galatia: in Ac. xvi 6 Φρυγίαν is adj.
φύλαξ, a guard (one person).
φυσικός, natural; φυσικά, 2 Pet. ii 12, creatures of instinct.
φύω, I grow, I grow up.
χρίσμα, anointing, referring to the gift of holy spirit.
Χριστιανός (the formation is Latin, and indicates either partisan of Christ or more exactly soldier of Christ, cf. Fimbriani, Caesariani, Pompeiani), Christian, a follower of Christ. (See χριστός.)
ψευδής, false; untrue in word, &c.
ψῆφος, (a) a pebble, Rev. ii 17: (b) hence, from their use in voting, a vote.
ψῦχος (frigus), cold.
ὠδίνω, I suffer birth-pangs: c. acc. of the children that are being born, met., Gal. iv 19.
ὠτίον (see ὠτάριον), an ear.

words.g: Abiud, son of Zorobabel and father of Eliakim
words.s: Ἀβιούδ (Hebr.), Abiud, son of Zorobabel and father of Eliakim.
Ἅγαβος, Agabus, a Christian prophet (Ac. xi 28, xxi 10).

words.g: Hagar, the servant of Sarah, wife of Abraham
words.s: Ἅγαρ (Hebr.), Hagar, the servant of Sarah, wife of Abraham, and interpreted by Rabbinic lore, countenanced by Paul, as a type of Mt. Sinai, where the Mosaic Law was given (Gal. iv 24–5).
ἀγγελία, a message.
ἁγιότης, holiness (see ἅγιος), as an abstract quality.

words.g: (of cloth) unfulled, unmilled, not yet dressed
words.s: ἄγναφος, (of cloth) unfulled, unmilled, not yet dressed (by the fuller).
ἁγνεία, purity, chastity.
ἁγνότης, purity, chastity.
ἀγνωσία, disgraceful ignorance.
ἀγοραῖος, (a) a lounger in the market-place, perhaps with the idea of agitator, Ac. xvii 5; (b) ἀγοραῖοι (understand ἡμέραι), market days; or (understand σύνοδοι, conuentus) assizes.
ἄγρα, catching, a catch.
ἀγριέλαιος, a wild olive.

words.g: the state of being awake (at night)
words.s: ἀγρυπνία, the state of being awake (at night).
ἀδελφότης, brotherhood (in the collective sense), the members of the Christian Church, Christendom.
ἄδηλος, unseen, inconspicuous, indistinct (also of sound).
ἀδιάλειπτος, unceasing, unremitting.
ἀδυνατέω, of things, to be impossible.

words.g: Azor, son of Eliakim and father of Zadok
words.s: Ἀζώρ (Hebr.), Azor, son of Eliakim and father of Zadok, an ancestor of Jesus.
ἀθέμιτος, illegal, unlawful; thus (nefastus) abominable.
ἄθεσμος, lawless, ignoring the (divine) ordinances.
ἀθέτησις, annulment.
Ἀθηναῖος, Athenian, belonging to Athens.

words.g: I engage, compete, in an (athletic) contest
words.s: ἄθλέω, I engage, compete, in an (athletic) contest.
ἀθῷος (sometimes, unpunished), guiltless, innocent.
ἀΐδιος, lasting for ever.
Αἰθίοψ, Ethiopian, Abyssinian.
Αἰνέας, Aeneas, a citizen of Lydda.
αἶνος, praise.
αἰσχροκερδής, fond of base gain.
αἰφνίδιος, sudden.
ἄκακος, innocent, guileless; simple, Rom. xvi 18.
ἀκάνθινος, made of thorns.
ἀκατακάλυπτος, not veiled, unveiled.
ἀκατάκριτος, uncondemned (probably an attempt to translate the Latin re incognita or causā indictā, ‘(our, one's) case not having been tried’).
ἀκατάστατος (in LXX staggering, reeling), unsettled, unstable (though these are hardly strong enough equivalents), almost anarchic.
ἀκρασία (= ἀκράτεια), incontinence, intemperance (in wide sense).
ἀκριβόω, I examine carefully, inquire strictly.

words.g: in the corner (of a building), corner-(stone)
words.s: ἀκρογωνιαῖος (= Attic γωνιαῖος) (adj.), in the corner (of a building), corner-(stone).
ἀλάβαστρος, an alabaster phial or bottle.
ἀλαζονεία, arrogant display, ostentation; plur. = occasions of ostentation.

words.g: boastful, giving one's self airs in a loud and flaunting way
words.s: ἀλαζών (gloriosus), boastful, giving one's self airs in a loud and flaunting way.
ἀλαλάζω (onomatopoeic, cf. Hebrew), I cry aloud, generally of persons (in Mk. v 38 from sorrow): κύμβαλον -άζον, a clanging or clashing cymbal (1 Cor. xiii 1).
Ἀλεξανδρεύς, an Alexandrian, a native (or resident) of Alexandria in Egypt.
Ἀλεξανδρινός (or -ῖνος), belonging to Alexandria in Egypt.
ἄλευρον, meal.
ἀληθεύω, I say (speak) truth, Gal. iv 16; I do truth, I maintain truth (the truth) (see ἀλήθεια for the sense of ‘truth’).
ἀλήθω, I grind.

words.g: I salt, salten, sprinkle with salt
words.s: ἁλίζω, I salt, salten, sprinkle with salt (of sacrifices or of those who offer sacrifice), keep fresh and sound, and so acceptable to God.
ἅλων (= ἅλως), a threshing-floor.
ἄμαχος (originally a military word), not quarrelsome, peaceable.
ἀμέμπτως, blamelessly.
ἀμέριμνος, free from anxiety (though ‘anxiety’ is rather too strong a word).
ἀμετάθετος, unchanged, unchangeable.
ἀμεταμέλητος, not to be repented of, about which no change of mind can take place, not affected by change of mind.
ἄμετρος (inmensus), unmeasurable, immeasurable: εἰς τὰ ἄμετρα, to a limitless degree.
ἀναβαθμός, a step; plur. a flight of steps, the well-known ‘stairs’ leading up from the temple to the tower of Antonia at Jerusalem.
ἀνάγαιον, an upper room; another form is ἀνώγεων.

words.g: I beget again, I beget into a new life
words.s: ἀναγεννάω, I beget again, I beget into a new life.
ἀναδείκνυμι, I show forth or clearly; hence, I proclaim (a person's appointment to an office), I appoint.
ἀναδέχομαι, I welcome, receive kindly; in Heb. xi 17 perhaps I undertake, I assume the responsibility of.

words.g: I come to life again, I revive
words.s: ἀναζάω, I come to life again, I revive (in Lk. xv 24 text doubtful).

words.g: I look up at, I gaze up at
words.s: ἀναθεωρέω, I look up at, I gaze up at.
ἀναίτιος, guiltless.
ἀνακαθίζω (in class. Gk. I cause to sit up), I sit up (text in Lk. vii 15 doubtful).

words.g: I renew, I make new again
words.s: ἀνακαινόω (not cited before Paul), I renew, I make new again (cf. ἀνακαινίζω).
ἀνακαίνωσις (not cited earlier), renewing.
ἀνακαλύπτω, I unveil.
ἀνακεφαλαιόομαι (a literary word, from κεφάλαιον, capitulum, chapter, section), I sum up, summarize, recapitulate; in Eph. i 10 gather up in one.
ἀνακύπτω, I raise myself, become erect (Lk. xiii 11); I look up (Lk. xxi 28).
ἀναλίσκω, I destroy, annihilate (in 2 Thess. ii 8 text is doubtful).
ἀναλύω (see ἀνάλυσις), I depart, Phil. i 23; perhaps, I return, Lk. xii 36 (Jerome demands this sense also in Phil. i 23).
ἀνάπηρος (debilis), maimed.
ἀναπολόγητος, without (ground of) defence, indefensible, inexcusable.
ἀνάπτω, I kindle.

words.g: I shake up, stir up, excite
words.s: ἀνασείω, I shake up, stir up, excite.
ἀνασπάω, I drag up, pull up.

words.g: I lay (a case) before, I impart, I communicate
words.s: ἀνατίθεμαι, I lay (a case) before, I impart, I communicate, I relate (with a view to consulting).
ἀνατρέπω, I overturn (lit. or metaph.) (in John ii 15 text is doubtful).
ἀναφαίνω, (a) a nautical term, I sight (a place); (b) mid. I appear (as it were, out of the unseen).

words.g: that cannot be tracked out, inexplorable, unsearchable
words.s: ἀνεξιχνίαστος (perhaps from Job LXX), that cannot be tracked out, inexplorable, unsearchable.

words.g: I examine (a person on trial, a witness) judicially
words.s: ἀνετάζω, I examine (a person on trial, a witness) judicially (frequently by the aid of torture).
ἀνευρίσκω, I find by seeking out.
ἀνθρακιά, a coal-fire.

words.g: a men-pleaser, a renderer of service to human beings
words.s: ἀνθρωπάρεσκος, a men-pleaser, a renderer of service to human beings (as opposed to God).
ἄνιπτος, unwashed.
ἄνοια, senselessness.
ἀνοικοδομέω, I rebuild, build up (what has fallen or been razed to the ground): sometimes merely I build.
ἀνόμως, without law.
ἀνόσιος, regarding nothing as holy.
ἀνοχή, forbearance; suspense or delay (of punishment).
ἀντάλλαγμα, an exchange, purchasing price.

words.g: a gift in return (for another), a return, a recompense
words.s: ἀνταπόδομα, a gift in return (for another), a return, a recompense.
ἀνταποκρίνομαι, I give a hostile answer.
ἀντιμισθία, a reward, recompense (a more emphatic expression than the simple μισθός).

words.g: I pass opposite, on the opposite side of the road
words.s: ἀντιπαρέρχομαι, I pass opposite, on the opposite side of the road.

words.g: typical of, representing by type (or pattern)
words.s: ἀντίτυπος (from τύπος, impress, impression left by a die), typical of, representing by type (or pattern), corresponding to: neut., as noun, an image.
ἀνωφελής, useless, unprofitable (perhaps also with the further idea, harmful, as in Plato).
ἀξίνη, axe.
ἀπαιτέω (requiro), I ask back, or I ask what is my due.
ἁπαλός, tender.
ἀπαντάω, I meet.
ἀπειλέω (apparently going out of popular speech), I threaten.

words.g: I put off (as a garment) from myself, I throw off
words.s: ἀπεκδύομαι (probably coined by Paul), I put off (as a garment) from myself, I throw off.
ἁπλοῦς (simplex), single: of the eye, directed towards one object.
ἀποβολή, a casting away, a loss.

ἀπογραφή, an enrolment, a census-taking, in which particulars not only of the persons but also of their property were generally given on the census-papers. The system began 10–9 B.C., and such an enrolment took place every fourteen years.
ἀπόδεκτος, worthy to be received (welcomed), acceptable, welcome.
ἀποδοχή (properly reception, welcome, of guests), acceptance, appreciation, approbation.

words.g: a putting off, a laying down
words.s: ἀπόθεσις, a putting off, a laying down.
ἀποκαραδοκία (perhaps coined by Paul), eager expectation.

words.g: I bring forth, give birth to (a child)
words.s: ἀποκυέω, I bring forth, give birth to (a child), a medical or physical word, marking the close of pregnancy.

words.g: the faculty or experience of enjoyment
words.s: ἀπόλαυσις, the faculty or experience of enjoyment.
ἀπολούω, I wash off; mid. I wash away (my sins, in baptism).
ἀποπλανάω, I cause to wander astray: 1 Tim. vi 10 (aor. pass.), I have wandered away.
ἀποπνίγω, (a) I choke, drown; (b) I stop the growth of.
ἀποστασία, a revolting, revolt, especially religious apostasy.
ἀποτελέω, I complete, accomplish, Lk. xiii 32; I form fully, James i 15.
ἀποτινάσσω, I shake off.
ἀποτομία (lit. sheerness, of a rock), peremptoriness, inexorableness, harshness, severity.
ἀποτόμως, sharply, severely.
ἀποχωρίζομαι, I separate myself from.

words.g: Arabia, the district south of Palestine
words.s: Ἀραβία, Arabia, the district south of Palestine.

words.g: Aram, son of Esrom and father of Aminadab
words.s: Ἀράμ (Hebr.), Aram, son of Esrom and father of Aminadab.

words.g: the Areopagus, a hill in Athens
words.s: Ἄρειος Πάγος (lit. Hill of Ares [the Athenian war-god, corresponding to Mars]), the Areopagus, a hill in Athens. As on this hill the Council of the Areopagus (ἡ ἐξ Ἀρείου Πάγου βουλή), the supreme court of Athens, had met in early times, the expression ὁ Ἄρειος Πάγος came to be used (as in Ac. xvii 19, 22) for the Council of the Areopagus, wheresoever it met.
ἀρσενοκοίτης, a paederast.

words.g: a ruler of angels, a superior angel, an archangel
words.s: ἀρχάγγελος, a ruler of angels, a superior angel, an archangel.
Ἄρχιππος, Archippus, a Christian of Colossae.
ἀσάλευτος, unshaken, immovable.

words.g: Asaph, Asa, son of Abijah and father of Jehoshaphat
words.s: Ἀσάφ (Hebr.), Asaph, Asa, son of Abijah and father of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah about 900 B.C. for 41 years.

words.g: Asher, one of the sons of Jacob
words.s: Ἀσήρ (Hebr.), Asher, one of the sons of Jacob, and founder of one of the Twelve Tribes.
ἀσσάριον (assarius, dimin. of as), a penny (1/16 of a δηνάριον and the tenth part of a drachma or franc).
Ἆσσος, Assos, a port of Mysia, in the Roman province Asia.
ἀστεῖος (lit. belonging to the city: then witty, clever), elegant, pretty, fair, fine.
ἀστήρικτος (rather literary) (lit. unpropped), unsteady, unstable.
ἄστοργος, unloving, devoid of affection.
ἀστράπτω, I flash, (with, then like, lightning).

words.g: I am unseemly, I behave unbecomingly
words.s: ἀσχημονέω, I am unseemly, I behave unbecomingly (or even dishonourably); perhaps, I consider (something) unseemly.
ἀσχημοσύνη, unseemly behaviour, indecency, or concrete, an indecent (lewd) act.
ἀτάκτως, in a disorderly manner (see ἄτακτος, ἀτακτέω).
ἄτεκνος, childless.
ἄτερ (originally poetical), apart from, without.
ἀτμίς, (a) breath; (b) steam, vapour.
αὐθάδης, self-satisfied; hence arrogant.
αὐθαίρετος, of one's own accord.
αὐλητής, a flute-player.

words.g: I bivouac, I pass the night
words.s: αὐλίζομαι, I bivouac, I pass the night.
αὔξησις, increasing, increase, growth.
αὐστηρός (tristis), grim, severe; strict, exacting.
αὐτάρκεια, self-sufficiency; independence.
αὐτόματος, of its own accord.
ἀφεδρών, a drain, latrine.
ἁφή, a band, fastening (hence, possibly, a ligament).
ἀφιλάργυρος, not loving money, not avaricious.

words.g: I look away from (something else) to
words.s: ἀφοράω (cf. ἀποβλέπω), I look away from (something else) to: ἀφίδω, Phil. ii 23, aspirated from ἀπίδω by analogy with ἀφοράω.
ἀφρίζω, I foam (at the mouth).
ἀχάριστος, ungrateful.

words.g: Acheim, son of Zadok and father of Eliud
words.s: Ἀχείμ (Hebr.), Acheim, son of Zadok and father of Eliud.
ἀχρεῖος, unprofitable, useless, unworthy.
ἄχυρον, chaff.
βαρέως, heavily, with difficulty.
Βαρσαββᾶς (Aram.), Barsabbas, son of Sabbas, a surname of Joseph (Ac. i 23) and Judas (Ac. xv 22).
βδελύσσομαι, I abominate, detest.
βεβαίωσις, confirmation, ratification, establishment.
βεβηλόω, I profane.

words.g: Beroea, a town of the province Macedonia
words.s: Βέροια, Beroea, a town of the province Macedonia.

words.g: I use force, I force my way, I come forward violently
words.s: βιάζομαι, (a) mid. I use force, I force my way, I come forward violently, cf. Mt. xi 12 (where perhaps pass.); (b) pass. I am forcibly treated.
Βιθυνία, Bithynia, a Roman province, NW. of Asia Minor and SW. of the Black Sea.
βλάπτω, I injure.
βοήθεια, (a) abstr., assistance; (b) concr. (a technical term of nautical language), a help.

words.g: I cast the line (for sounding), I sound
words.s: βολίζω, I cast the line (for sounding), I sound.
βορρᾶς, the north wind, hence the north.

words.g: a member of a βουλή (city council)
words.s: βουλευτής, a member of a βουλή (city council), in N. T. of the συνέδριον, Sanhedrin at Jerusalem.
βουνός (tumulus), a hillock, hill.
βραβεῖον, a prize.
βραδύνω, I am slow, I delay: followed by gen., 2 Pet. iii 9.
βροχή, a wetting, rain.
βυθίζω, I cause to sink.
Γαβριήλ (Hebr.), Gabriel, a messenger of God.

words.g: Galatic, belonging to the province Galatia
words.s: Γαλατικός, Galatic, belonging to the province Galatia: τὴν Φρυγίαν καὶ Γαλατικὴν χώραν, Ac. xvi 6, ‘the region which is both Phrygian (racially) and Galatic (by administration)’.

words.g: Gamaliel, a noted Pharisee, teacher of Saul
words.s: Γαμαλιήλ (Hebr.), Gamaliel, a noted Pharisee, teacher of Saul.
Γεθσημανεί, Gethsemani, a small place between the brook Kidron and the Mount of Olives near Jerusalem.
γελάω, I laugh.
γενεαλογία, genealogy.
γενέσια, birthday-anniversary feast.
γεννητός, begotten, used as subst.
γηράσκω, I become old, grow old.
γλωσσόκομον (a vernacular word), bag, purse: some prefer to take as box, chest.

words.g: I hold up as an example
words.s: δειγματίζω, I hold up as an example.
δεινῶς, terribly.

words.g: I tithe, I collect tithe from
words.s: δεκατόω, I tithe, I collect tithe from.
δερμάτινος, made of hide, leathern.
δεσμώτης, a prisoner, captive.
διαβεβαιόομαι, I assert emphatically.
διαγινώσκω, I learn thoroughly, I determine (Ac. xxiv 22).

words.g: I murmur greatly, I continue murmuring
words.s: διαγογγύζω, I murmur greatly, I continue murmuring.

words.g: I spend time, pass time, live
words.s: διάγω (either tr. or intr.), I spend time, pass time, live.
διαιρέω, I divide, distribute.
διαλαλέω, I interchange talk; of conversation passing from mouth to mouth.
διαπονέομαι, I am greatly troubled.
διαπρίω (lit. I saw through), I cut to the quick (with indignation and envy).
διασαφέω, I make clear, explain.
διασπάω, I tear apart, burst.
διαταγή, ordaining, ordinance, disposition.
διατηρέω, I keep safe, hold fast.
διαχειρίζομαι, I lay my hands upon, and so, I slay, kill.

words.g: able to teach, apt to teach
words.s: διδακτικός, able to teach, apt to teach.

words.g: a double-drachma, two drachmae, a Greek silver coin
words.s: δίδραχμον, a double-drachma, two drachmae, a Greek silver coin, roughly equal to the modern two-franc-piece in value, but greater in purchasing power. In the time of Christ 1 drachma roughly = 1 denarius = ¼ shekel: δίδραχμον, the yearly temple-tax thus = ½ shekel.

words.g: a period of two years, two years
words.s: διετία, a period of two years, two years. (According to ancient practice this means any period between one and two years.)
διισχυρίζομαι, I assert emphatically.

words.g: justifying, justification, a process of absolution
words.s: δικαίωσις, justifying, justification, a process of absolution.
δικαστής, a judge.
διοδεύω, I travel through.
διόπερ (δι’ ὅπερ), an emphatic διό.
διστάζω, I doubt.
διχοστασία, division (between persons).
διχοτομέω, I cut in two.
δίψυχος (lit. of two souls, of two selves), double-minded, wavering.

words.g: what is genuine, the approved part, the pure part
words.s: δοκίμιον (neut. of δοκίμιος genuine, as opposed to alloyed, counterfeit), what is genuine, the approved part, the pure part.

words.g: the Greek name of Tabitha, Dorcas
words.s: Δορκάς, the Greek name of Tabitha, Dorcas (lit. gazelle), (δορκάς dicitur a uidendo; δορκατικόν etenim uisus acutioris est, Ambros. expos. ps. cxviii 6. 12 § 1).
δόσις, giving (from God).
δοχή, a reception, party.
δυναμόω, I empower, fill with power.
δύνω, I sink (intr.).
δώρημα, a gift: in James i 17 (of God).
ἐάνπερ, if indeed.
ἔγκλημα, an accusation, charge.

words.g: I exercise self-control, I am continent
words.s: ἐγκρατεύομαι, I exercise self-control, I am continent.

words.g: Hezekiah, son of Achas (Ahaz), father of Manasseh
words.s: Ἑζεκίας (Hebr.), Hezekiah, son of Achas (Ahaz), father of Manasseh, and king of Judah (727–686 [?] B.C.).
εἰλικρινής (sincerus) (originally unmixed), pure, uncontaminated.

words.g: making for peace, productive of peace
words.s: εἰρηνικός, making for peace, productive of peace.
ἔκβασις, (a) a way out, escape, 1 Cor. x 13; (b) result, Heb. xiii 7.

words.g: I give a complete narrative of
words.s: ἐκδιηγέομαι, I give a complete narrative of.
ἔκδικος, avenging, an avenger. (The word occurs frequently in the sense of a special advocate [champion] of a city.)
ἐκεῖσε (illuc), (a) thither, Ac. xxi 3; (b) there, Ac. xxii 5.
ἐκκαθαίρω, I clean (cleanse) out, 1 Cor. v 7; I clean thoroughly, 2 Tim. ii 21.
ἐκκεντέω, I pierce through (or deeply).
ἐκκλείω, I shut out, exclude.
ἐκμυκτηρίζω, I mock greatly.
ἑκουσίως, willingly, with the will.
ἔκπαλαι, from of old, long since.
ἐκπέμπω, I send out.

words.g: I complete, bring to completion, carry out, perform
words.s: ἐκτελέω, I complete, bring to completion, carry out, perform.
ἐκτενῶς, earnestly, strenuously.
ἐκτρέφω, I nourish, nurture.
ἔκφοβος, exceedingly afraid.

words.g: I put forth, cause to sprout
words.s: ἐκφύω, I put forth, cause to sprout.
ἑκών, willing, willingly.
ἐλαφρός (leuis), light.

words.g: Eleazar, son of Eliud, and father of Matthan
words.s: Ἐλεάζαρ (Hebr.), Eleazar, son of Eliud, and father of Matthan.
ἐλεεινός, merciful, pitiful.
ἐλεήμων, pitiful, merciful.

words.g: Eliud, son of Acheim, and father of Eleazar
words.s: Ἐλιούδ (Hebr.), Eliud, son of Acheim, and father of Eleazar.
ἑλίσσω, I roll, roll up.
Ἑλληνίς (fem.), Greek; see Ἕλλην.
Ἑλληνιστί, in the Greek language.

words.g: I put down (set) to some one's account, reckon, impute
words.s: ἐλλογάω (ἐλλογέω), I put down (set) to some one's account, reckon, impute.
ἐλωί (Aramaic), my God (form of word is doubtful).
ἐμβάπτω, act. and mid. I dip in.
ἐμπαίκτης, a mocker.
ἐμπλέκω, I enfold, entangle.

words.g: I travel as a merchant, engage in trade
words.s: ἐμπορεύομαι, I travel as a merchant, engage in trade: c. acc. I traffic in, make gain or business of.
ἐμφανής, manifest, visible.
ἐναγκαλίζομαι, I take (fold) in my arms.
ἔναντι, before, in the presence of.
ἐνάρχομαι, I begin (in).
ἐνδιδύσκω, (somewhat rare) (of clothing, I put on another): mid. I put on (myself).
ἔνδικος, just.

words.g: I glorify, acknowledge the glory belonging to
words.s: ἐνδοξάζω (I make ἔνδοξος), I glorify, acknowledge the glory belonging to (cf. δόξα), recognize as glorious.
ἐνέδρα (insidiae), ambuscade; hence plot, treachery, fraud.

words.g: I lie in wait (ambush) for, seek to entrap
words.s: ἐνεδρεύω, I lie in wait (ambush) for, seek to entrap (hence I defraud, deceive).
ἐνέργημα, a working.
ἐνευλογέω, I bless (of God) (ἐν is considered to have instrumental force).
ἔνθεν, hence, from this place.
ἐνθυμέομαι, I meditate upon, reflect upon.

words.g: I strengthen within, I fill with strength
words.s: ἐνισχύω, I strengthen within, I fill with strength.
ἐνκαινίζω, (I restore or carry out anew, then) I dedicate.
ἔννοια (intelligence, thought), intention, purpose.
ἔννομος, (a) legal, statutory, duly constituted, Ac. xix 39; (b) under the law, obedient to the law, 1 Cor. ix 21.
ἑνότης, oneness, unity.
ἐνοχλέω, I disturb, torment (Heb. xii 15 is from the LXX, where ἐνοχλῇ appears to be a corruption for ἐν χολῇ, in gall).
ἐνταφιάζω, I embalm, prepare for burial.

words.g: embalming, preparation of corpse for burial
words.s: ἐνταφιασμός, embalming, preparation of corpse for burial.
ἔντευξις (lit. approaching the king, hence a technical term), a petition.
ἐντός, within, inside (so also Lk. xvii 21); τὸ ἐντός, the inside.
ἐντροπή (from ἐντρέπω), shame.

words.g: I dream (see visions) in my sleep
words.s: ἐνυπνιάζομαι, I dream (see visions) in my sleep.
ἐξαγγέλλω, I announce publicly, proclaim.
ἑξακόσιοι, six hundred.

words.g: I rise (spring) up out (of the ground)
words.s: ἐξανατέλλω, I rise (spring) up out (of the ground).

words.g: I am at my wits' end, I despair
words.s: ἐξαπορέομαι, I am at my wits' end, I despair: c. gen. about, 2 Cor. i 8.

words.g: I fit up, equip, furnish, supply
words.s: ἐξαρτίζω, (a) I fit up, equip, furnish, supply, 2 Tim. iii 17; (b) I accomplish, finish, Ac. xxi 5.
ἐξεγείρω, I raise up, arouse.
ἐξορύσσω, (a) I dig out: hence, I open up; (b) I gouge, Gal. iv 15.
ἐξωθέω, I push out, thrust out: εἰς αἰγιαλὸν ἐξῶσαι, to drive the ship upon the beach, Ac. xxvii 39.
ἔοικα, I am like, resemble.
ἐπάγγελμα, a promise.
ἐπαιτέω, I beg, am a beggar.
ἐπαναπαύομαι, I rest upon.
ἐπανέρχομαι, I return.
ἐπανίστημι, intr. tenses, I rise against.
ἐπαρχεία, the official equivalent of Lat. prouincia, sphere of duty, province.
ἐπεγείρω, I arouse, stimulate.
ἐπενδύομαι, I put on (as a garment).
ἐπηρεάζω, I insult, treat wrongfully, molest.
ἐπιδέχομαι, I welcome.
ἐπιδημέω, I am resident (temporarily, in a foreign city).
ἐπιείκεια, considerateness, forbearance, fairness.

words.g: on whom a curse has been invoked, accursed
words.s: ἐπικατάρατος, on whom a curse has been invoked, accursed.
ἐπιλέγομαι, (a) mid. I choose for myself, Ac. xv 40; (b) pass. I am named.
ἐπιλύω, I explain.
ἐπιούσιος (from ἡ ἐπιοῦσα [ἡμέρα]), belonging to the morrow.
ἐπιπόθησις, eager longing (desire).
ἐπιρίπτω, I throw (cast) (upon).
ἐπίσημος, notable, conspicuous.
ἐπισκοπέω, I exercise oversight (care).
ἐπίστασις, caballing (conspiring) against.

words.g: I enjoin, generally in writing, I write
words.s: ἐπιστέλλω, I enjoin, generally in writing, I write.
ἐπισυναγωγή, gathering (collecting) together, assembling.
ἐπιφέρω, I bring forward (against).

words.g: of the next day, I draw on
words.s: ἐπιφώσκω, of the next day, I draw on.
ἐπιχορηγία, supply, provision, equipment.
ἐπιχρίω, I besmear, anoint.

words.g: I am an eyewitness of, behold
words.s: ἐποπτεύω, I am an eyewitness of, behold.
ἐρεθίζω, I stir up, 2 Cor. ix 2: I arouse to anger, provoke, Col. iii 21.
ἔριον, wool.
ἔριφος, a goat.
ἑρμηνεία, translation, interpretation.

words.g: Hermes, the messenger and herald of the Greek gods
words.s: Ἑρμῆς, (a) Hermes, the messenger and herald of the Greek gods, or rather the corresponding Lycaonian deity: to him also corresponded the Latin Mercurius, Ac. xiv 12; (b) Hermes, a Roman Christian.
ἔσοπτρον, a mirror, looking-glass (made of highly polished metal).
ἐσώτερος, inner: τὸ ἐσώτερον, the part that is within, c. gen.
ἑτεροδιδασκαλέω, I teach different things, that is, different from the true or necessary teaching.

words.g: Eva, Eve, wife of Adam, the first man
words.s: Εὔα, Εὕα (Hebr.), Eva, Eve, wife of Adam, the first man.

words.g: good action, well-doing, benefiting, kind service
words.s: εὐεργεσία, good action, well-doing, benefiting, kind service.
εὐθυδρομέω, I run a straight course.
εὐθύνω, (a) I make straight (of the direction, not the surface, of a road); (b) I steer, James iii 4.
εὐκαιρία, a good opportunity, an opportunity.
εὔκαιρος, opportune, timely, suitable: in Mk. vi 21 perhaps = empty, holiday, festal.
εὐκαίρως, opportunely, in season, conveniently.
εὐλάβεια, caution, care; then anxiety, fear (in a good sense); then almost piety.

words.g: I make into a eunuch, emasculate, castrate
words.s: εὐνουχίζω, I make into a eunuch, emasculate, castrate.
εὐσεβέω, I am dutiful, pious: c. acc. pers. towards one who has the right to it, man or God.
εὐσεβῶς, piously.
εὔσπλαγχνος, tender-hearted, merciful.
εὐτόνως, vehemently, powerfully.

words.g: the Euphrates, boundary river of the province Syria
words.s: Εὐφράτης, the Euphrates, boundary river of the province Syria.
εὐφροσύνη, gladness.

words.g: a class of priests who served for a stated number of days
words.s: ἐφημερία, a class of priests who served for a stated number of days.
ἐφικνέομαι, I reach as far as.
ζεῦγος, a yoke, team; hence a pair.

words.g: Zeus, the Greek god of the sky in all its manifestations
words.s: Ζεύς, Zeus, the Greek god of the sky in all its manifestations, corresponding to the Roman Jupiter and to the leading god of the native Lycaonians, &c.
ζέω (lit. I boil, I am boiling), I burn (in spirit).

words.g: I capture alive or I capture for life
words.s: ζωγρέω, I capture alive or I capture for life.
ἡγεμονεύω, I govern.
ἡδύοσμον, mint, peppermint.
ἧλος, a nail.
ἡνίκα, when; ἡνίκα ἄν, whensoever.
ἤπιος, gentle.
ἥσσων (sometimes ἥττων under the influence of ἡττάομαι), less; worse.
ἡσύχιος, quiet.
ἥττημα, a defeat (failure).

words.g: Thaddaeus, one of the twelve disciples
words.s: Θαδδαῖος (Aram. = Theodotus or some similar name), Thaddaeus, one of the twelve disciples (v. l. Λεββαῖος).
θάλπω, (properly I warm, then) I cherish.
θαῦμα, (a) concr., a marvel, a wonder; (b) abstr., wonder.

words.g: Theophilus, a friend of Luke of equestrian rank
words.s: Θεόφιλος, Theophilus, a friend of Luke of equestrian rank, to whom the Gospel and Acts are dedicated.
θεριστής, a reaper, harvester.

words.g: I lead around, I make a show (spectacle) of
words.s: θριαμβεύω, (properly, I lead one as my prisoner in a triumphal procession, hence) I lead around, I make a show (spectacle) of.
θυγάτριον, a little (young) daughter.
θυρίς, a window-sill.

words.g: Jaïrus, a Jewish ruler of the synagogue
words.s: Ἰάειρος, Jaïrus, a Jewish ruler of the synagogue.
ἱερατεία, the duty (office) of a priest.
ἱεράτευμα, act or office of priesthood.
Ἱεροσολυμείτης, an inhabitant of Jerusalem, see Ἱερουσαλήμ.

words.g: Jechoniah, son of Josiah and father of Salathiel
words.s: Ἰεχονίας (Hebr.), Jechoniah, son of Josiah and father of Salathiel.

words.g: I make sufficient, I make fit
words.s: ἱκανόω, I make sufficient, I make fit.

words.g: I have mercy on, I show favour to
words.s: ἱλάσκομαι, (a) c. dat. I have mercy on, I show favour to; (b) tr. with obj. of sins, I forgive.
ἱλασμός, a propitiation (of an angry god).

ἱλαστήριον (original idea, propitiation of an angry god), (a) a sin offering, by which the wrath of the deity shall be appeased, a means of propitiation, Rom. iii 25; (b) the covering of the ark, which was sprinkled with the atoning blood on the Day of Atonement (Hebr. Kappôreth), Heb. ix 5.
ἵλεως, propitious, forgiving, Heb. viii 12: ἵλεώς σοι = ἵλεως εἴη σοι ὁ θεός, may the god be favourable to you, God be merciful to you, may God help you, God forbid! Mt. xvi 22.

words.g: I clothe, I provide clothing for
words.s: ἱματίζω, I clothe, I provide clothing for.
Ἰουδαϊσμός, the Jewish religion, Judaism.

words.g: Julius, a Roman centurion on special service
words.s: Ἰούλιος, Julius, a Roman centurion on special service.

words.g: a horse-soldier, a mounted soldier, a cavalryman
words.s: ἱππεύς, a horse-soldier, a mounted soldier, a cavalryman.
ἶρις, a rainbow.
ἰχθύδιον, a little fish.

words.g: Joatham, son of Ozias and father of Achaz
words.s: Ἰωάθαμ (Hebr.), Joatham, son of Ozias and father of Achaz.

words.g: Jobed, Obed, son of Boaz and Ruth, father of Jesse
words.s: Ἰωβήδ (Ὠβήδ) (Hebr.), Jobed, Obed, son of Boaz and Ruth, father of Jesse, and grandfather of David.

words.g: Joram, son of Jehoshaphat and father of Ozias
words.s: Ἰωράμ (Hebr.), Joram, son of Jehoshaphat and father of Ozias.

words.g: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, son of Asaph
words.s: Ἰωσαφάτ (Hebr.), Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, son of Asaph, father of Joram, an ancestor of Jesus.

words.g: Josiah, king of Judah, son of Amos and father of Jechoniah
words.s: Ἰωσείας (Hebr.), Josiah, king of Judah, son of Amos and father of Jechoniah.
καθηγητής, a leader, a teacher.
καθήκω, impers. καθήκει, it is fitting: τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα (a technical phrase of the Stoic philosophy), what is unfitting.

words.g: Cainam, one of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Καϊνάμ (Καϊνάν) (Hebr.), Cainam, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
καινότης, freshness, newness.
καίτοι, and yet.
κακουχέω, I treat evilly.
καμμύω, I close.
κάμνω, (a) I am weary, Heb. xii 3; (b) I am ill, James v 15.

words.g: a Cananaean, a (former) adherent of the party of Zealots
words.s: Καναναῖος, a Cananaean, a (former) adherent of the party of Zealots (= ζηλωτής).
Καππαδοκία, Cappadocia, a large Roman province in the central eastern part of Asia Minor.

words.g: a knower of the inner life (character)
words.s: καρδιογνώστης, a knower of the inner life (character).
καταβάλλω (cf. iacere), (a) mid. I lay, of a foundation, Heb. vi 1 (cf. καταβολή); (b) met. I cast down, 2 Cor. iv 9.
καταδουλόω, I enslave.
καταδυναστεύω, I overpower, quell; I treat harshly.
κατακλάω, I break up.
κατακλείω, I shut up.
κατακολουθέω, I follow after.
κατάκρισις, condemnation.
καταλαλιά, evil-speaking, backbiting, detraction.
καταπονέω, I illtreat; pass. I am getting the worse.
καταποντίζομαι, I am submerged, I drown.
κατασκάπτω, I dig down.
κατασκήνωσις, a dwelling.
καταστέλλω, I quieten.
καταστρέφω, I overturn.
καταστροφή, destruction, material or spiritual.
κατάσχεσις, abstr., (permanent) possession.
κατατίθημι, (a) (depono) I lay down, deposit; (b) mid. χάριν, χάριτα, I lay down or deposit a favour, with the view of receiving one in return, I seek favour.
καταφεύγω (confugio), I flee for refuge (implying that the refuge is reached); aor. indicates moment of arrival.
καταχέω, I pour (down) over.

words.g: I use to the full, I use up
words.s: καταχράομαι (abutor), I use to the full, I use up.
κατεξουσιάζω, I have (exercise) power (authority) over.
κατοικητήριον, a habitation, dwelling-place.
καῦμα, burning heat, heat.
καυσόω, tr. I burn (perhaps by internal heat).
κενοφωνία, a worthless utterance.

words.g: Cenchreae, the harbour town of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf
words.s: Κενχρεαί, Cenchreae, the harbour town of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf.

words.g: a little hook, an apostrophe on letters of the alphabet
words.s: κεραία (variation κερέα), a little hook, an apostrophe on letters of the alphabet, distinguishing them from other like letters, or a separation stroke between letters.
κεράμιον, an earthenware pitcher.

words.g: the chief matter, the main point
words.s: κεφάλαιον, (a) the chief matter, the main point, Heb. viii 1; (b) a sum of money, Ac. xxii 28.

words.g: I play on the harp, I harp
words.s: κιθαρίζω, intr. and tr., I play on the harp, I harp, with acc. of the tune.
κιθαρῳδός, a harpist.
κλάσις, breaking.
κλίβανος, an oven, a furnace.

words.g: a couch or litter of a sick person
words.s: κλινίδιον, a couch or litter of a sick person.
κλοπή, thieving, theft.
κλύδων, rough water, roughness of water; κ. θαλάσσης a rough sea, James i 6.

words.g: a quadrans, the smallest Roman copper coin
words.s: κοδράντης (Latin, = quadrans), a quadrans, the smallest Roman copper coin, a quarter of an as, the sixteenth part of a sestertius.
κολάζω, I punish; mid. I cause to be punished.
κόλασις, punishing, punishment, perhaps with the idea of deprivation, 1 John iv 18.

words.g: I wear the hair long, I allow the hair to grow long
words.s: κομάω, I wear the hair long, I allow the hair to grow long.
κονιάω, I whitewash.

words.g: I fill, sate, glut, feed full
words.s: κορέννυμι, I fill, sate, glut, feed full.
Κορίνθιος, Corinthian, of Corinth.
κοσμικός, earthly, worldly (belonging to the present, earthly world as opposed to the heavenly and future).
κόσμιος, orderly, virtuous.
κρέας (caro), flesh: plur. (carnes) pieces of flesh, kinds of flesh.

words.g: a Cretan, an inhabitant of Crete
words.s: Κρής, a Cretan, an inhabitant of Crete.
κρίθινος, made of barley.
κρίνον, a lily growing wild, variously identified with the red anemone, the white lily, the sword lily.

words.g: Crispus, ruler of the synagogue at Corinth
words.s: Κρῖσπος, Crispus, ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, converted and baptized by St. Paul.
κρύσταλλος, crystal.
κρυφαῖος, hidden, secret: ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ = ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ.
κυβερνήτης, a steersman, a pilot.
κυρία, a lady: voc. my lady, an address of courtesy.

words.g: of the Lord (κύριος), special to the Lord
words.s: κυριακός (dominicus), of the Lord (κύριος), special to the Lord: δεῖπνον, supper (dinner) for church members, combined with the Eucharist: ἡμέρα, Sunday (cf. Fr. dimanche, Span. domingo, Ital. domenica). [In constitutional law means imperial.]
κυρόω, I ratify, confirm.
λατομέω, I hew (of stone).
λεμά (Aramaic), why.
λεντίον (Latin, = linteum), a towel.
λευκαίνω, I whiten.
λίβανος (Semitic word), frankincense, incense.
λιβανωτός, a censer.
λικμάω, I crush to powder.
λιμήν, a harbour, port.
λίνον, flax; linen.

words.g: a Roman pound, of about twelve ounces
words.s: λίτρα (libra), a Roman pound, of about twelve ounces, 327½ grammes.
λογεία, λογία (from λογεύω, ‘I collect’), a collection, collecting (of money), particularly of an irregular local contribution for religious purposes.
λογικός, (a) reasonable, rational, Rom. xii 1; (b) metaphorical, as contrasted with literal, 1 Pet. ii 2 (so perhaps also in Rom. xii 1).
λογισμός, reasoning, thinking.
λοίδορος, a railer, reviler, abuser.
λοιμός (pestis), (a) a pestilence; (b) a pestilent fellow, Ac. xxiv 5.

Λούκιος, Lucius, (a) of Cyrene, an early Christian, in the church of Antioch, Ac. xiii 1, by some identified with the evangelist Luke; (b) a Christian with Paul at Corinth, by some identified with (a), Rom. xvi 21.

words.g: a bath (of the water, not the vessel), water for washing
words.s: λουτρόν, a bath (of the water, not the vessel), water for washing, washing.

words.g: Lydia, a lady resident of Philippi
words.s: Λυδία, Lydia, a lady resident of Philippi, native of Thyatira in Lydia (Asia Minor), and engaged in the clothing trade.

words.g: Claudius Lysias, a Roman tribune of the soldiers in Jerusalem
words.s: Λυσίας, Claudius Lysias, a Roman tribune of the soldiers in Jerusalem.

words.g: the purchasing money for manumitting slaves, a ransom
words.s: λύτρον, the purchasing money for manumitting slaves, a ransom, the price of ransoming; especially the sacrifice by which expiation is effected, an offering of expiation.

words.g: Matthat, son of Levi and father of Jorem
words.s: Μαθθάτ (Ματθάτ) (Hebr.), Matthat, son of Levi and father of Jorem, an ancestor of Jesus.

words.g: Matthias, elected one of the Twelve
words.s: Μαθθίας, Matthias, elected one of the Twelve in room of the deceased Judas.
μακαρίζω, I deem (declare) happy.

words.g: in vain, in an unreal way
words.s: μάτην, in vain, in an unreal way.

words.g: Matthan, son of Eleazar and father of Jacob
words.s: Μαθθάν (Hebr.), Matthan, son of Eleazar and father of Jacob, an ancestor of Jesus.
Ματταθίας (Hebr.), Mattathias, an ancestor of Jesus.
μεθοδεία (from μέθοδος, a way of search after something, an inquiry; a method), scheming, craftiness.
μέθυσος (originally, tipsy), a drunkard.
μελετάω, I devise, plan; practise, exercise myself in.

words.g: Melchi, one of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Μελχεί (Hebr.), Melchi, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
μέμφομαι, I blame.
μερισμός, (a) a distributing, a distribution, Heb. ii 4; (b) a parting, dividing, severance, separation.
μεσημβρία (lit. midday, hence, the position of the sun at midday), the south.

words.g: Mesopotamia, the Country between the (two) Rivers
words.s: Μεσοποταμία, Mesopotamia, the Country between the (two) Rivers, i.e. the Euphrates and the Tigris.
Μεσσίας (Hebrew), Messiah, the Anointed One, generally translated into Greek as Χριστός.

words.g: I turn about, I change the position of
words.s: μετάγω (usually transfer, transport, and met., to a better mind), I turn about, I change the position of.
μεταίρω, I change my position, remove.
μεταλλάσσω, I transform, alter.
μεταστρέφω, I turn, change.
μετοικίζω, I transport.
μηδαμῶς, not at all.
μήπω, not yet.
μήτρα, the womb.

words.g: a paid worker, a hired servant, a hireling
words.s: μίσθιος (mercennarius), a paid worker, a hired servant, a hireling (contrasted with a slave).
μισθόομαι, I hire, engage.
Μιχαήλ, Michahel, Michael, an archangel.
μοιχεία, adultery.
μονή, (a) abstr., μονὴν ποιεῖσθαι, to stay, to dwell, John xiv 23; (b) concr., lodging, dwelling-place, room.
μόνον, acc. sing. neut. of μόνος, used as adv., only.
μονόφθαλμος, one-eyed, with one eye only.
μόρφωσις, a mere form, outline.

words.g: Mysia, a country in the NW. of the Roman province Asia
words.s: Μυσία, Mysia, a country in the NW. of the Roman province Asia (and of Asia Minor).
μωμάομαι, I calumniate, slander.
Ναζαρά (the Greek form, declined), Ναζαρέτ (the native form, not declined), Nazareth, a city of Galilee, where Jesus lived before His ministry.
νάρδος (Hebr., borrowed into Persian and Sanscrit), spikenard, a perfume made originally from the Nardostachys Jatamansi growing on the Himalayas.
ναυαγέω (naufrago), (a) I am shipwrecked; so (b) figuratively, I come to ruin.
νέκρωσις, (a) putting to death, 2 Cor. iv 10; (b) dead or lifeless condition, Rom. iv 19.
νεύω, I nod, make a sign.
νήθω (a vulgar and late form of νέω, neo), I spin.
νῆστις, fasting, without food.

words.g: a Nicolaitan, a follower of Nicolaus
words.s: Νικολαΐτης, a Nicolaitan, a follower of Nicolaus (a heretic at Ephesus).
νομή, (a) pasture; (b) ἔχειν νομήν, to spread, 2 Tim. ii 17.

words.g: in a legitimate way, according to law and regulation
words.s: νομίμως (legitime), in a legitimate way, according to law and regulation.

words.g: I ordain, lay down, give the sanction of law to, enact
words.s: νομοθετέω, (a) I ordain, lay down, give the sanction of law to, enact, Heb. viii 6; (b) I base legally, I regulate, I direct.
νυστάζω, I sleep, slumber; met. 2 Pet. ii 3.
νωθρός, blunt, dull, hence spiritually; sluggish, remiss, slack.
ξενία (hospitium), a lodging, or rather, abstr., hospitality.
ξύλινος, made of wood.
ὀγδοήκοντα, eighty.
ὁδοιπορία, journeying, travelling, travel.
ὀδύνη, acute mental pain.
ὀδυρμός, mourning, grieving.

words.g: a sheet, made of fine linen
words.s: ὀθόνη (a word of Semitic origin), a sheet, made of fine linen.
οἰκητήριον (habitaculum), a dwelling-place, lit. and met.
οἰκιακός, a member of one's household.
οἰκτείρω (Attic οἰκτίρω), I pity.
οἰνοπότης, an excessive wine-drinker.
ὁλόκληρος (properly a word of Greek ritual, of either victim for sacrifice or priest, free from bodily defect), complete (in every part), entire, whole.
ὄμμα, an eye.

words.g: of like feelings, almost, of like nature
words.s: ὁμοιοπαθής, of like feelings, almost, of like nature.
ὁμοιότης, resemblance: understand ἡμῶν in Heb. iv 15, cf. vii 15.

words.g: Onesimus, a slave of Philemon, a Christian of Colossae
words.s: Ὀνήσιμος (originally adj. useful, hence the play upon words in Philem. 10, 11, and very common as slave name), Onesimus, a slave of Philemon, a Christian of Colossae.

words.g: Onesiphorus, a Christian of the province of Asia
words.s: Ὀνησίφορος, Onesiphorus, a Christian of the province of Asia. (An Onesiphorus, probably intended to be the same person, comes into the Acts of Paul).
ὀνικός, connected with an ass; μύλος ὀνικός, an upper millstone so heavy that it requires an ass to turn it (in contrast to the ordinary handmill).
ὀπή, a crevice (in a rock); a cave.
ὀργυιά, a fathom (six feet).
ὀρεινός, ὀρινός; ἡ ὀρεινὴ (sc. γῆ), the mountain (mountainous) country (region), the highlands.
ὀρθός, straight, erect (perhaps with reference to recovery of health, cf. ‘non erigit aegros . . . Bacchus,’ Lucan, B. C. iv 378), Ac. xiv 10; met. that goes in the right direction, Heb. xii 13.
ὄρθρος, dawn, early morning, day-break.
ὁρκίζω, with double acc., of the one adjured and of the one in the name of whom he is adjured, I adjure.
ὁρμή, a sudden movement, an impulse, communicated by the hand, James iii 4; inclination, hostile intention, instigation.
ὄρνις, a bird.
ὀρφανός, orphaned; an orphan; hence friendless, John xiv 18.
ὁσιότης, holiness, piety.
ὀστράκινος, made of pottery, of earthenware.
οὐρανόθεν, from heaven, from the sky.
οὐσία, property.
ὀφείλημα, (a) a debt; (b) in Aramaic the same word indicates a debt and a sin; hence a sin (probably as that for which we owe reparation to God or to another person).
ὀφθαλμοδουλεία, enslavement to the eye, the subjection that waits upon a glance of a master's eye.
παιδευτής, one who disciplines, a trainer; almost a chastiser, Heb. xii 9.

παλινγενεσία, (a) an eschatological term (used by Pythagoreans and Stoics, found in Josephus of the rebirth of the fatherland after the exile, and in Philo of the re-birth of the earth after the flood), in Mt. xix 28 for the current conception of the Messianic renewal of the world or of the people Israel, rebirth; (b) rebirth of the individual life following on or typified in baptism, Tit. iii 5.
παντελής; εἰς τὸ παντελές (omnino), utterly, at all, Lk. xiii 11; in Heb. vii 25 either entirely, or, more probably, for ever, finally.
παραβιάζομαι, I urge, press.
παραινέω, I admonish, advise.
παράκειμαι, I rest with.
παραλέγομαι (lego), I coast along, sail along.
παραλογίζομαι, I deceive, beguile.
παραπικρασμός, embitterment, provocation, irritation.

words.g: I come in from the side
words.s: παρεισέρχομαι, I come in from the side.

words.g: I sojourn (in), as a resident stranger
words.s: παροικέω, I sojourn (in), as a resident stranger.

words.g: a sojourn in a foreign city or land
words.s: παροικία, a sojourn in a foreign city or land; so also in the spiritual sense (cf. παρεπίδημος), 1 Pet. i 17.

words.g: one given too much to wine, an excessive drinker
words.s: πάροινος, one given too much to wine, an excessive drinker.

words.g: I arouse to anger, I provoke
words.s: παροξύνω, I arouse to anger, I provoke.

words.g: irritation of mind, sharp feeling, indignation
words.s: παροξυσμός, (a) irritation of mind, sharp feeling, indignation; (b) spurring, incitement, Heb. x 24.
παροργίζω, I provoke to anger.
παροψίς, a bowl, dish.

words.g: Paphos, a city at the western end of Cyprus
words.s: Πάφος, Paphos, a city at the western end of Cyprus.
παχύνω, I thicken: used with καρδία, of obtuseness of mind, it has become obtuse.
πεῖρα, an attempt, a trial; πεῖραν λαμβάνειν, to have experience of.
πέλαγος, the open sea: in Mt. xviii 6 the use of the two words for sea produces a more impressive effect.
πεντακόσιοι, five hundred.

words.g: Pergamum, an important city of the Roman province Asia
words.s: Πέργαμον (possibly the other form Πέργαμος, Pergamus, was intended), Pergamum, an important city of the Roman province Asia.
περιαστράπτω, I flash (gleam) around like lightning.
περιβόλαιον, a wrapper, mantle.
περίεργος, (a) inquisitive, prying, a busybody; (b) curious, magical, Ac. xix 19.
περιέχω, (a) I contain (of a book containing subject matter): hence, impersonal, it stands (has its content) thus, 1 Pet. ii 6; (b) I encompass, surround; I get hold of, seize.
περικεφαλαία, a helmet.
περιλάμπω, I shine around.
περιλείπω, I leave behind.
πέρυσι, adverb, the previous year, last year.
πηδάλιον, a helm, rudder.
πηλίκος, how large, how great.
πικρός, bitter, lit. and met.
πικρῶς, bitterly.

words.g: Pisidia, a country of Asia Minor
words.s: Πισιδία, Pisidia, a country of Asia Minor, being the south-western part of the Roman province Galatia.
πιστικός, probably = genuine, pure.
πλάσσω, I mould out of clay; I create.
πλήκτης, a striker; a pugnacious person.
πνευματικῶς, spiritually, in a spiritual way; from a spiritual point of view.
πνοή, (a) breath, Ac. xvii 25; (b) gust, breeze, wind, Ac. ii 2. (Cf. Augustine, De Natura et Origine Animae I 14 § 19).
ποίημα (concrete), creation, workmanship, handiwork; plur. pieces of work.
πολιτάρχης, a politarch, a city-magistrate (a special, characteristically Macedonian, title of the chief magistrates (5 or 6 in number) of Thessalonica and a few other cities).
πολιτεία (ciuitas), (a) commonwealth, polity; citizen body, Eph. ii 12; (b) (the Roman) citizenship, citizen-rights, franchise, Ac. xxii 28.

words.g: I live the life of a citizen
words.s: πολιτεύομαι (a characteristic Greek idea), I live the life of a citizen; I live as a member of a (citizen) body; I fulfil corporate duties: in Phil. i 27 some take simply of manner of life.
πόμα, drink.

words.g: Pontus, a Roman province in the north of Asia Minor
words.s: Πόντος, Pontus, a Roman province in the north of Asia Minor, bordering on the Black Sea, governed along with Bithynia.

words.g: the Greek form of the Latin name Publius
words.s: Πόπλιος, the Greek form of the Latin name Publius (originally the same in form as the Greek form); a governor of Malta.
πορεία, a journey.

words.g: a means of gain, a way of making a living
words.s: πορισμός (quaestus), a means of gain, a way of making a living, a livelihood, a living.
πόρρωθεν, from a long distance, Heb. xi 13: hence (cf. ἔξωθεν), at a long distance, far away, Lk. xvii 12.
πράκτωρ, (usually, a collector of revenue, but in Lk.) an officer (usher) of the court.
πρασιά, a vegetable or flower bed: πρασιαὶ πρασιαί, colloquial type of phrase, like vegetable or flower beds, referring to the rectangular arrangement of the groups.
πρεσβεία, an embassy, delegation.
πρεσβεύω (especially, I am on embassy to the Emperor), I am an ambassador.
προαμαρτάνω, I sin previously.
προβάλλω, (a) tr. I put forward; (b) I put forth shoots, I sprout, burst into leaf, Lk. xxi 30.
πρόγνωσις, foreknowledge.
πρόγονος, an ancestor.
προενάρχομαι, I begin earlier (previously).
προεπαγγέλλομαι, I promise beforehand.
προετοιμάζω, I prepare beforehand.
προκαταγγέλλω, I announce beforehand.
πρόνοια, forethought, foresight; πρόνοιαν ποιοῦμαι = προνοέω.
προπετής (of thoughtless haste), impulsive, rash, reckless.

words.g: I journey in front, I go before
words.s: προπορεύομαι, I journey in front, I go before.
προσαίτης, a beggar.

words.g: I fill up by adding, make up, supply
words.s: προσαναπληρόω, I fill up by adding, make up, supply.
προσανατίθεμαι, I turn (have recourse) to.
προσδοκία, expectation, waiting.
προσκολλάω, (lit. I glue one thing to another), I join (unite) closely: fut. pass. probably as middle, I cleave (to).
προσκυλίω, I roll to (up to).
προσλαλέω, I speak to.
προσοχθίζω, I entertain anger (disgust, abhorrence).
προσρήγνυμι, I dash against.
προτρέχω, I run forward.

words.g: I am (previously), I have been already
words.s: προϋπάρχω, I am (previously), I have been already.
προφέρω, I bring forth (out), produce.
προφῆτις, a prophetess.
πρωΐα, early morning.
πρωϊνός (from πρωΐ) (matutinus), belonging to the morning, morning: opposite ἑσπερινός.

words.g: the prow, the bow of a ship
words.s: πρῴρα, the prow, the bow of a ship.

words.g: the gable, roof, projection of the temple roof, pinnacle
words.s: πτερύγιον, the gable, roof, projection of the temple roof, pinnacle; or possibly (see ἱερόν), the wall surrounding the temple precinct.

words.g: I scare, I strike with panic
words.s: πτοέω, I scare, I strike with panic.

words.g: a winnowing-fan, a simple wooden pitchfork
words.s: πτύον, a winnowing-fan, a simple wooden pitchfork.
πτῶσις, falling, fall.
πυκνός, (spissus, thick; hence) frequent: acc. plur. neut. πυκνά as adv., frequently, often (cf. regular comparative of adverb, Ac. xxiv 26).
πυρά, a fire.

words.g: I have fever, I suffer from fever
words.s: πυρέσσω, I have fever, I suffer from fever.
πυρράζω, I am red (ruddy).
πυρρός, red.
Ῥαάβ (Hebr.), Rahab, a Canaanitess, who rescued the Hebrew spies at Jericho, by tradition wife of Salmon (Mt. i 4, 5).
ῥαββουνεί (Aramaic, a fuller form of ῥαββεί), my master.
ῥαβδίζω, I flog (beat) with a rod (staff), a Roman punishment.
ῥαβδοῦχος (lictor), (lit. a rod holder, holder of rods), a lictor, an attendant (orderly), of certain Roman magistrates, a tipstaff.
ῥάκος, a piece of cloth.
ῥαντισμός, sprinkling, as a symbolic purification (cf. Exod. xxiv 6–8).
ῥαπίζω, I slap, strike.
ῥαφίς, a sewing needle (= classical βελόνη, used by Lk.).

words.g: Rehoboam, son of Solomon, and King of Israel
words.s: Ῥοβοάμ (Hebr.), Rehoboam, son of Solomon, and King of Israel.

words.g: Rufus, a Christian man in Rome
words.s: Ῥοῦφος, Rufus, a Christian man in Rome (Rom. xvi 13), probably to be identified with the brother of Alexander and son of Simon of Cyrene mentioned in Mk. xv 21.
ῥυπαρός, shabby, soiled: hence morally, filthy, corrupt, sinful, Rev. xxii 11.
σαβαχθανεί (Aramaic), thou hast forsaken.
σαβαώθ (Hebrew), hosts, armies.
Σαδώκ (Hebr.), Zadok, an ancestor of Jesus.

words.g: Sala, the name of two of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Σαλά (Hebr.), Sala, the name of two of the ancestors of Jesus (v. l. in Lk. iii 32).
Σαλήμ, Salem, doubtless identical with Jerusalem.

words.g: Salmon, son of Naasson and father of Boes (Boaz)
words.s: Σαλμών, Salmon, son of Naasson and father of Boes (Boaz) (v. l. in Lk. iii 32).

words.g: Salome, wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John
words.s: Σαλώμη, Salome, wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John, the disciples.
Σαμαρεῖτις, a Samaritan woman.

words.g: a sandal, an open-work shoe, a shoe
words.s: σανδάλιον, a sandal, an open-work shoe, a shoe.

words.g: sardius, sard, a quartz of a deep red colour
words.s: σάρδιον, sardius, sard, a quartz of a deep red colour.

words.g: a large measure equivalent to 1½ modii
words.s: σάτον (Aramaic), a large measure equivalent to 1½ modii, that is, nearly three English gallons.

words.g: an object of worship, a thing worshipped
words.s: σέβασμα, an object of worship, a thing worshipped.

words.g: I bring under the influence of the moon
words.s: σεληνιάζω, I bring under the influence of the moon: pass. I am epileptic (the state of an epileptic being attributed to the moon [σελήνη]).
σιαγών, a cheek.
σιγή, silence.
Σιδώνιος, belonging to Sidon, Sidonian; hence, as subst., a Sidonian: ἡ Σιδωνία (sc. χώρα), the region or territory of Sidon, Lk. iv 26.
σκῆνος, a tent: so met. (used in Pythagorean philosophy) of the body as the temporary dwelling-place of the soul.
σκυθρωπός, with downcast countenance; sad-faced; gloomy.
σμύρνα (= μύρρα), myrrh, a fragrant gum-resin from the Arabian Balsamodendron Myrrhae.

words.g: Smyrna, a great port of the Roman province Asia
