words.s: Σμύρνα (better spelling Ζμύρνα), Smyrna, a great port of the Roman province Asia.
σοφίζω, I make wise: σεσοφισμένος, fictitious, 2 Pet. i 16.

words.g: Spain, roughly co-extensive with the modern country
words.s: Σπανία (Latin = Hispania), Spain, roughly co-extensive with the modern country of the name.
σπάομαι, I draw my (sword).
σπαργανόω, I swathe.

words.g: I am a voluptuary, I am wanton
words.s: σπαταλάω, I am a voluptuary, I am wanton.

words.g: I pour out an offering of wine to a god
words.s: σπένδω, I pour out an offering of wine to a god: hence pass. met. of the outpouring of one’s life blood in service and suffering.
σπίλος, a spot of disfigurement.
σπιλόω, I stain, lit. or met.
στέλλω (originally, I set, place: hence, I bring together, make compact; then, I restrain, check), mid. I draw (shrink) back from anything.
στεναγμός, a groan.
στρατεία, military service, used met.
στρατιά, an army.
στρηνιάω, I am wanton, I wanton.
στυγνάζω, (a) I am sad, Mk. x 22; (b) I am dull (overcast), Mt. xvi 3.
συκοφαντέω (calumnior), I accuse falsely.
σύμμορφος, sharing the form of another.
συμπόσιον, properly a drinking bout, following dinner: συμπόσια συμπόσια (colloquial), in companies of diners.
σύμφορος, advantageous: τὸ σύμφορον, as substantive.
συναθλέω, I compete together with others, originally of athletic contests, and then met.
συναθροίζω, tr. I gather together, assemble.
συναναβαίνω, I go up with.

words.g: I lend a hand along with
words.s: συναντιλαμβάνομαι, I lend a hand along with, I take interest in (a thing) along with (others), I assist jointly to perform some task, I co-operate with, I take my share in.

συναρμολογέω (an architectural term, ἁρμός meaning ‘the side of a stone’, and -λογεῖν added by analogy with λιθολόγος without its proper force), I fit together (by means of all the elaborate preparatory processes necessary).

words.g: I reign along with (together with) another
words.s: συνβασιλεύω, I reign along with (together with) another, I am a king with, in met. sense.

words.g: I go in with, I enter with
words.s: συνεισέρχομαι, I go in with, I enter with.
συνέκδημος, a travelling-companion.
συνευωχέομαι, I feast along with.
συνζωοποιέω, I make living along with.
συνθάπτω, I bury along with.

words.g: I break in pieces, break completely
words.s: συνθλάω, I break in pieces, break completely.
συνθλίβω, I press closely upon, hustle.
συνκάθημαι, I am sitting (seated) with: in Ac. xxvi 30, perhaps to be compared with English assessor.

words.g: I cause to sit along with
words.s: συνκαθίζω, (a) tr. I cause to sit along with; (b) intr. I sit in company (together).

words.g: I am ill treated along with, I take my share of suffering
words.s: συνκακοπαθέω, I am ill treated along with, I take my share of suffering (in 2 Tim. i 8 the dat. is not governed by συν, but = for the benefit of).
συνκεράννυμι, (a) I mix together, compound, 1 Cor. xii 24; (b) pass. with dat. of instrument (πίστει), I agree with, Heb. iv 2 (reading acc. plur.).
συνμέτοχος, a fellow sharer, a partner.

words.g: I share knowledge with another, I am privy to anything
words.s: σύνοιδα (conscius sum), I share knowledge with another, I am privy to anything. In fact the word especially implies consciousness of guilt, e.g. 1 Cor. iv 4.
συνοχή (lit. compression; then narrowness), met. anxiety.
συνπαθέω, I suffer along with.
συνπάσχω, I suffer together.
συνπέμπω, I send along with.

words.g: I wrap round, swathe in a sort of winding-sheet
words.s: συνστέλλω, (a) I wrap round, swathe in a sort of winding-sheet, or possibly, I lay out, Ac. v 6; (b) I contract, compress; hence I shorten, 1 Cor. vii 29.
συνστρατιώτης, a fellow-soldier, comrade in arms.
συντόμως, briefly.

words.g: I throw violently on the ground
words.s: συσπαράσσω, I throw violently on the ground.
συστρέφω, (a) tr. I gather together, collect, Ac. xxviii 3; (b) mid. either, I press together (about one) or I stroll.
συστροφή, a crowding together; hence, a seditious meeting, Ac. xix 40; a conspiracy, Ac. xxiii 12.
Συχέμ, Sychem, Shechem, Sicyma (later Neapolis, from which modern Nablus), a city of Samaria.
σχῆμα, the outward (changeable) fashion (form).
σχοινίον, a rope; a cable, hawser.
σχολάζω, (a) I have leisure, c. dat. for, 1 Cor. vii 5; (b) I stand empty, of a house, Mt. xii 44, [Lk.] xi 25.
σωματικός, (a) bodily, hence almost = visible, tangible, Lk. iii 22; (b) bodily, physical, contrasted with ‘mental’, ‘spiritual’, 1 Tim. iv 8.
σωρεύω, I heap: c. acc. et dat., I overwhelm some one with something, 2 Tim. iii 6.

words.g: Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue at Corinth
words.s: Σωσθένης, Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue at Corinth (Ac. xviii 17), probably to be identified with the Christian of 1 Cor. i 1.

words.g: Tabitha, a Christian woman at Joppa
words.s: Ταβειθά, Tabitha, a Christian woman at Joppa.
ταλαιπωρία, wretchedness, distress, misery.
ταλαίπωρος, wretched, miserable.
τάραχος, disturbance.
Ταρσεύς, belonging to Tarsus, a Tarsian.
τάχα, perhaps.
ταχινός, speedy, possibly sudden.

words.g: a worker in wood, a carpenter
words.s: τέκτων, a worker in wood, a carpenter.
τελειότης, moral completeness (perfection).
τελείωσις, a bringing to completion (perfection, fulfilment).

words.g: Tertullus, a barrister acting as professional prosecutor
words.s: Τέρτυλλος (Latin), Tertullus, a barrister acting as professional prosecutor of St. Paul at Caesarea.

words.g: of forty years, forty years long
words.s: τεσσαρακονταετής, of forty years, forty years long.
τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατος, fourteenth.
τιμωρέω, I punish.
τίτλος (Latin) (titulus), an inscription.
τοιγαροῦν, accordingly, wherefore.
τόκος (from τίκτω, cf. Shakespeare’s ‘breed of barren metal’), interest.
τραυματίζω, I wound.
τραχύς, rough.
τριακόσιοι, three hundred.
τρίβολος, a thistle.
τρύβλιον, a dish.
τρυφή, luxury.
ὕαλος, glass.
ὑβριστής, noun as adj. insolent, insulting, outrageous.
Ὑμέναιος, Hymenaeus, a backsliding Christian.
ὕμνος, a hymn, especially of praise to God.
ὕπαρξις, a possession, generally of personal property.
ὑπεναντίος, opposing, hostile; substantive, adversary, Heb. x 27.
ὑπερλίαν (lit. more than very much): in irony, οἱ ὑπερλίαν ἀπόστολοι, the super-apostles.
ὑπέρογκος (lit. of great or excessive bulk), arrogant.
ὑπεροχή, superiority, 1 Cor. ii 1; a position of superiority, 1 Tim. ii 2.
ὑπερπερισσεύω, (a) intr. I abound exceedingly; (b) mid. as act. I overflow.
ὑποζύγιον, a beast of burden, either an ass or a mule.

words.g: I sail under the lee of (close to)
words.s: ὑποπλέω, I sail under the lee of (close to).

words.g: I place (put) under some danger, I expose
words.s: ὑποτίθημι, (a) I place (put) under some danger, I expose; (b) mid. I suggest, advise.

words.g: a figurative representation, serving as an example
words.s: ὑποτύπωσις, a figurative representation, serving as an example.
ὑποχωρέω, I withdraw.

words.g: I strike under the eye, bruise
words.s: ὑπωπιάζω (from ὑπώπιον, which is from ὑπό and ὤψ, ‘that part of the face under the eyes’), I strike under the eye, bruise; hence, I treat severely, 1 Cor. ix 27, I molest, annoy, harass, worry, exhaust, Lk. xviii 5.
ὕσσωπος, hyssop. In John xix 29 ὑσσώπῳ is a graphic error for ὑσσῷ (pilum), pike.
ὑστέρησις, poverty, want.
ὕψωμα, (a) height, Rom. viii 39; (b) loftiness, haughtiness, (self-)exaltation, 2 Cor. x 5 (but including concrete as well as abstract, whatever is lofty, &c.).
φάγος, a glutton, gourmand.
φανέρωσις, a showing forth, with objective gen.
φάντασμα, an appearance; hence a ghost, a spirit.
φαρμακεία, the practice of drugging, drugging; hence, especially, from the use of mysterious liquids, sorcery, witchcraft, inextricably combined with idolatry.
φαρμακός (see φαρμακεία), a sorcerer, magician.
φειδομένως, sparingly.
φήμη (fama), a report, a rumour.

words.g: a measured harmonious sound, of voice or instrument
words.s: φθόγγος, a measured harmonious sound, of voice or instrument; an utterance.
φιλανθρωπία, (a) love of (for) mankind; (b) humanity, kindness, Ac. xxviii 2.
φιλάργυρος, loving money.
φιλοξενία, love to foreigners; entertainment of strangers.
φλογίζω, I set on fire.
φοῖνιξ, a palm tree, John xii 13; a branch of a palm tree, a palm, Rev. vii 9.
φορτίζω, I load, burden.
φραγελλόω (Latin, flagello), I lash, flog.
φρήν, the mind.

words.g: understanding, which leads to right action
words.s: φρόνησις, understanding, which leads to right action.
φωλεός, a hole in the earth.
φωστήρ, a light, perhaps a sun, Rev. xxi 11; a star, Phil. ii 15.
φωτισμός, (a) act. enlightening, 2 Cor. iv 4; (b) pass. enlightenment, 2 Cor. iv 6.
χαλεπός, (a) hard, difficult, 2 Tim. iii 1; (b) difficult to restrain, dangerous, Mt. viii 28.
χαλιναγωγέω, I bridle, met. I keep in check, restrain.
χαλινός, a bridle.

χαλκολίβανος, a word of uncertain signification, translated ‘aeramentum turinum’ (incense bronze) in certain Old Latin authorities, and ‘orichalcum’ (= ὀρείχαλκος [mountain bronze]) in the Vulgate: the latter was understood to be a mixture of gold and copper.
χαμαί (humi), on the ground.
Χαναάν, Canaan, the whole of Palestine (Ac. xiii 19) or Palestine west of the river Jordan (Ac. vii 11).

words.g: I endue with grace (the divine favour)
words.s: χαριτόω (properly, I endow with χάρις), I endue with grace (the divine favour): in Eph. i 6 followed by cognate acc. (genit.).

words.g: Haran, identical with Carrae, in Mesopotamia
words.s: Χαρράν, Haran, identical with Carrae, in Mesopotamia.
χειραγωγέω, I lead by the hand.
χειροτονέω (lit. I stretch out the hand, thus expressing agreement with a motion, then, I elect by show of hands [of popular vote]), I elect.
χιών, snow.
χλαμύς, a cloak.

words.g: a Greek dry measure, equivalent to 1·92 pints
words.s: χοῖνιξ, a Greek dry measure, equivalent to 1·92 pints.
χολή (in LXX represents three Hebrew words meaning respectively, (a) gall, bile, (b) wormwood, (c) poison), (a) gall, bile, Mt. xxvii 34; (b) met. bitterness, that is, intense malignity.
Χοραζείν, Chorazin, probably the present Kerâze, ruins half-an-hour north-west of Tell-ḥum (Capernaum?).
χορηγέω, I supply (with lavish hand).
χοῦς, dust.
χρεοφειλέτης, χρεωφειλέτης, a debtor.
χρῆσις, usage, use.

words.g: I adorn with gold, I overlay with gold
words.s: χρυσόω, I adorn with gold, I overlay with gold.
ψευδάδελφος, a false brother, i.e. an unreal (insincere) Christian.
ψευδομαρτυρία, giving of false evidence; false witness.

words.g: a false witness, one who gives untrue evidence
words.s: ψευδομάρτυς, a false witness, one who gives untrue evidence.

words.g: a false Messiah, a pretended Messiah
words.s: ψευδόχριστος, a false Messiah, a pretended Messiah.
ψηφίζω, I count up (lit. with pebbles).
ψιχίον, a crumb.
ψωμίζω, (a) I confer a dole upon, Rom. xii 20; (b) I dole out.
ὦμος, shoulder.
ὠτάριον (auricula, hence Fr. oreille), an ear.
ὠφέλεια, advantage.

words.g: Destroyer (i. e. Destroying Angel) or ‘place of destruction’
words.s: Ἀβαδδών (Hebr.), Destroyer (i. e. Destroying Angel) or ‘place of destruction’ (personified).

words.g: unburdensome, bringing no weight or oppression upon
words.s: ἀβαρής, unburdensome, bringing no weight or oppression upon.

words.g: Abiathar, a priest in King David's time
words.s: Ἀβιάθαρ (Hebr.), Abiathar, a priest in King David's time.

words.g: I work that which is good, I perform good deeds
words.s: ἀγαθοεργέω (ἀγαθουργέω), I work that which is good, I perform good deeds.

words.g: the doing of that which is good
words.s: ἀγαθοποιία, the doing of that which is good.

words.g: a doer of that which is good
words.s: ἀγαθοποιός (adj. as noun), a doer of that which is good (ἀγαθοποιῶν gen. pl. masc., 1 Pet. ii 14) (opp. κακοποιός).

words.g: contracted form of ἀγαθοεργέω, which see
words.s: ἀγαθουργέω (contracted form of ἀγαθοεργέω, which see).
ἀγανάκτησις, feeling of anger, vexation.
ἀγγεῖον, a vessel, flask, can.
ἀγγέλλω, I report, I announce (as messenger).
ἄγγος, a vessel.

words.g: unprovided with a genealogy, whose descent cannot be traced
words.s: ἀγενεαλόγητος, unprovided with a genealogy, whose descent cannot be traced.
ἀγενής, literally, without γένος (family); hence ignoble.

words.g: an arm, especially as bent to receive a burden
words.s: ἀγκάλη, an arm, especially as bent to receive a burden.
ἄγκιστρον, a fish-hook.
ἁγνισμός, (ceremonial) purification.
ἀγνόημα, an offence committed through ignorance, an error due to (wilful or culpable) ignorance.
ἁγνῶς, purely, with pure motives, honestly.
ἄγνωστος, unknown, unknowable.
ἀγράμματος, unlettered, illiterate, uneducated, perhaps with the narrower idea, unacquainted with Rabbinic teaching.

words.g: I spend the night in the open, bivouac
words.s: ἀγραυλέω, I spend the night in the open, bivouac.
ἀγρεύω, I catch, capture.
ἀγωγή, leading; hence, mode of life, conduct.
ἀγωνία (properly the feeling of the athlete before a contest), great fear, terror, of death; anxiety.

words.g: without expense, for which nothing has to be paid
words.s: ἀδάπανος, without expense, for which nothing has to be paid.

words.g: Addei, son of Cosam, and father of Melchei
words.s: Ἀδδεί (Hebr.), Addei, son of Cosam, and father of Melchei, one of the ancestors of Jesus (Lk. iii 28).

words.g: the quality of being unseen (of disappearing)
words.s: ἀδηλότης, the quality of being unseen (of disappearing), indefiniteness, uncertainty.
ἀδήλως, out of sight, obscurely, inconspicuously; in 1 Cor. ix 26 perhaps=uncertainly, without certain aim.

words.g: without dividings of mind, undivided, whole-hearted
words.s: ἀδιάκριτος, without dividings of mind, undivided, whole-hearted.
ἀδίκως, unjustly.

words.g: Admein, son of Arnei, father of Naasson
words.s: Ἀδμείν (Hebr.), Admein, son of Arnei, father of Naasson, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
ἄδολος, unadulterated, pure.

words.g: belonging to Adramyttium, a port in Mysia, NW. Asia Minor
words.s: Ἁδραμυντηνός (Ἀδραμυττηνός), belonging to Adramyttium, a port in Mysia, NW. Asia Minor.

Ἁδρίας, the Hadria, a name given by sailors not merely to the Adriatic Sea, to which it properly belonged, but also to the open Mediterranean to the south-east of Italy, to the sea that lay between Malta, Italy, Greece, and Crete.
ἁδρότης, lavishness, lavish generosity.

words.g: Azotus, Ashdod, a coast town of Palestine
words.s: Ἄζωτος, Azotus, Ashdod, a coast town of Palestine belonging to the ancient Philistia, and part of Herod's kingdom.

words.g: without god, without (the only true) god, godless
words.s: ἄθεος, without god, without (the only true) god, godless.

words.g: a struggling (as in an athletic contest)
words.s: ἄθλησις, a struggling (as in an athletic contest).
ἀθροίζω, I gather together, collect.
ἀθυμέω, I lose heart, am despondent.
αἴγειος, of a goat.
αἰδώς (apparently absent from papyri), shame, modesty.

words.g: a shedding or pouring forth of blood (in sacrifice)
words.s: αἱματεκχυσία, a shedding or pouring forth of blood (in sacrifice).

words.g: I suffer from a continual flow (oozing) of blood
words.s: αἱμορροέω, I suffer from a continual flow (oozing) of blood.
αἴνεσις, praise, commendation.
αἴνιγμα, a riddle.
Αἰνών, Aenon. Eusebius and Jerome place this site 8 (Roman) miles south of Scythopolis near the Jordan.
αἱρετίζω, I choose.

words.g: disposed to form sects, sectarian, factious
words.s: αἱρετικός, disposed to form sects, sectarian, factious.
αἰσθάνομαι, I perceive.
αἴσθησις, perception.
αἰσθητήριον, perceptive faculty.

words.g: in a spirit of eagerness for base gain
words.s: αἰσχροκερδῶς, in a spirit of eagerness for base gain.
αἰσχρολογία, filthy speech, foulmouthedness.
αἰσχρότης, baseness.
αἴτιον (neut. of adj. αἴτιος), cause shading into crime; guilt, criminality.
αἰτίωμα, a charge, accusation.
αἰχμαλωτεύω, I take captive (in war).
αἰχμάλωτος, a captive (in war), hence generally.

words.g: I am without a suitable opportunity (to effect something)
words.s: ἀκαιρέομαι, I am without a suitable opportunity (to effect something).

words.g: unseasonably, out of due season, inopportunely
words.s: ἀκαίρως, unseasonably, out of due season, inopportunely.
ἀκατάγνωστος, uncondemned, unimpeachable.

words.g: indissoluble, that cannot be broken up
words.s: ἀκατάλυτος, indissoluble, that cannot be broken up.

words.g: not ceasing from, not abandoning (giving up)
words.s: ἀκατάπαυστος, not ceasing from, not abandoning (giving up), c. gen.
ἀκλινής, unbent, unyielding, resolute.
ἀκμάζω, I reach maturity, become ripe: I am in full vigour.
ἀκμήν, (properly adverbial acc. of ἀκμή [full time, maturity], and meaning just now) thus, Mt. xv 16 (where parallel in Mk. vii 18 has οὕτως).
ἀκρατής, (impotent, hence) lacking self-control, inclined to excess.
ἄκρᾱτος (from κεράννυμι), unmixed, undiluted.

words.g: accuracy, exactness, attention to detail, scrupulousness
words.s: ἀκρίβεια (diligentia), accuracy, exactness, attention to detail, scrupulousness.

words.g: careful, accurate, exact, strict, scrupulous, precise
words.s: ἀκριβής (diligens), careful, accurate, exact, strict, scrupulous, precise.
ἀκροατήριον, auditorium, recitation hall; court room (for hearing cases).
ἀκροθίνιον (lit. top of a heap), spoil, treasure (taken in war).
ἀκωλύτως (characteristic of legal documents), without let or hindrance.
ἄκων, unwilling, generally used where English would express by an adverb, unwillingly (cf. inuitus).
ἀλάλητος, unutterable, that baffles words.
ἀλεκτοροφωνία (galli cantus, gallicinium), cockcrow, as a period of time, between midnight and 3 a.m.
ἁλιεύω, I fish.
ἀλίσγημα (from ἀλισγέω, read in Freer MS. at Mk. ix 49), pollution, perhaps a polluted thing (specially of food).
ἀλλαχόθεν, from another quarter, practically by another way.
ἀλλαχοῦ (= ἄλλοσε, ἀλλαχόσε, elsewhither), elsewhere.

words.g: I allegorize, I interpret as an allegory
words.s: ἀλληγορέω, I allegorize, I interpret as an allegory.

words.g: a man of another race, a foreigner
words.s: ἀλλογενής, a man of another race, a foreigner.

words.g: a pryer into other men's affairs
words.s: ἀλλοτριοεπίσκοπος (a word of uncertain application, perhaps) a pryer into other men's affairs, by means of soothsayers, astrologers, &c.
ἀλλόφυλος, a foreigner.
ἄλλως, otherwise: τὰ ἄλλως ἔχοντα, things that are otherwise.

words.g: aloes, the powdered fragrant aloe wood
words.s: ἀλόη, aloes, the powdered fragrant aloe wood.
ἁλυκός, salty, saline.
ἄλυπος, free from pain (grief, trouble).
ἀλυσιτελής, profitless, unprofitable.
ἅλωσις, capture, capturing.
ἀμαθής (very rare in Hellenistic period), unlearned.
ἀμαράντινος, unfading, fadeless.
ἀμάραντος, unfading.
ἀμάρτυρος, unwitnessed, untestified to.
ἀμάω, I mow, reap.
ἀμέθυστος, amethyst (a kind of rock crystal: the best specimens are the colour of unmixed wine, whence perhaps the name).
ἀμετακίνητος, immovable.
ἀμετανόητος, unrepentant.

words.g: whose mother's name is not recorded (or known)
words.s: ἀμήτωρ (lit. motherless), whose mother's name is not recorded (or known).
ἀμοιβή, a change, an exchange; hence, plur. reciprocal good deeds (services), a fitting requital.
ἀμπελουργός (uinitor, vigneron), a vine-dresser.

words.g: Ampliatus, a male member of the church at Rome
words.s: Ἀμπλιᾶτος (pet form Ἀμπλίας), Ampliatus, a male member of the church at Rome, probably of the imperial household.

words.g: I attack in defence, I defend (by force)
words.s: ἀμύνομαι (very rare in the colloquial language), I attack in defence, I defend (by force).

words.g: I clothe, I put clothing (covering) on (over)
words.s: ἀμφιάζω (from ἀμφί, as ἀντιάζω is from ἀντί), I clothe, I put clothing (covering) on (over).

words.g: I cast (a fishing net), I fish
words.s: ἀμφιβάλλω, I cast (a fishing net), I fish.
ἀμφίβληστρον, a (casting) net.

words.g: Amphipolis, a leading city of Macedonia
words.s: Ἀμφίπολις, Amphipolis, a leading city of Macedonia.

words.g: a street, or rather a quarter or block
words.s: ἄμφοδον, a street, or rather a quarter or block (insula) of a city.
ἀμώμητος (a literary word), unblemished. (The Greek word properly means not to be blamed, but under the influence of Hebrew the other sense has come into prominence.)
ἄμωμον, spice, an odorous unguent derived from an Eastern plant with fruit like grapes, Rev. xviii 13.
ἀναβάλλομαι, I postpone, especially I postpone the trial of, with accus. of the person affected.

words.g: I cause to come up, bring up
words.s: ἀναβιβάζω, I cause to come up, bring up, regularly from sea to land.
ἀνάβλεψις, recovery of sight.

words.g: I shout upwards, cry out, raise my voice
words.s: ἀναβοάω, I shout upwards, cry out, raise my voice, Mt. xxvii 46 (text doubtful).
ἀναβολή, postponement, delay, putting off.

words.g: by way of compulsion, by force
words.s: ἀναγκαστῶς, by way of compulsion, by force.

words.g: I make known to again, I make to be recognized
words.s: ἀναγνωρίζω, I make known to again, I make to be recognized (text doubtful in Ac. vii 13).

words.g: the proclamation of an appointment (to an office)
words.s: ἀνάδειξις, the proclamation of an appointment (to an office); perhaps rather admission to membership of a society.

words.g: I send up, deliver, hand over
words.s: ἀναδίδωμι (reddo), I send up, deliver, hand over.
ἀναζώννυμι, I gird up, brace up (with a view to active exertion). A metaphor from the girding of the flowing tunic, to prevent its hampering one in active work.

words.g: I stir up the fire, fan the flame of
words.s: ἀναζωπυρέω, I stir up the fire, fan the flame of.
ἀναθάλλω, I cause to bloom again.
ἀναίδεια, shamelessness, shameless persistence (e.g. in greed).

words.g: taking away (of life), killing, slaying, murder
words.s: ἀναίρεσις, taking away (of life), killing, slaying, murder.

words.g: I make fresh again, I make fresh as at the first
words.s: ἀνακαινίζω, I make fresh again, I make fresh as at the first.
ἀνάκρισις, judicial examination, preliminary inquiry.
ἀνάλημψις, a taking up, lifting up (of the Ascension; lit. Assumption).
ἀναλογία, proportion, measure.
ἀναλογίζομαι (from λόγος = account), I reckon up, count over.
ἄναλος, saltless, tasteless, flat.
ἀνάλυσις, departing, departure (from this life). (Probably a metaphor from the yoking and unyoking of transport animals.)

words.g: I await (one whose coming is expected)
words.s: ἀναμένω, I await (one whose coming is expected).
ἀνανεόομαι (regularly a legal word), I am renewed.

words.g: I become sober again, I recover sound sense
words.s: ἀνανήφω, I become sober again, I recover sound sense.
ἀναντίρητος (ἀναντίρρητος), that cannot be gainsaid, undeniable.
ἀναντιρήτως (ἀναντιρρήτως), without saying anything against (the request), unquestioningly.
ἀνάξιος, unworthy.
ἀναξίως, unworthily, in an unworthy manner.

words.g: I urge by (evil) persuasion, I tempt
words.s: ἀναπείθω, I urge by (evil) persuasion, I tempt.
ἀναπηδάω, I leap up.
ἀναπτύσσω (euoluo), I unroll (reading uncertain).

words.g: uncountable, innumerable, that cannot be numbered
words.s: ἀναρίθμητος, uncountable, innumerable, that cannot be numbered.
ἀνασκευάζω, I pack up; hence, I carry away, or dismantle; hence, I upset, destroy, overthrow, subvert (lit. and metaph.).
ἀνασταυρόω, I crucify again (so the sense seems to require, but elsewhere simply = σταυρόω, I crucify).
ἀναστενάζω, I groan.
ἀνατάσσομαι, I arrange, draw up, but perhaps, as Blass thought, I set down from memory, I restore from memory, Lk. i 1.
ἀναφωνέω, I call out, shout.
ἀνάχυσις (probably literary), outpouring, excess.
ἀνάψυξις (refrigerium), refreshing, refreshment.
ἀναψύχω, I refresh, revive, comfort.

words.g: an enslaver, one who forcibly enslaves, a kidnapper
words.s: ἀνδραποδιστής, an enslaver, one who forcibly enslaves, a kidnapper.

words.g: I act in manly fashion, I play the man
words.s: ἀνδρίζομαι, I act in manly fashion, I play the man, I display manly qualities.

words.g: Andronicus, a member of the Roman church
words.s: Ἀνδρόνικος, Andronicus, a member of the Roman church, probably husband of Junia, and a kinsman or fellow-tribesman of St. Paul.
ἀνδροφόνος, a murderer.

words.g: indescribable, that cannot be thoroughly related
words.s: ἀνεκδιήγητος, indescribable, that cannot be thoroughly related.
ἀνεκλάλητος, incapable of expression in speech.
ἀνέκλειπτος (ἀνέγλειπτος), unfailing.
ἀνελεήμων, unpitying, unmerciful.
ἀνέλεος, unmerciful.

words.g: I am blown with the wind
words.s: ἀνεμίζομαι, I am blown with the wind (referring to the gentler motions of the air).
ἀνένδεκτος, impossible.

words.g: that cannot be searched into, inscrutable
words.s: ἀνεξεραύνητος, that cannot be searched into, inscrutable.
ἀνεξίκακος, enduring evil, patient of evil.
ἀνεπαίσχυντος, not ashamed (of his work).
ἀνεύθετος, unfitted, unsuitable.
ἀνεψιός, (male) cousin, whether on the father's or on the mother's side.
ἄνηθον, dill (anethum graveolens).
ἀνήμερος, ungentle; untamed.

ἀνθομολογέομαι, I confess (so e.g. the Latin and Sahidic versions), acknowledge, formally admit: I give thanks (so e.g. the Peshitta Syriac and the Bohairic versions, and moderns generally). (The senses I agree, I answer to (come up to), I come to an understanding with, appear in papyri.)
ἄνθραξ, a coal.

words.g: Anna, a prophetess, who visited the infant Jesus
words.s: Ἄννα (the aspirated form Ἅννα, favoured by W-H, is contradicted by the evidence of the versions), Anna, a prophetess, who visited the infant Jesus.
ἄνοιξις, opening (abstr.).
ἀνταγωνίζομαι, I struggle against.

words.g: I fill up in place of some one else
words.s: ἀνταναπληρόω, I fill up in place of some one else.
ἀνταπόδοσις, orig. abstr., giving in return, but in Col. iii 24 practically = ἀνταπόδομα.

words.g: I throw at in opposition (or quasi-opposition)
words.s: ἀντιβάλλω, I throw at in opposition (or quasi-opposition), I exchange (words) with; perhaps, I compare.

words.g: I am adversely affected against, I oppose
words.s: ἀντιδιατίθεμαι, I am adversely affected against, I oppose.
ἀντίθεσις, a proposition, tenet, opinion advanced by one party against another.
ἀντικαθίστημι: 2 aor. I stoutly resisted.
ἀντικαλέω, I invite in return.
ἄντικρυς, right opposite, off (nautical sense).

words.g: a lending a hand to, a helping
words.s: ἀντίλημψις, a lending a hand to, a helping (cf. ἀντιλαμβάνομαι, both being often used in petitions).

words.g: I abuse in return, I give abuse for abuse
words.s: ἀντιλοιδορέω, I abuse in return, I give abuse for abuse.
ἀντίλυτρον, a stronger form of λύτρον, a ransom.

words.g: I measure in return, I give equivalent measure
words.s: ἀντιμετρέω, I measure in return, I give equivalent measure, Lk. vi 38 (text doubtful).

words.g: an Antiochian, an inhabitant of (Syrian) Antioch
words.s: Ἀντιοχεύς, an Antiochian, an inhabitant of (Syrian) Antioch.

words.g: Antipas, a Christian martyr of Pergamum
words.s: Ἀντίπας (Ἀντείπας, Ἀντίφας, a pet form of Ἀντίπατρος), Antipas, a Christian martyr of Pergamum.
Ἀντιπατρίς, Antipatris, a town, where was a Roman colony, on the road between Caesarea and Jerusalem.
ἀντίπερα, opposite.
ἀντιπίπτω, I fall foul of; I resist, oppose.
ἀντιστρατεύομαι, I campaign against, war against.

words.g: a pail attached to a rope
words.s: ἄντλημα, a pail attached to a rope, by which it is let down into a well.
ἀντοφθαλμέω, I face (lit. ‘I present my eye to’); I resist.
ἀνωτερικός, upper, higher-lying (the high central plateau of Asia Minor in contrast to the road through the valley).

words.g: higher, to a more honourable place
words.s: ἀνώτερον (compar. of ἄνω, q. v.), (a) higher, to a more honourable place (at the dinner-table), Lk. xiv 10; (b) (superius) previously, in an earlier passage (of the book), above.
ἀπάγχομαι, I choke, strangle, hang myself.
ἀπαίδευτος, untrained, uneducated, showing a want of training or education.

words.g: I am past feeling, cease to care
words.s: ἀπαλγέω (lit. I cease to feel [my] pain), I am past feeling, cease to care (suggesting sometimes despair, sometimes recklessness), I become callous.
ἀπαράβατος, inviolate, inviolable.
ἀπαρασκεύαστος, unprepared.
ἀπαρτισμός, setting up, erection; hence completion.
ἀπάτωρ, without (recorded) father, of unknown father.

words.g: a light flashing forth (from), radiation, gleam
words.s: ἀπαύγασμα, a light flashing forth (from), radiation, gleam.
ἀπεῖπον: in middle, ἀπειπάμην, I have renounced.
ἀπείραστος, untried, inexperienced (c. gen. = in); or untempted (c. gen. = to).
ἄπειρος (from πεῖρα), inexperienced (in), without experience (of), unacquainted (with).

words.g: a putting off (as of a garment), a casting off
words.s: ἀπέκδυσις (probably coined by Paul), a putting off (as of a garment), a casting off.
ἀπελαύνω, I drive away.
ἀπελεγμός, refutation, rejection; hence disrepute.
ἀπελεύθερος, a freedman, one who has been a slave but has been manumitted by his master.
Ἀπελλῆς, Apelles, a Christian (man) in Rome.
ἀπελπίζω (ἀφελπίζω), I despair: in Lk. vi 35, if μηδέν be the correct reading, μηδὲν ἀφελπίζοντες must be translated, despairing not at all, if μηδένα ἀφ., despairing of no one.
ἀπέραντος, unaccomplished, unending, endless.
ἀπερισπάστως, without distraction, without being distracted.
ἀπερίτμητος, uncircumcised; hence practically unclean; met. used of rankness, want of restraint.
ἁπλῶς, singly, simply: in James i 5 either graciously or unreservedly, without reserve.

words.g: I look away from one thing to another
words.s: ἀποβλέπω, I look away from one thing to another, I turn my attention to.

words.g: worthy to be cast away, worthless
words.s: ἀπόβλητος, worthy to be cast away, worthless.
ἀπογίνομαι (denascor) (opposite of γίνομαι: therefore, I go out of being, I cease to be), with the dat., I die away from.
ἀπόδειξις, display, exhibition (abstr.); the ordinary sense is proof.
ἀπόδημος (see ἀποδημέω), away from home.
ἀποδιορίζω (I make a [logical] distinction), I make an (invidious) distinction.
ἀποθησαυρίζω, I store up, treasure up.
ἀποθλίβω (lit. I rub), I jostle.
ἀποκατάστασις, re-establishment, restoration.
ἀποκλείω, I shut.
ἀπόκριμα (rescriptum), an answer (of God to the apostle's appeal, preserved in his heart).
Ἀπολλύων (properly pres. pcpl. of ἀπολλύω, cf. ἀπόλλυμι), The Destroying One, a Greek translation of the Hebr. Abaddon.
Ἀπολλωνία, Apollonia, a city of Macedonia.

words.g: I wipe off myself (on to another)
words.s: ἀμομάσσομαι, I wipe off myself (on to another).
ἀπονέμω, I apportion, render (as due).
ἀπονίπτω, I wash dirt off.

words.g: I fall away (from), I fall off
words.s: ἀποπίπτω, I fall away (from), I fall off.
ἀπορία, state of difficulty, distress.

words.g: I throw away from, I throw overboard
words.s: ἀπορίπτω, I throw away from, I throw overboard.
ἀπορφανίζω, I separate from some one.

words.g: a shadow cast by an object
words.s: ἀποσκίασμα, either a shadow cast by an object, or a faint image or copy of an object.

words.g: I unroof, take the roof off
words.s: ἀποστεγάζω, I unroof, take the roof off.
ἀποστοματίζω (literary, from ἀπὸ στόματος), I draw out by questioning.
ἀποστυγέω, I shrink from (with horror).

words.g: I repay, pay what is due
words.s: ἀποτίνω, I repay, pay what is due (by way of punishment or fine).
ἀποτολμάω (literary), I break out boldly.
ἀποτρέπομαι, I turn myself away from.
ἀπουσία, absence.
ἀποφορτίζομαι, I discharge my cargo.
ἀπόχρησις, using up.
ἀποψύχω, I faint or I die.
Ἄππιος, Appius (censor 312 B. C.), after whom the township Appi Forum on the Appian Way, 43 Roman miles from Rome, was named.
ἀπρόσιτος, unapproachable.

words.g: without any preference (undue favour, partiality) for a person
words.s: ἀπροσωπολήμπτως (literary and Jewish), without any preference (undue favour, partiality) for a person.
ἄπταιστος (literary and rare), not stumbling.

words.g: Apphia, a Christian lady of Colossae
words.s: Ἀπφία, Ἀφφία, Apphia, a Christian lady of Colossae, either wife or sister of Philemon.
ἀρά, cursing, a curse.
ἄραφος, without seam.
Ἄραψ, an Arabian.
ἀργέω, I am idle (unemployed, without occupation) (generally, outside N.T., of necessity, and not blameworthily).
ἀργυροκόπος (silver-cutter, literally), a silversmith.

words.g: member of the Council of the Areopagus, an Areopagite
words.s: Ἀρεοπαγίτης, member of the Council of the Areopagus, an Areopagite.
ἀρέσκεια, pleasing, willing service.

words.g: Aretas, Aretas IV, King of the Nabataeans
words.s: Ἀρέτας (Ἁρέτας, for Ἁρέθας, Arabic Ḥāriṯā), Aretas, Aretas IV, King of the Nabataeans.
(ἀρήν), a lamb: acc. pl. ἄρνας (Lk. x 3); the nom. (= ϝαρήν) is found only in early times, and its place is taken by ἀρνίον.
Ἀριστόβουλος, Aristobulus, a Christian in Rome.
ἄρκος (a later form of ἄρκτος), a bear.
ἁρμόζομαι, I fit, join (the middle indicating deep personal interest).
ἁρμός, a joint of the body.
ἄροτρον, a plough.

words.g: snatching, robbery, the action of plundering
words.s: ἁρπαγμός, either (a) snatching, robbery, the action of plundering, rapacity, self-aggrandizement, or (b) a thing to be snatched, plunder, prey, booty, a prize, spoil.
ἄρρητος, not to be uttered (because too sacred), secret.
Ἀρτεμᾶς (a pet form of Ἀρτεμίδωρος), Artemas, a Christian in Rome.

words.g: a foresail, set on the bow
words.s: ἀρτέμων, a foresail, set on the bow.
ἀρτιγέννητος, newly begotten, newly born.
ἄρτιος, perfect.

words.g: Arphaxad, son of Shem, and father of Cainam
words.s: Ἀρφαξάδ (Hebr.), Arphaxad, son of Shem, and father of Cainam.

words.g: Archelaus, Herod Archelaus, son and successor of Herod I
words.s: Ἀρχέλαος, Archelaus, Herod Archelaus, son and successor of Herod I, reigned over Judaea from 4 B.C. to A.D. 6 and died before A.D. 18.

words.g: high priestly, to which the chief priest belongs
words.s: ἀρχιερατικός, high priestly, to which the chief priest belongs.
ἀρχιποίμην, chief shepherd.
ἀρχιτέκτων, master-builder.

words.g: head of a custom-house, chief tax gatherer
words.s: ἀρχιτελώνης, head of a custom-house, chief tax gatherer.
ἀσεβέω, (a) intr. I am impious, irreverent; (b) tr. I do impiously.
ἄσημος (lit. unmarked, unstamped), undistinguished, obscure.
ἀσθένημα, weakness.

words.g: belonging to the Roman province Asia
words.s: Ἀσιανός, belonging to the Roman province Asia.

words.g: Asiarch, an official connected with the worship of Rome
words.s: Ἀσιάρχης, Asiarch, an official connected with the worship of Rome and the Emperor in the Roman province Asia.

words.g: lack of corn, lack of food
words.s: ἀσιτία, either lack of corn, lack of food (the lit. meaning), or abstinence from food, loss of appetite, sea-sickness (the extended meaning).
ἄσιτος, either without corn, without food, or sea-sick.
ἀσκέω, I train, practise, exercise.
ἀσμένως, joyfully, with delight.
ἄσοφος, unskilled, unwise, foolish.
ἀσπίς, an asp (hooded-snake, cobra da capello).
ἄσπονδος, untrue to one's promise.
ἆσσον (compar. of ἄγχι adv.), nearer.

words.g: I am unsettled, have no place of abode
words.s: ἀστατέω, I am unsettled, have no place of abode, lead a vagabond life.
ἀσύμφωνος, inharmonious, disagreeing.

words.g: not covenanting, untrue to an agreement, treacherous
words.s: ἀσύνθετος, not covenanting, untrue to an agreement, treacherous.
Ἀσύνκριτος, Asyncritus, a Christian in Rome.
ἀσχήμων, unseemly, indecent.
ἀσώτως, prodigally: ζῶν ἀσώτως, with prodigal living (Field).

words.g: I am disorderly, I neglect my duty
words.s: ἀτακτέω (lit. I march out of order; then I riot, I rebel), I am disorderly, I neglect my duty, I am careless (or idle) in habits.
ἄτακτος (lit. out of order), disorderly, slack (in performance of duty).

words.g: an indivisible part of time, a second
words.s: ἄτομος (lit. that cannot be cut), an indivisible part of time, a second.

words.g: Attalia, the port of Perga in Pamphylia
words.s: Ἀττάλεια, Attalia, the port of Perga in Pamphylia.

words.g: I flash, gleam, appear white, bright
words.s: αὐγάζω, I flash, gleam, appear white, bright (as in LXX), but perhaps, I see, I see clearly (as in classical poetry).
αὐγή, light (of day).

words.g: Augustus, a title conferred on the first Roman Emperor
words.s: Αὔγουστος, Augustus, a title conferred on the first Roman Emperor, C. Iulius Octauianus, denoting sanctity (almost divinity); grecized as Σεβαστός (q. v.).
αὐθεντέω (a colloquial word, from αὐθέντης, ‘master’, ‘autocrat’ [= αὐτός + root sen, ‘accomplish’, in ἁνύω]), I domineer over.
αὐλός, a flute.
αὐτάρκης, self-sufficient, independent, contented (a literary use).
αὐτοκατάκριτος (perhaps a new coinage), self-condemned.
αὐτόπτης, eye-witness.
αὐτόχειρ (probably exclusively literary), with one's own hand.

words.g: I speak with proud confidence of, I boast of
words.s: αὐχέω (mostly in poetry), I speak with proud confidence of, I boast of.
αὐχμηρός (poetical, lit. dry and parched; then squalid and rough), dingy, dusky, obscure, dark, funereal.
ἀφανής, invisible.
ἀφανισμός, disappearing, disappearance.
ἄφαντος (originally poetical), disappearing, invisible, hidden.
ἀφειδία (lit. unsparingness), severe treatment.
ἀφελότης, simplicity.

words.g: incorruptness, incorruption, purity, freedom from taint
words.s: ἀφθορία, (moral) incorruptness, incorruption, purity, freedom from taint.
ἀφικνέομαι (in ordinary use very rare at this time), I arrive, reach.

words.g: not loving that which is good
words.s: ἀφιλάγαθος, not loving that which is good.

ἄφιξις, departure. (This is the sense required by Ac. xx 29, but as the word comes from ἀφικνέομαι, it ought to mean arrival. No certain parallel (except Josephus, Antiq. ii 18 fin., where = departure or journey) for this change of sense has been found.)
ἀφομοιόω, I make like to.
ἀφρός, foam (at the mouth).
ἀφυπνόω (very rare), I fall asleep.
ἀφυστερέω, I withdraw, take away.
Ἀχαϊκός, Achaicus, a Corinthian Christian.
ἀχλύς, mist.
ἀχρεόομαι (earlier ἀχρειόομαι) (lit. I become sour, I turn, of milk), I am good for nothing.
ἄχρηστος, unprofitable, useless (a play upon words, with ὀνήσιμος).
ἀψευδής, not guilty of falsehood, truthful.
ἄψινθος, wormwood; ὁ Ἄψινθος, a star.
ἄψυχος, lifeless.

words.g: Baal, a god worshipped by the Hebrews
words.s: Βάαλ (Bahal, properly Lord, and so not a proper name), Baal, a god worshipped by the Hebrews (in Rom. xi 4 fem., because Jews in reading substituted αἰσχύνη), being the highest god of all the West-Semitic peoples.
βαθμός, a step (of a stairway); hence, a stage in a career, a position.
βαθύνω, I deepen.
βαΐον, a palm branch.

words.g: Balac, Balak, son of Zippor, King of Moab
words.s: Βαλάκ (Hebr.), Balac, Balak, son of Zippor, King of Moab.

words.g: Barak, one of the Judges of Israel
words.s: Βαράκ (Hebr.), Barak, one of the Judges of Israel.
Βαραχίας (Hebr.), Barachias, Baruch. His identity is uncertain, perhaps father of the Zacharias killed by the Zealots in the last Jewish War (Josephus, B.J. iv 5. 4). See Ζαχαρίας.
Βαριησοῦς (Aram.), Bar-Jesus (i.e. son of Jesus), the name of the magician and false prophet at Paphos in Cyprus. He is also called Elymas.
Βαριωνᾶς (Aram.), Bar-jonas, son of Jonas, the surname of Simon Peter.
Βαρτίμαιος (Aram.), Bartimaeus, son of (?) Timaeus.
βαρύτιμος, heavy in price, very expensive.
βασανιστής, a torturer.

βασίλειος, (a) in Lk. vii 25 either masc. courtiers, or neut. palaces; (b) the LXX intended βασίλειον as subst., a body of kings, in the passage quoted by 1 Pet. ii 9, but Peter clearly takes βασίλειον as adj., royal.
βάσις (properly, that on which something may rest), a foot.

words.g: I give the evil eye to, fascinate, bewitch, overpower
words.s: βασκαίνω, I give the evil eye to, fascinate, bewitch, overpower.
βάτραχος, a frog.

words.g: I chatter, am long-winded, utter empty words
words.s: βατταλογέω, I chatter, am long-winded, utter empty words.
βδελυκτός, abominable, detestable.

words.g: Beliar (spelt sometimes Belial, Beliab), a demon
words.s: Βελίαρ (originally a Hebrew word = uselessness, corruption), Beliar (spelt sometimes Belial, Beliab), a demon, among the Jews, and in fact a name for Satan.
βελόνη, a needle.
βέλος, a missile, dart.
βέλτιον (very rare in this period), an adverb, comparative in form, superlative in meaning, best.
Βεροιαῖος, belonging to Beroea, Beroean.

words.g: a beryl, a precious stone of various colours
words.s: βήρυλλος, a beryl, a precious stone of various colours, the best known being sea-green.
βίαιος, strong, violent.
βιαστής, a forceful, violent man.
βιβρώσκω, I eat.
βιόω, I live.
βίωσις, manner of life.
βλαβερός, injurious.

words.g: Blastus, chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa I
words.s: Βλάστος, Blastus, chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa I.
βλέμμα, look, the faculty of looking.
βλητέον (verbal adj. from βάλλω): sc. ἐστίν, one must put.
Βοανηργές, Boanerges, a doubtful name of doubtful origin and meaning: see my crit. note.
βοή, a shout.
βοηθός, helper.
βολή, a casting, throw: in acc. as measure of distance.

words.g: Boos or Boes (Boaz), son of Salmon (Sala) and Rahab
words.s: Βοός, Βοές (Hebr.), Boos or Boes (Boaz), son of Salmon (Sala) and Rahab, husband of Ruth, father of Iobed.
βόρβορος, a miry dungeon. hole.
Βοσόρ, Bosor, father of Balaam: but see Βεώρ.
βοτάνη, fodder, food.
βότρυς, cluster (bunch) of grapes.
βραβεύω, I decide (in a conflict between contending forces); hence, I rule, I administer.
βραδυπλοέω, I sail slowly.
βραδυτής, tardiness, dilatoriness.
βρόχος, a noose.
βρύχω, I gnash, crunch.

words.g: I cause to gush forth, send forth
words.s: βρύω, I cause to gush forth, send forth.
βρώσιμος, eatable, suitable for food.
βυθός, the deep sea.
βύσσος (Semitic origin), fine-linen. (Some authorities consider cotton to be meant; others silk.)
βωμός, an altar.

Γαββαθά, Gabbatha, i.e. Gab Baitha, ‘the ridge (back) of the House’, i.e. the Aramaic name for what the Greeks called Λιθόστρωτον, a sort of paved square, on which the procurator had his judgement seat.
γάγγραινα, a cancerous sore, a cancer.

words.g: Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel
words.s: Γάδ (Hebr.), Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
Γαδαρηνός, Gadarene, belonging to Gadara (an important Hellenized town, one of the Decapolis, and SE. of the Sea of Galilee), see Γερασηνός, Γεργεσηνός.
γάζα (a Persian loan-word), treasure.
Γαλάτης, a Galatian (meaning any inhabitant of the Roman province Galatia).
γαμίσκομαι, I am given in marriage (reading doubtful).

words.g: Gideon, one of the Judges of Israel
words.s: Γεδεών (Hebr.), Gideon, one of the Judges of Israel.
γέλως, laughter.

words.g: I am put into a genealogy
words.s: γενεαλογέομαι, I am put into a genealogy.
γενετή, birth.

words.g: the assembly or body of elders
words.s: γερουσία, the assembly or body of elders, probably as synonymous with or explicative of συνέδριον and πρεσβύτεροι. (The term γερουσία was often used in such a collective sense in the cities of Asia Minor, cf. Ramsay, Cities and Bishoprics of Phrygia, vol. i, p. 64.)
γέρων, an old man.

words.g: I work the soil, I cultivate the soil
words.s: γεωργέω, I work the soil, I cultivate the soil.
γεώργιον, a cultivated field.
γῆρας, old age.
γλεῦκος, sweet wine, made perhaps from a small specially sweet grape.
γναφεύς, fuller.
γνησίως, truly, genuinely; honourably.
γνόφος, darkness.
γνώστης, a knower, expert.
γογγυστής, murmurer, grumbler.
γόης, a conjuror, juggler, sorcerer; a tricky (crafty) deceiver, impostor.
γραπτός, written.

words.g: belonging to old women, such as old women tell
words.s: γραώδης (anilis), belonging to old women, such as old women tell.
γυμνασία (physical) exercise, in a wide sense, ‘escarum, balnearum, uenationum et huius modi’ (Pelagius).
γυμνιτεύω, I am habitually γυμνός, that is, I wear the under-garment (χιτών, tunica) only, it being the regular practice to wear two garments.

words.g: a woman with all a woman's weakness
words.s: γυναικάριον (muliercula), a woman with all a woman's weakness, a poor weak woman.
γυναικεῖος, belonging to woman, of woman.

words.g: Gog, a name borrowed from Ezekiel
words.s: Γώγ, Gog, a name borrowed from Ezekiel (xxxviii 2 ff., where = prince over Mesech and Thubal), to indicate a race or races to be led astray by Satan at the end of the thousand years.
δαιμονιώδης, demon-like, such as demons have.
δαίμων, an evil-spirit, a demon, much less common than the diminutive δαιμόνιον.
δάκνω, I bite; hence, I backbite, or harm seriously.
δακρύω, I shed tears, weep.
δακτύλιος, a finger-ring.
Δαλμανουθά, Dalmanutha: nothing is known of name or place, and text is probably corrupt (a conjecture of Burkitt in Amer. Journ. Theol. xv (1911) 174).

words.g: Dalmatia, a province of the Roman Empire
words.s: Δαλματία, Dalmatia, a province of the Roman Empire, E. of the Adriatic, a later name for part of what was earlier called Illyricum (Rom. xv 19).
δάμαλις, a heifer.
Δάμαρις, Damaris, an Athenian woman.

words.g: a Damascene, an inhabitant of Damascus
words.s: Δαμασκηνός, a Damascene, an inhabitant of Damascus.
δάνειον (δάνιον), a loan.
Δανιήλ (Hebr.), Daniel, loosely called a ‘prophet’.
δανιστής, a lender, creditor.
δαπάνη, cost, expense.
δεῖγμα, an example, type.
δειλία, cowardice.
δειλιάω, I shrink, am fearful.

words.g: so and so, such an one
words.s: δεῖνα: ὁ δεῖνα, so and so, such an one, where the name of the person is known but not used.
δεισιδαιμονία, superstition.

words.g: respectful of what is divine, religious perhaps
words.s: δεισιδαίμων, respectful of what is divine, religious perhaps, rather than superstitious (the usual meaning).

words.g: a word of uncertain meaning, indicating some class of soldier
words.s: δεξιολάβος, a word of uncertain meaning, indicating some class of soldier (cf. Nestle in Archiv für lateinische Lexikographie, Bd. xii, 581-2).
Δερβαῖος, Derbean, belonging to Derbe.
δέρμα, a hide, skin.
δέσμη, a bond.

words.g: on the second day, on the next day
words.s: δευτεραῖος, adj. where Eng. requires adv., on the second day, on the next day.

words.g: I make a public speech, I address a multitude
words.s: δημηγορέω, I make a public speech, I address a multitude.
δημιουργός, a constructor, builder.
δήπου (δή που), of course, qualifying and yet strengthening the assertion.
διαβάλλω, I slander: merely I complain of (without idea of malice), Lk. xvi 1.
διάγνωσις (cognitio), investigation and decision.

words.g: I awake out of sleep, I am thoroughly awake
words.s: διαγρηγορέω, I awake out of sleep, I am thoroughly awake.
διαδέχομαι, I receive in my turn.
διάδοχος, a successor.
διακαθαίρω, I clean thoroughly.
διακαθαρίζω, I clean thoroughly.
διακατελέγχομαι, I effectively (utterly) refute (confute).
διακούω, I hear throughout, of a judicial hearing.
διακωλύω, I obstinately prevent.

words.g: I cease, give over, give up
words.s: διαλείπω, I cease, give over, give up.

words.g: I become reconciled to, I reconcile myself with
words.s: διαλλάσσομαι, I become reconciled to, I reconcile myself with.
διαλύω, I break up, disperse.
διαμάχομαι, I strive greatly.
διαμερισμός, breaking up; discord, hostility.
διανέμω, I divide into portions, distribute; I spread abroad.
διανεύω, I nod continually.
διανόημα, a reasoning, thought, cogitation.
διανυκτερεύω, I spend the whole night.
διανύω, I finish, complete.
διαπαρατριβή, perpetual wrangling.
διαπλέω, I sail over (across).
διαπραγματεύομαι, I gain by business (trading).
διασείω (concutio), I blackmail, extort from.
διάστημα, an interval.
διάταγμα, a commandment.
διαταράσσω, I disturb greatly.
διατελέω (act. and) mid. I continue.
διατροφή, nourishment, food.

words.g: I dawn (of the light coming through the shadows)
words.s: διαυγάζω, I dawn (of the light coming through the shadows).
διαυγής, through which light passes, transparent.
διαφεύγω, I flee through, I escape.
διαφυλάσσω, I guard securely, I preserve, or guard through (a danger), save.
διαχλευάζω, I mock (scorn) greatly, with words and gesture.

words.g: I separate myself from, I part from
words.s: διαχωρίζομαι, I separate myself from, I part from.

words.g: I weigh in my mind, ponder
words.s: διενθυμέομαι, I weigh in my mind, ponder.

words.g: a going out in various directions, a parting
words.s: διέξοδος, a going out in various directions, a parting; hence, the issue of a street, where it leads out of the city into the country.
διερμηνευτής, an interpreter.
διερωτάω, I inquire for.
διετής (bimus), two years old.
διήγησις, a narrative.

words.g: between two seas, which has sea on both sides
words.s: διθάλασσος, between two seas, which has sea on both sides.
διικνέομαι, I pass through (to), come through (to).
δικαιοκρισία, just judging, just judgement.
δίλογος, double-tongued.
Διονύσιος, Dionysius, an Athenian.
διόρθωμα, a correction, reform.
διόρθωσις, amendment, improvement (originally right ordering; then bettering).

words.g: the Dioscuri, Castor and Pollux, sons of Zeus and Leda
words.s: Διόσκουροι (= Διὸς κοῦροι, boys of Zeus), the Dioscuri, Castor and Pollux, sons of Zeus and Leda, and patrons of sailors.
Διοτρέφης, Diotrephes.
διπλόω, I double.
δισχίλιοι, two-thousand.

words.g: I strain, put through a sieve
words.s: διυλίζω, I strain, put through a sieve.

words.g: I make to differ from, I make to be hostile
words.s: διχάζω, I make to differ from, I make to be hostile.
δίψος, thirst.
διώκτης, a persecutor.

words.g: I subject myself to regulations, or I am decree-ridden
words.s: δογματίζομαι, I subject myself to regulations, or I am decree-ridden.
δοκιμασία, testing, proving.
δόλιος, treacherous, deceitful.
δολιόω, I act deceitfully, treacherously.
δολόω, I adulterate (cf. ἄδολος).
δότης, giver.
δουλαγωγέω, I enslave.
δράσσομαι, I take hold of, grasp.

words.g: Drusilla (born A.D. 39), daughter of Herod Agrippa I
words.s: Δρούσιλλα, Drusilla (born A.D. 39), daughter of Herod Agrippa I and his cousin Kypros, wife, first of Azizos, King of Emesa, and then of Antonius Felix, procurator of Judaea.
δυσβάστακτος, difficult to carry.
δυσεντέριον, dysentery.
δυσερμήνευτος, difficult to interpret.
δύσκολος, difficult.
δυσνόητος, hard to understand.

words.g: I am badly spoken of, I have a bad reputation
words.s: δυσφημέω, I am badly spoken of, I have a bad reputation.
δυσφημία, evil repute.
δωδέκατος, twelfth.
δωδεκάφυλον, the Twelve Tribes (of Israel).
ἔα, an interjection, ho! It is supposed to imply surprise, fear and indignation.
ἑβδομηκοντάκις, seventy times.

words.g: Eber, father of Phalek and son of Sala
words.s: Ἔβερ (Hebr.), Eber, father of Phalek and son of Sala.
ἔγγυος, a surety, security.
ἔγερσις, a waking up.
ἐγκομβόομαι, I clothe myself (originally, I tie round in a knot).
ἐγκρατής, self-controlled.
ἐγκρύπτω, I hide (within).
ἐγχρίω, I besmear, anoint.
ἐδαφίζω, I dash to the ground.
ἔδαφος, ground.
ἑδραίωμα, a foundation.

words.g: service (worship) of the will, worship of self
words.s: ἐθελοθρησκεία (cf. ἐθελοδουλεία), service (worship) of the will, worship of self, practically; worship of the angels.
ἐθίζω, I accustom: τὸ εἰθισμένον, the custom.

words.g: ethnarch, tribal lord, a subordinate ruler
words.s: ἐθνάρχης, ethnarch, tribal lord, a subordinate ruler.
ἐθνικῶς, in the manner of Gentiles.
εἰδωλεῖον, a temple for (containing) an image (of a god).
εἴκω, I yield.
εἰρηνοποιέω, I make peace.
εἰρηνοποιός, peace-making, peace-maker.
εἰσδέχομαι, I welcome in.
εἰσκαλέω, mid. I call in (to my house).
εἰσπηδάω, I leap into, rush into.
εἰστρέχω, I run in(to).
ἑκάστοτε, on each occasion.
ἑκατονταετής, a hundred years old.

words.g: a throwing out, a jettisoning of cargo, to lighten a ship
words.s: ἐκβολή (iactura), a throwing out, a jettisoning of cargo, to lighten a ship.
ἔκγονος, descended, hence subst. a descendant.
ἐκδαπανάω, I spend (give out) completely.
ἔκδηλος, perfectly evident, manifest.
ἐκδιώκω, I drive out.
ἔκδοτος, given up, delivered up.
ἐκδοχή, waiting, expectation.
ἐκζήτησις, a seeking out, searching questioning.
ἔκθαμβος, full of astonishment.
ἐκθαυμάζω, I wonder greatly.
ἔκθετος, exposed (to the elements).
ἐκκαίομαι, I burn (with lust).
ἐκκολυμβάω, I swim out (of the water).
ἐκκομίζω (effero), I carry out (of the city gate for burial).

words.g: a block, check, obstacle; obstacle, check, hindrance
words.s: ἐκκοπή (ἐνκοπή), a block, check, obstacle. ἐνκοπή, ἐκκοπή, obstacle, check, hindrance.
ἐκκρέμαμαι (-ομαι), c. gen. I hang upon (met.).
ἐκλαλέω, I speak out, tell out.
ἐκλάμπω, I shine forth (out).
ἐκλανθάνομαι, I quite forget.
ἐκνεύω (lit. I bend the head aside, to avoid a blow), I retire, withdraw.
ἐκνήφω, I am thoroughly sober (in mind).
ἑκούσιος, willing: κατὰ ἑκούσιον, with right good will.
ἐκπερισσῶς, most exceedingly, with exceeding emphasis.
ἐκπετάννυμι, I spread (stretch) out.
ἐκπηδάω, I leap (rush) out.

words.g: I fill completely, I fulfil in every particular
words.s: ἐκπληρόω, I fill completely, I fulfil in every particular (to the utmost), I make good.
ἐκπλήρωσις, completion, fulfilment.
ἐκπορνεύω, I am guilty of fornication (the force of ἐκ is uncertain).
ἐκπτύω (cf. Fr. conspuer), I spit upon, disdain.
ἐκστρέφω, I pervert.
ἐκταράσσω, I disturb (trouble) greatly (exceedingly).
ἐκτένεια, earnestness, strenuousness.
ἐκτενής, intent, constant, strenuous.
ἔκτρωμα, (strictly a lifeless abortion) an untimely birth.
ἐκφοβέω, I terrify exceedingly.
ἐκχωρέω, I go out.
Ἐλαιών (oliuetum), Olive-grove, Olive-yard, probably the right text in Lk. xix 29, xxi 37, as well as Ac. i 12.
Ἐλαμείτης, an Elamite, one of a people living to the north of the Persian Gulf in the southern part of Persia.
ἐλαττονέω, I have less, I lack.
ἐλαφρία (leuitas), levity, fickleness.
ἐλεγμός, reproof.
ἔλεγξις, rebuke, reproof.
ἔλεγχος, a proof: possibly a persuasion.
ἔλευσις, coming, arrival.
ἐλεφάντινος, made of ivory.

words.g: Eliezer, son of Joreim and father of Joshua
words.s: Ἐλιέζερ (Hebr.), Eliezer, son of Joreim and father of Joshua.
Ἑλισαῖος, Helisaeus, grecized form of Elisha.
ἑλκόομαι, I am covered with sores.

words.g: Hellas, the native name for Greece
words.s: Ἑλλάς, Hellas, the native name for Greece.
Ἑλληνικός, Greek: ἡ Ἑλληνικὴ (γλῶσσα), the Greek language.

words.g: Elmadam, father of Kosam, son of Er
words.s: Ἐλμαδάμ (Hebr.), Elmadam, father of Kosam, son of Er.

words.g: Elymas, the name of the sorcerer at Paphos
words.s: Ἐλύμας, Elymas, the name of the sorcerer at Paphos (the form of the name is doubtful: some MSS read Ἑτοιμᾶς, Son of the Ready).
ἐμβάλλω, I cast in, throw in.

ἐμβατεύω, (I enter on, take possession of, hence) technical expression connected with the pagan Mysteries, I enter, set foot on (the inner shrine, after the first initiation). It indicates the final act in mystic ceremonial, the entrance on a new life in presence of the god.
ἐμβιβάζω, tr. I embark, put on board.
ἐμέω, I vomit.
ἐμμαίνομαι, I am madly enraged with.
Ἐμμανουήλ (Hebr.), Emmanuel, a Messianic title derived from Isa. vii 14 = God with us.

words.g: Emmaus (Ammaus), a village not far from Jerusalem
words.s: Ἐμμαούς, Emmaus (Ammaus), a village not far from Jerusalem.
Ἐμμώρ (Hebr.), Emmor, Hamor, a man whose sons sold a field at Shechem to Jacob.
ἐμπαιγμονή, mockery.
ἐμπαιγμός, mockery.
ἐμπλοκή, braiding.
ἐμπορία, trading, trade, trafficking, business.

words.g: a place of traffic, mart, market, market-house
words.s: ἐμπόριον, a place of traffic, mart, market, market-house.
ἐμφυσάω, I breathe into, breathe upon.
ἔμφυτος, inborn, ingrown, congenital, natural.
ἐνάλιος (rather a poetical word), of creatures, living in the sea.
ἐνδεής, in need, needy.
ἔνδειγμα, (a thing proved, hence) a plain token (sign, proof).
ἐνδέχομαι, ἐνδέχεται, impers., it is possible.
ἐνδύνω, I enter into.
ἔνδυσις, putting on (of a garment).
ἐνδώμησις, roofing, coping. (So probably, from δῶμα = roof, but most interpret building.)

words.g: I wrap up, roll up in (something)
words.s: ἐνειλέω, I wrap up, roll up in (something).
ἔνειμι, I am in (within): τὰ ἐνόντα, probably the contents (of the dish), or perhaps what you can, but the words are obscure and may be a mistranslation of an Aramaic original.
ἐνεός (= ἄνεως), speechless, dumb, unable to speak.
ἐνκάθετος, a snare-setter, spy.
ἐνκαίνια, festival of dedication of the Temple, to celebrate the re-dedication of the Temple by Judas Maccabeus in 164 B.C., held at Jerusalem about the middle of December.

words.g: I am settled among, dwell among
words.s: ἐνκατοικέω, I am settled among, dwell among.
ἐνκαυχάομαι, I boast in (because of) something.

words.g: I judge (reckon) to belong to, I class with
words.s: ἐνκρίνω, I judge (reckon) to belong to, I class with.
ἔνκυος, pregnant.

words.g: I make a sign to by nodding
words.s: ἐννεύω, I make a sign to by nodding.
ἔννυχα, in the night.
ἐνορκίζω (a strengthened ὁρκίζω), c. dupl. acc. I adjure some one by, I solemnly appeal to some one by.
ἐνπεριπατέω, I walk among.
ἐνπνέω (lit. I breathe in), I breathe of, breathe.

words.g: belonging to the place, native, resident
words.s: ἐντόπιος, belonging to the place, native, resident.
ἐντρέφω, I nourish (sustain) on.
ἐντρυφάω, I revel (in).
ἐντυπόω, I engrave.
ἐνυβρίζω, I insult, outrage.
ἐνύπνιον, a dream, vision.

words.g: Enos, son of Seth, and father of Cainam
words.s: Ἐνώς (Hebr.), Enos, son of Seth, and father of Cainam.

words.g: I take into my ear, give ear to
words.s: ἐνωτίζομαι (from ἐν and οὖς), I take into my ear, give ear to.
ἐξαίρω, I remove.
ἐξαιτέομαι, I beg earnestly for: aor. = I have procured to be given up to me (Field).
ἐξάλλομαι, I leap up (for joy).
ἐξανάστασις, rising up and out, resurrection.
ἐξάπινα, suddenly.
ἐξαστράπτω (corusco), I flash forth like lightning.
ἐξέλκω (lit. I draw out of the right place, or I draw aside out of the right way), I entice.
ἐξέραμα, vomit, purge.

words.g: I search diligently, I examine carefully (minutely)
words.s: ἐξεραυνάω, I search diligently, I examine carefully (minutely).
ἐξηχέω, I sound out (forth) (referring either to the clearness or to the loudness of the sound).
ἕξις, condition, state, especially good condition of body or soul.

words.g: I have strength for (a difficult task)
words.s: ἐξισχύω, I have strength for (a difficult task).
ἐξολεθρεύω, I destroy utterly, annihilate, exterminate.

words.g: I exorcize, cast out by appeal to a god
words.s: ἐξορκίζω, I exorcize, cast out by appeal to a god.

words.g: an exorcist, a caster out of evil spirits
words.s: ἐξορκιστής, an exorcist, a caster out of evil spirits by the use of names or spells.
ἐξουδενέω, another (inferior) spelling of ἐξουθενέω.
ἐξοχή, projection, prominence: οἱ κατ’ ἐξοχήν, the prominent persons, the chief men.
ἐξυπνίζω, I wake out of sleep.
ἔξυπνος, awake out of sleep.

words.g: I take part in a festival, keep a feast
words.s: ἑορτάζω, I take part in a festival, keep a feast (allegorically).
ἐπαγωνίζομαι, I contend for.

words.g: I crowd upon (some one), press around
words.s: ἐπαθροίζομαι, I crowd upon (some one), press around.
Ἐπαίνετος, Epaenetus, a Christian in Rome.
ἐπακούω, I listen to, hear.
ἐπακροάομαι, I listen to, hearken to.
ἐπάναγκες, adv. used as adj. necessary, inevitable, obligatory.

words.g: I remind, possibly I remind again
words.s: ἐπαναμιμνήσκω, I remind, possibly I remind again.
ἐπανόρθωσις, setting straight (right) again.
ἐπάρατος, accursed, cursed.
ἔπαυλις, a farm, estate.
ἐπαφρίζω, I foam out (a metaphor from the seaweed and refuse borne on the crest of waves).
ἐπειδήπερ, since.
ἐπεισαγωγή, bringing in, introduction, importation.
ἐπεισέρχομαι, I come (in) upon.
ἐπέκεινα, beyond.
ἐπεκτείνομαι, I strain after.
ἐπενδύτης, a coat, outer wrap.
ἐπερώτημα = ἐρώτημα, a request.
ἐπιγαμβρεύω, I take to wife after.
ἐπιγίνομαι, I come on, supervene.

words.g: I make an additional testamentary disposition
words.s: ἐπιδιατάσσομαι, I make an additional testamentary disposition, I furnish with additions.

words.g: I put besides into a state of order, I put in order
words.s: ἐπιδιορθόω, I put besides into a state of order, I put in order.
ἐπιδύω, I sink, set.

words.g: at the point of death, doomed to death
words.s: ἐπιθανάτιος, at the point of death, doomed to death.
ἐπιθυμητής, a longer after, luster after.
ἐπικαθίζω, I sit.
ἐπικάλυμμα, a covering, pretext.

words.g: I put a cover on, cover up
words.s: ἐπικαλύπτω, I put a cover on, cover up.

words.g: I beach, run aground, drive a ship on to
words.s: ἐπικέλλω, I beach, run aground, drive a ship on to.

words.g: an Epicurean, one who holds the tenets of Epicurus
words.s: Ἐπικούρειος, an Epicurean, one who holds the tenets of Epicurus (341–270 B.C.).
ἐπικουρία, succour (against foes), help.
ἐπικρίνω, I give decision, decide.
ἐπιλείπω, I fail, leave behind.
ἐπιλείχω, I lick.
ἐπιλησμονή, forgetting, in James i 25 a Hebraistic gen. = that forgets.
ἐπίλοιπος, remaining, that is left over.
ἐπίλυσις, solution, explanation, interpretation.
ἐπιμαρτυρέω, I call to witness.
ἐπιμέλεια, care, attention.
ἐπιμελῶς, carefully, attentively.
ἐπινεύω, I consent.
ἐπίνοια, thought.
ἐπιορκέω, ἐφιορκέω, I take an oath, swear.
ἐπίορκος, perjuring, a perjurer.
ἐπιπλήσσω, I reprove.
ἐπιπόθητος (desiderabilis, desiderantissimus), longed for, missed.
ἐπιποθία, longing, eager desire.
ἐπιπορεύομαι, I journey (to).
ἐπιράπτω, I sew (on).
ἐπισιτισμός, provision, nourishment, food.
ἐπισκευάζομαι, I equip (horses).
ἐπισκηνόω, I raise a tent (over).

words.g: I undo the effects of circumcision on myself
words.s: ἐπισπάω (lit. I draw over), mid. I undo the effects of circumcision on myself.
ἐπισπείρω, I sow above (over), I resow.
ἐπιστήμων, knowing by experience (personal acquaintance).
ἐπιστομίζω, I muzzle, silence.
ἐπιστροφή, a turning (to God).
ἐπισυντρέχω, I run together to (towards).
ἐπισφαλής, dangerous.
ἐπισχύω, I persist, insist.
ἐπισωρεύω, I heap up.
ἐπιτήδειος, necessary.
ἐπιτιμία, punishment.
ἐπιτροπή, commission.
ἐπιφανής, manifest.
ἐπιφαύσκω, I shine upon.
ἐπιχέω, I pour on.

words.g: I name, impose a name on
words.s: ἐπονομάζω, I name, impose a name on.
ἐπόπτης (originally of one initiated into the mysteries, but also found of a surveyor, supervisor), an eyewitness.
ἔπος, a word: ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν (a literary phrase), one might almost say, modifying a statement, Heb. vii 9.
ἑπτακισχίλιοι, seven thousand.
ἐρείδω, I strike; I run aground (of a ship).
ἐρεύγομαι, (lit. I belch forth, hence) I utter, declare.
ἐρίζω, I strive.
ἐρίφιον, a goat, or kid.
Ἑρμᾶς, Hermas, a Roman Christian.

words.g: Hermogenes, a faithless Christian at Rome
words.s: Ἑρμογένης, Hermogenes, a faithless Christian at Rome.
ἐρυθρός, red.

words.g: Eslei, son of Naggai and father of Nahum
words.s: Ἐσλεί (Hebr.), Eslei, son of Naggai and father of Nahum.

words.g: ἐσχάτως ἔχειν, to be at the extremity
words.s: ἐσχάτως: ἐσχάτως ἔχειν, to be at the extremity, to be ‘in extremis’, to be at the last gasp.
ἑτερόγλωσσος, speaking another language.

words.g: I am yoked with one different from myself, unequally yoked
words.s: ἑτεροζυγέω, I am yoked with one different from myself, unequally yoked.
ἑτέρως, differently.
ἑτοιμασία, (in LXX, a stand, base, but also) readiness (of bearer of good tidings).
εὐαρέστως, in a well-pleasing way.

words.g: Eubulus, a Christian with St. Paul in Rome
words.s: Εὔβουλος, Eubulus, a Christian with St. Paul in Rome.
εὖγε, interj. well done! bravo!
εὐδία, fair weather, good weather.

words.g: I do good deeds, perform kind service, benefit
words.s: εὐεργετέω, I do good deeds, perform kind service, benefit.

words.g: Benefactor, an honorary title of kings and governors
words.s: εὐεργέτης, Benefactor, an honorary title of kings and governors.
εὔθυμος, in good spirits.
εὐθύμως, with good courage.
εὐθύτης, straightness, uprightness.
εὐλαβέομαι (cf. εὐλάβεια), I am anxious, περί, about.
εὐμετάδοτος, willingly sharing, ready to impart.
Εὐνίκη, Eunice, mother of Timothy.
εὐνοέω, I have good-will.
εὔνοια, good-will.
Εὐοδία, Euodia, Evodia, or rather Euhodia, a Christian woman of Philippi.
εὐπάρεδρος, promotive of fit waiting on.
εὐπειθής, compliant.
εὐπερίστατος, easily surrounding, easily encircling.
εὐποιία, good doing. doing of good.
εὐπορέομαι, I am prosperous.
εὐπορία, wealth, gain.
εὐπρέπεια (with a notion of stateliness or majesty), glory.

words.g: I look well, I make a fair show
words.s: εὐπροσωπέω, I look well, I make a fair show (a good outward appearance, and so win good opinion).
Εὐρακύλων, Euraquilo, an East-north-east wind.
εὐρύχωρος, broad.
εὔσημος, with clear meaning.
εὐσχημοσύνη, comeliness.
εὐτραπελία, versatility (especially of speech); facetiousness, raillery.

words.g: Eutychus, a young hearer of St. Paul at Troas
words.s: Εὔτυχος, Eutychus, a young hearer of St. Paul at Troas.
εὐφημία, good reputation.
εὔφημος, well reported of.

words.g: I bear well, I bring a good harvest
words.s: εὐφορέω, I bear well, I bring a good harvest.
εὐχάριστος, thankful.
εὐψυχέω, I am of good cheer.
ἐφάλλομαι, I leap upon.
ἐφευρετής, a finder out, discoverer.

words.g: for the day, for a day
words.s: ἐφήμερος, for the day, for a day.

words.g: Ephraim, a city of uncertain situation
words.s: Ἐφραΐμ, Ephraim, a city of uncertain situation.
ἐφφαθά (Aramaic, meaning) be opened up.

words.g: Zara, son of Judah and Thamar
words.s: Ζαρά (Hebr.), Zara, son of Judah and Thamar.
ζευκτηρία, a band, a fastening.
ζηλεύω, I am zealous.
Ζηνᾶς (pet form of Ζηνόδυτος or Ζηνόδωρος), Zenas, a lawyer in Rome.
ἡγεμονία, rule, authority.
ἦθος, a habit.

words.g: Heli, the father of Joseph, husband of Mary
words.s: Ἡλεί (Hebr.), Heli, the father of Joseph, husband of Mary, according to Lk.
ἡμιθανής, half-dead.
ἡμίωρον, half an hour, but see ὥρα.
ἤπερ, an intensified ἤ, than.

words.g: Er, son of Joshua and father of Elmadam
words.s: Ἤρ (Hebr.), Er, son of Joshua and father of Elmadam.
ἤρεμος, undisturbed.
Ἡρῳδίων, Herodion, a Christian in Rome, a ‘relative’ of St. Paul.
ἤτοι, or of course.

words.g: I make a sound, give forth a sound, sound
words.s: ἠχέω, I make a sound, give forth a sound, sound (when struck).

words.g: Thamar, Tamar, mother of Phares and Zara by Judah
words.s: Θάμαρ (Hebr.), Thamar, Tamar, mother of Phares and Zara by Judah, son of Jacob.
θανάσιμος (mortifer), deadly.
θανατηφόρος, death-bringing, deadly.

words.g: Thara, Terah, the father of Abraham
words.s: Θαρά (Hebr.), Thara, Terah, the father of Abraham.
θάρσος, courage.
θαυμάσιος, wonderful.
θεά, a goddess.

words.g: I make a public show of, I expose to public shame
words.s: θεατρίζω, I make a public show of, I expose to public shame.
θειότης (diuinitas), divinity.
θειώδης, of brimstone, sulphurous.
θέλησις, willing, will.
θεοδίδακτος, taught by the god.
θεομάχος, fighting against the god.

words.g: inspired by the god, due to the inspiration of the god
words.s: θεόπνευστος, inspired by the god, due to the inspiration of the god.
θεοσέβεια, reverence for the god.
θεοσεβής, devout, religious.
θεοστυγής, hating the god.
θεότης (deitas), deity, godhead.
θεράπων, a servant, slave.
θέρμη, heat.

words.g: Theudas, a Jewish pretender of date about 4 B.C
words.s: Θευδᾶς, Theudas, a Jewish pretender of date about 4 B.C., otherwise unknown.
θεωρία (spectaculum), a sight.
θήκη, a scabbard, a sheath.
θήρα, hunting, entrapping.

words.g: I hunt, I seek to catch or entrap
words.s: θηρεύω, I hunt, I seek to catch or entrap.
θηριομαχέω, I fight with wild beasts (i. e. wild beasts in human form).
θορυβάζω, I disturb greatly.
θραύω, I crush.
θρέμμα, (lit. a nursling, hence probably) plur. cattle (rather than household, slaves).
θρῆσκος (religiosus) (refers probably to a careful observance of religious restrictions), religious (probably in a limited sense), James i 26.
θρόμβος, a clot.
θύελλα (procella), a storm, tempest.
θύϊνος, of the sandarach (so-called citron) tree.

θυμιατήριον, (ordinarily censer, but) either the altar of incense (Exod. xxx 1-10), or the shovel, on which the high-priest poured the coals, when he entered the Holy of Holies on the Day of Atonement (Lev. xvi 12).
θυμιάω, I burn incense.
θυμομαχέω, (lit. I fight desperately, hence) I am furiously angry with.

words.g: I am full of angry passion
words.s: θυμόομαι, I am full of angry passion.
θυρεός (scutum), the heavy oblong Roman shield.

words.g: Jambres, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh
words.s: Ἰαμβρῆς, Jambres, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh (v. l. Μαμβρῆς).

words.g: Jannai, an ancestor of Jesus, son of Joseph
words.s: Ἰανναί (Hebr.), Jannai, an ancestor of Jesus, son of Joseph, and father of Melchi.

words.g: Jannes, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh
words.s: Ἰαννῆς, Jannes, a sorcerer at the court of the Pharaoh (v. l. Ἰαμνῆς).

words.g: Jareth, son of Maleleel and father of Enoch
words.s: Ἰάρετ (Hebr.), Jareth, son of Maleleel and father of Enoch.

words.g: Idumaea, Edom, a district of Arabia
words.s: Ἰδουμαία, Idumaea, Edom, a district of Arabia, immediately S. of Judaea.
ἱδρώς, sweat, perspiration.

words.g: Jezebel, name given to a false prophetess of Thyatira
words.s: Ἰεζάβελ (Zezabel, Old Latin and Armenian), Jezebel, name given to a false prophetess of Thyatira, possibly borrowed from the name of Ahab’s wife, queen of Israel (1 Kings xvi 31, &c.).

words.g: Hierapolis, a city of the Lycus valley in Phrygia
words.s: Ἱεράπολις, Hierapolis, a city of the Lycus valley in Phrygia, near Laodicea and Colossae.
ἱερατεύω, I serve as priest.

words.g: slain as sacred, slain in sacrifice
words.s: ἱερόθυτος, slain as sacred, slain in sacrifice.

words.g: like those employed in sacred service
words.s: ἱεροπρεπής, like those employed in sacred service.
ἱεροσυλέω, I rob temples.
ἱερόσυλος, a robber of temples, but possibly simply sacrilegious.
ἱερουργέω, I sacrifice.

words.g: Jephthah, one of the Judges of Israel
words.s: Ἰεφθάε (Hebr.), Jephthah, one of the Judges of Israel.
ἱκανότης, sufficiency, ability, power.
ἱκετηρία (originally ἱ. ῥάβδος, the olive branch held in the hand of the suppliant), supplication, entreaty.
ἰκμάς, moisture.
ἱλαρός, cheerful.
ἱλαρότης, cheerfulness.

words.g: Illyricum, a Roman province, afterwards called Dalmatia
words.s: Ἰλλυρικόν, Illyricum, a Roman province, afterwards called Dalmatia, bounded by Pannonia on the N., Macedonia on the S., Moesia on the E., and the Adriatic Sea on the W.
Ἰουδαΐζω, I live as a Jew (in religion, ceremonially).
Ἰουδαϊκός, Jewish, Judaic.
Ἰουδαϊκῶς, in the manner of Jews (religiously, ceremonially).
Ἰουλία, Julia, a Roman Christian, probably a slave or freedwoman of the Imperial household.
Ἰουνία, Junia, a Roman Christian.
ἱππικός, adj. used as collective subst. cavalry.
ἰσάγγελος, like the angels.
ἰσότιμος, equally privileged, equal.
ἰσόψυχος, likeminded.
Ἰσσαχάρ (Hebr.), Issachar, one of the sons of Jacob and founder of a tribe of Israel.
ἱστορέω, I visit, see (some person or object of importance) (rendered ‘inspicio’ in one inscription).
ἴσως, perhaps (cf. Eng. likely).

words.g: Italic, the name of a cohort forming part of the Syrian army
words.s: Ἰταλικός, Italic, the name of a cohort forming part of the Syrian army.
Ἰτουραῖος, Ituraean, an adjective applied to a district (χώρα), also called Trachonitic, about 60 miles E. of the Sea of Galilee, and partly inhabited by the nomad tribe called Ituraeans (Ἰτουραῖοι).

words.g: Joanan, Johanan, one of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Ἰωανάν (Hebr.), Joanan, Johanan, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

words.g: Job, the hero of the Old Testament book of that name
words.s: Ἰώβ (Hebr.), Job, the hero of the Old Testament book of that name.
Ἰωδά (Hebr.), Jodah, an ancestor of Jesus.
Ἰωρείμ (Hebr.), Jorim, an ancestor of Jesus.
Ἰωσήχ (Hebr.), Josech, an ancestor of Jesus.
ἰῶτα, yod, the Hebrew or rather Aramaic letter which was smallest of all.
καθά (i. e. καθ’ ἅ, according to which things), as.
καθαίρω, I cleanse, purify.

words.g: I lay hold of, I fasten on to
words.s: καθάπτω, I lay hold of, I fasten on to, of a snake with short teeth harmless to the skin.
καθαρότης, cleanness.
καθημερινός, daily.
καθόλου (i. e. καθ’ ὅλου), at all.

words.g: I arm completely, I arm cap-à-pie
words.s: καθοπλίζω, tr. I arm completely, I arm cap-à-pie.
καθοράω, I see clearly.

words.g: according to the very manner in which, even as
words.s: καθώσπερ, according to the very manner in which, even as.
καίτοιγε, and yet.
κακοήθεια, evilmindedness, the tendency to put the worst construction on everything.
κακοπάθεια, experience of evil, suffering.
κάκωσις, ill-treating, ill treatment.
καλάμη, stubble.
καλλιέλαιος, a cultivated olive-tree.

words.g: a teacher of that which is noble (honourable)
words.s: καλοδιδάσκαλος, a teacher of that which is noble (honourable).
καλοποιέω, I do the noble (honourable) thing.

words.g: the Candace, a dynastic name for queens of the Ethiopians
words.s: Κανδάκη, the Candace, a dynastic name for queens of the Ethiopians in Abyssinia.

words.g: I hawk, trade in, deal in for purposes of gain
words.s: καπηλεύω, I hawk, trade in, deal in for purposes of gain.
καρποφόρος, fruit-bearing.
καρτερέω, I persevere, endure.
καταβαρέω, I burden, oppress.
καταβαρύνω, I weigh down, make heavy.
κατάβασις, descent.

words.g: I bring down, I cause to go down
words.s: καταβιβάζω, I bring down, I cause to go down.

words.g: of the umpire in a contest, I decide against
words.s: καταβραβεύω, of the umpire in a contest, I decide against, take part against, condemn (perhaps with the idea of assumption, officialism).

words.g: a reporter, announcer, proclaimer, herald, setter forth
words.s: καταγγελεύς, a reporter, announcer, proclaimer, herald, setter forth.
καταγωνίζομαι (debello), I subdue (in warfare).
καταδέω, I bind up.
κατάδηλος, quite clear.
καταδίκη, sentence of condemnation, condemnation.
καταδιώκω, I hunt down.
κατάθεμα, an accursed thing.
καταθεματίζω, I curse.
κατακληρονομέω, I give as an inheritance.
κατακλύζω, I flood over, overwhelm.
κατακόπτω, I beat.
κατακρημνίζω, I throw down a precipice.
κατάλαλος, speaking against; a backbiter.

words.g: I enter in a list, register
words.s: καταλέγω, I enter in a list, register.

words.g: I stone down, stone to death, overwhelm with stones
words.s: καταλιθάζω, I stone down, stone to death, overwhelm with stones.
κατάλοιπος, left behind; οἱ κατάλοιποι (reliqui), the rest, the remainder.

words.g: I understand, take in a fact about
words.s: καταμανθάνω, I understand, take in a fact about.
καταμένω, I wait, Ac. i 13; I stay, πρός, with, 1 Cor. xvi 6.
καταναλίσκω, I consume utterly.
κατανεύω, I nod, make a sign.
κατάνυξις, deep sleep, torpor, insensibility.
κατανύσσομαι, met. I am pierced, stung.
καταπλέω, I sail down (from the high seas to the shore).
καταριθμέω, I number.
κατάρτισις, restoration.

words.g: bringing to a condition of fitness, perfecting
words.s: καταρτισμός, bringing to a condition of fitness, perfecting.
κατασκιάζω, I overshadow.
κατασκοπέω, I spy out.
κατάσκοπος, a spy.
κατασοφίζομαι, I circumvent by trickery.
κατάστημα (a man's outward bearing, including gait, posture, expression of countenance, dress, &c., involving the idea of calmness and composure), demeanour, deportment.
καταστολή, garb, clothing.

words.g: I exercise my youthful vigour against
words.s: καταστρηνιάω, I exercise my youthful vigour against.
καταστρώννυμι, I scatter on the ground.
κατασύρω, I drag (down).
κατασφάζω, I slaughter.
κατασφραγίζω, I seal and thus close.
κατατομή, a word-play with περιτομή, a cutting up, spoiling.
κατατρέχω, I run down.
καταφθείρω, I destroy, I corrupt.
καταφρονητής, a despiser.
καταχθόνιος, under the earth, subterranean.
καταψύχω, I cool, I refresh.
κατείδωλος, full of images of gods.
κατευλογέω, I bless.
κατεφίστημι, aor. intr. I set upon.
κατήγωρ (an abbreviated vulgar form of κατήγορος), an accuser.

words.g: a downcast countenance as a sign of sorrow
words.s: κατήφεια, a downcast countenance as a sign of sorrow, gloominess, gloom, dejection.
κατιόομαι, I am rusted.
κατοίκησις, dwelling, abode.
κατοικία, dwelling, habitation.
κατοικίζω, I take up a dwelling, but probably κατῴκισεν is an itacistic error for κατῴκησεν (from κατοικέω), as κατοικίζω is properly transitive.
κατοπτρίζομαι, mid. for act., I mirror, reflect: elsewhere mid. = I gaze upon myself in a mirror.
κάτω, (a) down, below, also downwards; (b) compar. κατωτέρω, lower, under, less, of a length of a time, Mt. ii 16.
κατώτερος, compar. adj. lower, Hebraistic, with ref. to Sheol.
Καῦδα, Cauda (mod. Gaudho), an island twenty-three miles south of the Western end of Crete (v. l. Κλαῦδα, see my apparatus).
καῦσις, burning.

words.g: I cauterize, I burn with a hot iron
words.s: καυστηριάζω, I cauterize, I burn with a hot iron: hence met. I sear.
κέδρος, a cedar: in John xviii 1 τῶν Κέδρων is probably due to a popular misunderstanding of the original name τοῦ Κεδρών (Kidron, 1 Kings ii 37, &c.), especially as cedars grew in the vicinity.

words.g: a kind of girdle made of cords
words.s: κειρία, a kind of girdle made of cords: a bandage.

words.g: a word of command, a call
words.s: κέλευσμα, a word of command, a call.
κενοδοξία (cenodoxia), vainglory.
κενόδοξος, vainglorious.
κενῶς, falsely.

words.g: of clay, made by a potter
words.s: κεραμικός, of clay, made by a potter.
κέραμος, a tile; οἱ κέραμοι, practically the roof.
κεράτιον, a husk (pod) of the carob (siliqua graeca).
κέρμα, a small coin: plur. small change.

words.g: a changer of large into smaller coins, a money-changer
words.s: κερματιστής, properly a changer of large into smaller coins, a money-changer.
κεφαλιόω, I wound in the head.
κεφαλίς, (lit. little head, then the knob at the end of the wooden core of a roll of papyrus, then) a roll.
κημόω (from κῆμος, a muzzle), I muzzle.
κηπουρός, keeper of a garden.

words.g: a sea monster, a huge sea fish
words.s: κῆτος, a sea monster, a huge sea fish.
κιννάμωμον (a Semitic word), cinnamon.

words.g: Claudia, a Christian woman in Rome
words.s: Κλαυδία, Claudia, a Christian woman in Rome; if historical, probably a freedwoman of the imperial household.
κλέμμα, a theft.
Κλεόπας, Cleopas, one of the two companions of the risen Jesus from Jerusalem to Emmaus.
κλέος, glory, fame.

words.g: Clement, a fellow-worker of St. Paul in Rome
words.s: Κλήμης (Latin, = Clemens), Clement, a fellow-worker of St. Paul in Rome.

words.g: I choose by lot, I appoint by lot
words.s: κληρόω, lit. I choose by lot, I appoint by lot; hence I assign; mid. I assign to myself, choose; pass. I am assigned, I am chosen as God's portion (κλῆρος), Eph. i 11.

words.g: a couch or litter of a sick person
words.s: κλινάριον, a couch or litter of a sick person.
κλισία, properly a dining couch; hence a group of diners.

words.g: I toss as in a storm at sea
words.s: κλυδωνίζω, I toss as in a storm at sea.

words.g: Clopas, husband of one Mary, who stood by the cross
words.s: Κλωπᾶς, Clopas, husband of one Mary, who stood by the cross.
κνήθω, I rub, tickle: κνηθόμενοι τὴν ἀκοήν, with ears itching with eagerness to hear pleasant things, 2 Tim. iv 3.

words.g: Cnidus, a town on the coast of Caria
words.s: Κνίδος, Cnidus, a town on the coast of Caria (SW. Asia Minor) near the island of Cos.
κοίμησις, sleeping, followed by constituent gen. τοῦ ὕπνου, which is slumber.
κοινωνικός, willing to share.
κοιτών (cubiculum), bed-chamber: ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ κοιτῶνος (cubicularius), chamberlain.
κολακεία (adulatio), flattery, with a view to advantage or gain.
κολλούριον, eye-salve.

words.g: Colossae, a town of the Roman province Asia
words.s: Κολοσσαί, Colossae, a town of the Roman province Asia, in the Lycus valley, near Laodicea and Hierapolis.
κολυμβάω, (properly I dive; hence) I swim.
κολωνία (Latin, = colonia), a colony, a city settlement of Roman (soldier) citizens; a garrison city.
κόμη, hair, long hair.
κομψῶς (colloquial), nicely, finely, bravely.

words.g: beating of the breast or head in lamentation
words.s: κοπετός (planctus), beating of the breast or head in lamentation, lamentation.
κοπή (caedes), slaughter.
κοπρία, manure.
κόπριον, manure.
κόραξ, a raven.
κορβάν (Aramaic), a gift.
κορβανᾶς, the temple treasure.
Κορέ (Hebr.), Korah (Num. xvi 1 ff.).
κόρος (Hebr.), a (dry) measure, equivalent to ten Attic μέδιμνοι or 120 gallons.
κοσμοκράτωρ, ruler of this world, that is, of the world as asserting its independence of God; used of the angelic or demonic powers controlling the sublunary world, cf. ἀρχή, ἐξουσία, στοιχεῖον.

words.g: Quartus, a Christian, brother of Erastus the Corinthian
words.s: Κούαρτος, Quartus, a Christian, brother of Erastus the Corinthian. Cf. ἀδελφός.
κούμ (κοῦμι) (Aramaic), arise.
κουφίζω, I lighten.
κραιπάλη (crapula), surfeiting.
