κραταιός, strong, powerful.

words.g: Crescens, a Christian, coadjutor of St. Paul
words.s: Κρήσκης (Latin, = Crescens), Crescens, a Christian, coadjutor of St. Paul.
κριθή, barley.
κριτικός, able to judge.
κρύπτη (κρυπτή), a hidden place, cf. κρυπτός.
κρυσταλλίζω, I am clear as crystal.
κρυφῆ, in secret, secretly.
κτήτωρ, a possessor, owner.
κτίστης (often of the founder of a city), creator, God.
κυβεία, (lit. playing with dice, gaming, hence) trickery, sleight.
κυβέρνησις (lit. steering, piloting), governing, government, supposed to refer to such duty as was, later at least, performed by any presbyter or by that presbyter who was ἐπίσκοπος.
κυκλεύω, I encircle, invest, enclose.
κυλισμός, rolling, wallowing.
κύμβαλον, a cymbal.

words.g: cummin, a plant used as a spice
words.s: κύμινον (a Semitic word), cummin, a plant used as a spice.
κύπτω, I stoop.

words.g: Cyrene, a district W. of Egypt on the Mediterranean coast
words.s: Κυρήνη, Cyrene, a district W. of Egypt on the Mediterranean coast, forming with Crete a Roman province.

Κυρήνιος, Publius Sulpicius Quirinius (ob. A.D. 21), who conducted two censuses of the province Syria, one in 8, 7, or 6 B.C., Lk. ii 2, as plenipotentiary of the Emperor, and another as legatus pro praetore in A.D. 7, Ac. v 37.
κῶλον (membrum), a limb: plur. (membra) bodies.

words.g: a city which in constitution has only the status of a village
words.s: κωμόπολις, a city which in constitution has only the status of a village.
κώνωψ, a gnat, mosquito, referred to proverbially as something small.

words.g: Cos, an island in the Aegean Sea, SW. of Asia Minor
words.s: Κῶς, Cos, an island in the Aegean Sea, SW. of Asia Minor.

words.g: Cosam, son of Elmadam and father of Addei
words.s: Κωσάμ (Hebr.), Cosam, son of Elmadam and father of Addei.
λακτίζω, I kick.

words.g: Lamech, son of Methuselah and father of Noah
words.s: Λάμεχ (Hebr.), Lamech, son of Methuselah and father of Noah.
λαμπρότης, brightness.
λαμπρῶς, sumptuously.
λαξευτός, hewn out of the rock.

words.g: a Laodicean, an inhabitant of Laodicea
words.s: Λαοδικεύς, a Laodicean, an inhabitant of Laodicea.
λάρυγξ, the throat.
Λασέα, another spelling of Λασαία, Lasaea, a city in Crete, about the middle of the S. coast.
λεῖμμα, a remnant, a remainder.
λεῖος, smooth.
λειτουργικός, given to serving (ministration), ministering.
λεπίς, a scale, a scaly substance thrown off from the body.

words.g: belonging to the tribe of Levi, levitical
words.s: λευειτικός, belonging to the tribe of Levi, levitical.
λήθη, forgetfulness.
λῆμψις, receiving.
λῆρος, folly, nonsense, idle talk.

words.g: a freedman, one of the class of manumitted slaves
words.s: Λιβερτῖνος (Latin, = libertinus), a freedman, one of the class of manumitted slaves. A synagogue at Jerusalem appears to have been reserved for them.
Λιβύη, Libya, Africa (in the modern sense).
λιθόστρωτος, paved with stone.
Λίνος, Linus, a Christian in Rome.
λιπαρός, (lit. fat) rich, sumptuous.
λίψ (Africus), the south-west wind, and thus the quarter from which it comes.
λόγιος, eloquent.
λογομαχέω, I battle with (for) words.

words.g: a battling with (for) words, a battle of words
words.s: λογομαχία, a battling with (for) words, a battle of words.
λόγχη, a long lance.
Λυκαονία, Lycaonia; the country of the Lykaones, a district of Asia Minor, comprised within the Roman province Galatia and including the cities Derbe and Lystra.
Λυκαονιστί, in the Lycaonian language.

words.g: Lycia, a small Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor
words.s: Λυκία, Lycia, a small Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.
λυμαίνομαι, I ravage, harry, devastate.
Λυσανίας, Lysanias, tetrarch of Abilene.
λύσις, dissolution, release.

words.g: it is advantageous to, it profits
words.s: λυσιτελέω, impers. 3 sing. it is advantageous to, it profits.
λυτρωτής, a ransomer, a liberator.
Λωίς, Lois, grandmother of Timothy.

words.g: Maath, Mahath, an ancestor of Jesus
words.s: Μαάθ (Hebr.), Maath, Mahath, an ancestor of Jesus.

Μαγαδάν, Magadan. The reading and the site are uncertain. Two views are held with regard to the latter, (a) that it was in the Decapolis near Gerasa; (b) that it was at Meğdel on the western bank of the Sea of Galilee.
μαγία, sorcery, magic.

words.g: Magog, sometimes as name of a people
words.s: Μαγώγ (Hebr.), Magog, sometimes as name of a people, sometimes as name of a country in O.T. (Gen. x 2, Ezek. xxxviii 2, xxxix 6), probably the Scythians; hence, used in apocalyptic literature.
Μαδιάμ (Hebr.), Madiam, Midian, generally taken to mean or to include the peninsula of Sinai.
μαθήτρια, a woman disciple.

words.g: Methuselah, son of Enoch and father of Lamech
words.s: Μαθουσάλα (Hebr.), Methuselah, son of Enoch and father of Lamech.
μάκελλον (Latin, = macellum), meat-market.
μακροθύμως, with long-suffering, patiently.
μακροχρόνιος, long-timed, long-lived.

words.g: Maleleel, Malelehel, one of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Μαλελεήλ (Hebr.), Maleleel, Malelehel, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

words.g: Malchus, a slave of the high-priest at Jerusalem
words.s: Μάλχος (Aram. Malchu), Malchus, a slave of the high-priest at Jerusalem.
μάμμη, a grandmother.

words.g: Manaen, probably a member of Herod Antipas’ court
words.s: Μαναήν (grecized form of Aramaic Menahem), Manaen, probably a member of Herod Antipas’ court.
μανία (furor), raving madness.
μαντεύομαι, I practise soothsaying, suggesting the fraud involved in the practice.
μαραίνω: pass. I die, I wither (like the grass).

words.g: Our Lord hath come, or Our Lord cometh
words.s: μαρὰν ἀθά (Aramaic), either Our Lord hath come, or Our Lord cometh (will come, is at hand).
μάρμαρος (marmor), marble.
μασάομαι, I gnaw.
μαστίζω, I flog, scourge, see μάστιξ.
ματαιολογία, vain speaking, foolish talking.
ματαιολόγος, speaking vain things.

words.g: I am made vain, ineffective, godless
words.s: ματαιόομαι, I am made vain, ineffective, godless.
Ματταθά (Hebr.), Mattathah, an ancestor of Jesus.
μεγαλεῖος: τὰ μεγαλεῖα (magnalia), the mighty deeds.
μεγαλοπρεπής, magnificent, superb, transcendent.
μεγάλως, greatly: compar. μεῖζον.
μέγεθος, greatness.
μέγιστος (elative superlative, practically obsolete and only literary), very great: see μέγας (positive), μείζων (comparative and superlative).
μειζότερος, μείζων, (a) compar. greater (3 John 4); (b) superl. greatest, Mt. xiii 32, xxiii 11, 1 Cor. xiii 13, &c.

words.g: Meleah, one of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Μελεά (Hebr.), Meleah, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
Μελίτη (Μελιτήνη), Malta.

words.g: a parchment leaf, perhaps for notes
words.s: μεμβράνα (Latin, = membrana), a parchment leaf, perhaps for notes.

words.g: blaming one's lot or destiny, discontented
words.s: μεμψίμοιρος, blaming one's lot or destiny, discontented.

words.g: Menna, one of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Μεννά (Hebr.), Menna, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
μεριστής, a divider, partitioner, distributor.
μεσιτεύω, I mediate, interpose; but probably in Heb. vi 17 rather I am surety, I give bail.
μεσότοιχον, mid-wall.

words.g: I am in the middle of my course
words.s: μεσόω, I am in the middle of my course.
μεστόω, I fill.
μεταβάλλω: mid. I change my mind.
μετακινέω, tr. I move away, I dislodge.
μετάλημψις, partaking of, sharing in.
μετατρέπω, tr. I turn, change.
μετέπειτα, thereafter.

words.g: I am μετέωρος, i.e. suspended, anxious
words.s: μετεωρίζομαι, I am μετέωρος, i.e. suspended, anxious, Lk. xii 29.
μετοχή, sharing, partnership.
μετρητής, a measure, about 39·39 litres or 8¾ gallons.
μετριοπαθέω, I feel moderately, with particular reference to displeasure at men's sin.
μετρίως (modice), moderately: οὐ μετρίως, greatly, exceedingly.
μηδέποτε, not at any time.
μηδέπω, not yet.

words.g: a Mede, a Median, from East of Assyria
words.s: Μῆδος, a Mede, a Median, from East of Assyria.
μηλωτή, sheep's (sometimes pig's) hide, sheepskin.
μηρός, thigh.
μήτιγε, a modified μήτι, in elliptical construction, not to speak of.
μητραλῴας, a matricide.
μίασμα, a pollution, a defilement.
μιασμός, pollution, defilement.
μῖγμα, a mixture.
μίλιον (Latin, = milium, a false singular formed from milia [passuum], a thousand double paces), a Roman mile, measuring 1478·5 mètres.
μισθαποδότης (see μισθαποδοσία), a rewarder.
μίσθωμα, a rented apartment or flat.

words.g: Mitylene, the capital of the island of Lesbos
words.s: Μιτυλήνη (earlier Μυτιλήνη, as in the best MSS of the Vulgate), Mitylene, the capital of the island of Lesbos in the northern Aegean sea.

words.g: Mnason, an early Christian, native of Cyprus
words.s: Μνάσων, Mnason, an early Christian, native of Cyprus, resident at a place between Caesarea and Jerusalem.
μνήμη, memory, or mention.
μογιλάλος, (lit. speaking with difficulty, hence) dumb.
μόγις, with difficulty; scarcely, hardly.

words.g: Moloch, a god worshipped by several Semitic peoples
words.s: Μολόχ (Hebr.), Moloch, a god worshipped by several Semitic peoples (name is properly appellation = king).
μολυσμός, staining, contamination, pollution.
μομφή (lit. blame, fault-finding), a complaint, fault.
μορφόω, I form, shape (of the development of the embryo into the fully formed child).

words.g: I make a model of a calf
words.s: μοσχοποιέω, I make a model of a calf.
μουσικός, a musician, but probably in some narrower sense in Rev. xviii 22.
μυελός, marrow.
μυέω, (I initiate into the Mysteries, hence) I habituate.
μυκάομαι, I roar.
μυκτηρίζω (properly, I turn up the nose as a sign of contempt), I sneer at, disdain.
μυλικός, belonging to a mill.
μύλινος, a mill-stone.

words.g: Myra, a port in Lycia, SW. Asia Minor
words.s: Μύρα, Μύρρα, Myra, a port in Lycia, SW. Asia Minor.
μυρίζω, I anoint.

words.g: I half-close the eyes, I blink
words.s: μυωπάζω, I half-close the eyes, I blink.
μώλωψ, a weal, left on the body by scourging.
μῶμος, a blemish (a 'Hebraic' sense peculiar to Biblical Greek; the classical sense is blame).
μωρολογία, foolish talking.

words.g: Naggai, one of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Ναγγαί (Hebr.), Naggai, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

words.g: Nathan, son of David, and an ancestor of Jesus
words.s: Ναθάμ (Hebr.), Nathan, son of David, and an ancestor of Jesus.

words.g: Naaman, commander-in-chief of the army of a king of Syria
words.s: Ναιμάν, Naaman, commander-in-chief of the army of a king of Syria in the ninth century B.C. (2 Kings v).

words.g: Nain, a city SW. of the Sea of Galilee
words.s: Ναΐν, Ναΐμ, Nain, a city SW. of the Sea of Galilee.

words.g: Naum, Nahum, an ancestor of Jesus
words.s: Ναούμ (Hebr.), Naum, Nahum, an ancestor of Jesus.

words.g: Narcissus, a resident in Rome in Nero's time
words.s: Νάρκισσος, Narcissus, a resident in Rome in Nero's time.
ναύκληρος, a captain (master) of a ship.
ναῦς (literary), a ship, a vessel, Ac. xxvii 41 only (an almost obsolete word, rare in the vernacular; see πλοῖον).

words.g: Nachor, one of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Ναχώρ (Hebr.), Nachor, one of the ancestors of Jesus.
νεόφυτος (lit. newly planted), newly converted to Christianity.
νέφος, (lit. a cloud, hence) a dense crowd.
νεφρός, a kidney (as a general emotional centre).
νεωκόρος (lit. temple-sweeper), temple-warden; an honorary title.
νεωτερικός, associated with youth (younger men), youthful.
νή, with an acc. of adjuration, by.
νηπιάζω, I am childish (infantile).
Νηρεί (Hebr.), Nerei, an ancestor of Jesus.
Νηρεύς, Nereus, a Christian in Rome.
νησίον, a little island, an islet.

words.g: Niger, another name of Symeon, a Christian at Antioch
words.s: Νίγερ, Niger, another name of Symeon, a Christian at Antioch.

words.g: Nicanor, one of the original seven 'deacons'
words.s: Νικάνωρ, Nicanor, one of the original seven 'deacons' in the church at Jerusalem.
νίκη, victory.

words.g: Nicolaus, a Jewish proselyte of Antioch
words.s: Νικόλαος, Nicolaus, a Jewish proselyte of Antioch, one of the original seven 'deacons' in the church at Jerusalem.

words.g: Nicopolis, probably the city near Actium in Epirus
words.s: Νικόπολις, Nicopolis, probably the city near Actium in Epirus, N. W. Greece.
νιπτήρ, a basin.
νόθος, a bastard, an illegitimate son.
νόμισμα, a coin.

words.g: legislation (at Sinai), enactment of the Law
words.s: νομοθεσία, legislation (at Sinai), enactment of the Law.
νομοθέτης, a legislator.
νοσέω, I am diseased, hence of mental or spiritual disease.

words.g: a nestling, a young bird in the nest
words.s: νοσσιά (syncopated from νεοσσία), a nestling, a young bird in the nest.

words.g: a nestling, a young bird in the nest
words.s: νοσσίον, a nestling, a young bird in the nest; see νοσσιά.

words.g: a nestling, a young bird, a young one
words.s: νοσσός, a nestling, a young bird, a young one.
νουνεχῶς, reasonably, sensibly.

Νύμφᾰ, Nympha, a woman's name, if we read Νύμφᾰν and αὐτῆς in Col. iv 15, as we probably should; otherwise, Νυμφᾶν will be the accusative of the masculine name Νυμφᾶς, a pet form of Νυμφόδωρος, Nymphas, Nymphodorus.
νύσσω, I prick.
νυχθήμερον, a night and a day (not necessarily more than the latter part of a night and the earlier part of the succeeding day).
νῶτος (dorsum), the back.
ξενοδοχέω, I receive (entertain) strangers.

words.g: a Roman dry measure, rather less than a pint
words.s: ξέστης (Latin, = sextarius), properly a Roman dry measure, rather less than a pint: referred to rather as a household utensil than as a measure.
ὄγκος, (properly bulk, mass, hence) a burden.
ὁδεύω, I am on a journey.

words.g: I am on a journey, I journey
words.s: ὁδοιπορέω, I am on a journey, I journey.
οἰκέτεια (familia), household of slaves.
οἴκημα, a prison (euphemism for δεσμωτήριον).

words.g: I am (master or) mistress of a house
words.s: οἰκοδεσποτέω, I am (master or) mistress of a house.
οἰκοδόμος, a house-builder, a builder.

words.g: I am a steward, I do the work of a steward
words.s: οἰκονομέω, I am a steward, I do the work of a steward.
οἰκουργός, a house-worker, a housekeeper, v. l.

words.g: sottishness, steeping of oneself in wine
words.s: οἰνοφλυγία, sottishness, steeping of oneself in wine.

words.g: I shrink (from), I hesitate, I am afraid
words.s: ὀκνέω, I shrink (from), I hesitate, I am afraid.
ὀκταήμερος, eight days old.
ὀλιγοπιστία, smallness of belief (faith).
ὀλιγόψυχος, pusillanimous, of small courage.

words.g: I hold in low esteem, I make light of
words.s: ὀλιγωρέω (contemno), I hold in low esteem, I make light of.
ὀλίγως, slightly, just.
ὀλοθρευτής, the destroying angel (cf. Num. xvi 41 ff.).
ὀλοθρεύω: ὁ ὀλοθρεύων, the Destroyer, the destroying angel (cf. Exod. xii 23, and ὀλοθρευτής).
ὁλοκληρία, perfect (unimpaired) health.
ὀλολύζω (onomatopoeic), I howl.
ὁλοτελής, complete, rounded off.

words.g: Olympas, a Christian man in Rome
words.s: Ὀλυμπᾶς (pet form of Ὀλυμπιόδωρος probably), Olympas, a Christian man in Rome.
ὄλυνθος, an unripe fig.
ὄμβρος, a rain-storm.
ὁμείρομαι (perhaps a nursery word, derived from a word indicating ‘remembrance’), I long for, c. gen.
ὁμιλία, intercourse, companionship, conversation.
ὁμίχλη, a mist.
ὁμοιάζω, I am like.
ὁμοίωσις, making like; likeness (cf. Gen. i 26).
ὁμολογουμένως, admittedly.
ὁμότεχνος, of the same trade.
ὁμόφρων, of one mind (intent, purpose).
ὀνάριον, an ass (a conversational diminutive).
ὄνειδος, a reproach.
ὀνίνημι, tr. I profit: pass. c. gen. I have joy of.
ὁπλίζω, tr. I arm; mid. I arm myself: especially of defensive armour (breastplate, shield, &c.).
ὁπότε (in classical Greek whenever), when, Lk. vi 3 (v. l. ὅτε).

words.g: I appear, I am seen (by), I let myself be seen (by)
words.s: ὀπτάνομαι, I appear, I am seen (by), I let myself be seen (by).
ὀπτός, broiled.
ὀπώρα, autumn; hence fruit.
ὁρατός, to be seen, visible.
ὀργίλος (iracundus), irascible.
ὄρεξις, eagerness, strong desire.
ὀρθοποδέω, (strictly, I am an ὀρθόπους [a man with straight feet], and therefore πρός = with reference to; but it is possible that we ought to take it) I go straight, πρός, to.

words.g: I cut (or carve) according to rule
words.s: ὀρθοτομέω, perhaps, I cut (or carve) according to rule (and thus, I define according to the norm of the Gospel); if the metaphor be from drawing furrows (understanding τὴν γῆν), then it may be, I cultivate, I am occupied with.

words.g: I rise early, I come in the morning
words.s: ὀρθρίζω, I rise early, I come in the morning.
ὀρθρινός, belonging to the morning; hence, equivalent to adv., in the morning, early.
ὅρμημα, a mighty impulse (impetus).
ὁροθεσία (originally, a laying down [fixing] of a boundary), a boundary.
ὁσίως, religiously, piously.
ὄσφρησις, sense of smell.

words.g: in no way, in no respect, not at all
words.s: οὐδαμῶς, in no way, in no respect, not at all.
οὐκοῦν, (in a question) not really?

words.g: Urbanus, a Christian in Rome, fellow-worker of St. Paul
words.s: Οὐρβανός, Urbanus, a Christian in Rome, fellow-worker of St. Paul.

words.g: Uriah, husband of Bathsheba, the mother of Solomon
words.s: Οὐρίας (Hebr.), Uriah, husband of Bathsheba, the mother of Solomon.
ὀφρύς, (properly the brow; hence) the brow, a ridge (of a mountain).
ὀχλέω, I trouble, torment, worry.
ὀχλοποιέω, I gather a crowd.
ὀχύρωμα, a bulwark, a bastion: hence, met.
ὄψιμος, late in the year (opposite to πρόϊμος).
παγιδεύω, I ensnare, I entrap.
παθητός (passibilis), capable of suffering.

words.g: either a boy or a slave
words.s: παιδάριον (formerly a diminutive), either a boy or a slave.
παιδιόθεν, from childhood, from early boyhood.
παίζω, I play, I sport (includes singing and dancing).
παλαιότης, oldness.
πάλη, wrestling, a wrestling bout; hence a struggle, a conflict.
πανδοχεῖον, an inn, khan, hotel.
πανδοχεύς, an innkeeper, landlord, hotel-manager.
πανήγυρις; a festival assembly.
πανοικεί, with all (his) household.
πανοῦργος, crafty (playfully used).
πανπληθεί, adv. lit. with the whole crowd, almost equivalent to a subject of the sentence.
πανταχῆ, everywhere.
πάντῃ, in every way.

words.g: I cross over, I strike across
words.s: παραβάλλω, I cross over, I strike across.
παραβολεύομαι, I expose myself (to danger).
παραδειγματίζω, I put to open shame.
παράδοξος, unexpected; hence wonderful.

words.g: by the sea (lake), on the coast
words.s: παραθαλάσσιος, by the sea (lake), on the coast.
παραθεωρέω, I look past, overlook, neglect.
παρακαθέζομαι, I sit beside.
παρακαλύπτω, I conceal, veil.

words.g: on the sea-coast, on the sea-board
words.s: παράλιος, on the sea-coast, on the sea-board: ἡ παράλιος (sc. χώρα), the coast country.
παραλλαγή, a variation; hence, a periodic change of a heavenly body.
παραμυθία, encouragement, comfort, consolation.
παραμύθιον, consolation.
παρανομέω, I contravene a statute (law).
παρανομία, a breach of a statute (law).
παραπικραίνω, absol. I embitter, provoke, irritate.
παραπίπτω, I fall back (into the unbelieving and godless ways of the old time).
παραπλέω, I sail past (without stopping there).
παραπλήσιον, in a manner like.
παραπλησίως, correspondingly, in like manner.
παραρέω, (lit. I flow past, I glide past, hence) I am lost, I perish, or merely, I drift away (I fall away) from duty (or the way of salvation).
παράσημος, a figure-head.
παρατείνω, I prolong.
παρατήρησις, a watching for.

words.g: I come by chance, I am by chance in a certain place
words.s: παρατυγχάνω, I come by chance, I am by chance in a certain place.
παραυτίκα, adv. with force of adj., present, immediate.

words.g: I am out of my senses
words.s: παραφρονέω, I am out of my senses.
παραφρονία, madness.
παραχειμασία, spending the winter, wintering.
πάρδαλις, a leopard.

words.g: I have my seat beside, I attend
words.s: παρεδρεύω (adsideo), I have my seat beside, I attend.
παρεισάγω, I introduce from the side.
παρείσακτος, introduced (imported) from the side.
παρεισδύω, I creep in.

words.g: I bring in (import) from the side, I smuggle
words.s: παρεισφέρω, I bring in (import) from the side, I smuggle.
παρεμβάλλω, I throw (raise) up beside.
παρενοχλέω, I trouble, or perhaps, I trouble further.

words.g: overlooking, suspension, remission of punishment for
words.s: πάρεσις (from παρίημι), overlooking, suspension, remission of punishment for.
παρηγορία, a consolation.
παρθενία, maidenhood, virginity.
Πάρθος, a Parthian, an inhabitant of the country beyond the Eastern boundary of the Roman Empire between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf.
παρίημι, (a) I let pass, neglect, omit, Lk. xi 42; (b) I slacken, weary, Heb. xii 12.

words.g: Parmenas, one of the original seven ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem
words.s: Παρμενᾶς (a pet form of Παρμενίδης), Parmenas, one of the original seven ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem.
πάροδος, way-by, passage.
παροίχομαι, I have passed.
παρομοιάζω, I resemble.
παρόμοιος, like, similar.

words.g: the state of feeling provocation, wrath
words.s: παροργισμός (generally act. provocation), the state of feeling provocation, wrath.
παροτρύνω, I urge on.

words.g: Patara, a town on the coast of the Roman province Lycia
words.s: Πάταρα, Patara, a town on the coast of the Roman province Lycia.

words.g: Patmos, a small rocky island in the Aegean sea
words.s: Πάτμος, Patmos, a small rocky island in the Aegean sea, SW. of Ephesus.
πατρικός, belonging to the fathers (ancestors).
Πατρόβας, Patrobas, a Christian in Rome.

words.g: a parricide, a murderer of his father
words.s: πατρολῴας, a parricide, a murderer of his father.

words.g: handed down by (from) one's ancestors, inherited
words.s: πατροπαράδοτος, handed down by (from) one's ancestors, inherited.
πεδινός, level, low-lying.
πειθός, persuasive.
πεισμονή, persuasion, both the act of persuasion and the being persuaded.
πελεκίζω, I behead with an axe.
πένης, poor.
πενθερός, a father-in-law.
πενιχρός, poor.
πεντάκις, five times.
πεντεκαιδέκατος, fifteenth.
περαιτέρω (compar. of πέρα, beyond), further, beyond that.
περιάπτω, I light, ignite.
περιδέω, I bind (tie) around.

words.g: I am active around, I am a busybody
words.s: περιεργάζομαι, I am active around, I am a busybody.
περίθεσις, a putting around (or on).

words.g: a rinsing of a dirty vessel
words.s: περικάθαρμα, a rinsing of a dirty vessel.
περικρατής, mastering, gaining control over.

words.g: I conceal, hide (by putting something around it)
words.s: περικρύπτω, I conceal, hide (by putting something around it).
περικυκλόω, I encircle, invest.

words.g: I await the happening of something
words.s: περιμένω, I await the happening of something.
πέριξ, round about, in the neighbourhood.
περιοικέω, I dwell around (near).
περίοικος, neighbouring; a neighbour.
περιούσιος, of (for) one's own (special, private) possession.
περιοχή, a clause, sentence, short passage.

words.g: I pierce round about (on all sides)
words.s: περιπείρω, I pierce round about (on all sides).

words.g: I rend all round, I tear off
words.s: περιρήγνυμι, I rend all round, I tear off.
περισπάω, I distract, trouble greatly.

words.g: I turn round, I turn, change
words.s: περιτρέπω, I turn round, I turn, change.
περιτρέχω, I run round (around).
περιφρονέω, I lightly esteem; I despise.

words.g: that which is scraped off round anything, a scraping
words.s: περίψημα, that which is scraped off round anything, a scraping.
περπερεύομαι, I show myself off; I am boastful (a braggart).

words.g: Persis, name of a Christian lady in Rome
words.s: Περσίς, Persis, name of a Christian lady in Rome.

words.g: rue, a plant used for flavouring, garnishing dishes
words.s: πήγανον, rue, a plant used for flavouring, garnishing dishes, &c.
πήγνυμι, I fix, pitch; I erect.
πιέζω, I press down.
πιθανολογία, persuasive speech.
πίμπρημι, I cause to swell: passive, I become inflamed, I am swollen.

words.g: a little waxed tablet, on which to write with iron pen
words.s: πινακίδιον, a little waxed tablet, on which to write with iron pen.
πιότης, fatness.
πλανήτης, wandering (probably of shooting stars).
πλάσμα, a moulded thing; a created thing, a creature.
πλαστός (finctus), made up, fictitious.
πλέγμα, plaiting, braiding, dressing the hair.
πλημμύρα, a flooding, flood.
πλησμονή, repletion, satiety.
πλήσσω, I strike.

words.g: a tunic or robe reaching the feet
words.s: ποδήρης (talaris) (properly an adjective in the expression χιτὼν ποδήρης), a tunic or robe reaching the feet.
ποίησις, doing.

πολίτευμα (properly, that which one does as citizen), the constitution; citizenship, franchise; the state, the community, the commonwealth. The word sometimes means a colony of foreigners, whose organization is a miniature copy of the πολιτεία at home, and this gives excellent sense in Phil. iii 20.
πολλαπλασίων (multiplex), manifold, many times over.
πολυλογία, much-speaking, loquaciousness, volubility.
πολυμερῶς, in many portions (one at one time, another at another, and so on).
πολυποίκιλος, much varied, very varied.
πολύσπλαγχνος, full of tender feeling (a Hebraistic idiom, the bowels [σπλάγχνα, which see] being regarded as the seat of compassion and pity, &c.).

words.g: in many ways, under many aspects
words.s: πολυτρόπως, in many ways, under many aspects (with reference probably to different laws or injunctions).
Ποντικός, belonging to Pontus (which see).

words.g: Porcius, the middle (gentile) name of the procurator Festus
words.s: Πόρκιος, Porcius, the middle (gentile) name of the procurator Festus.

words.g: a woman dealer in purple-dyed garments
words.s: πορφυρόπωλις, a woman dealer in purple-dyed garments.

words.g: river-borne, carried off by a river
words.s: ποταμοφόρητος, river-borne, carried off by a river.
πότερον (utrum), whether.
Ποτίολοι, Puteoli (now Pozzuoli), the great harbour for traffic with Alexandria, &c., on the Bay of Naples.
πότος, a drinking bout.

words.g: Pudens, a Christian man in Rome
words.s: Πούδης (Latin), Pudens, a Christian man in Rome.
πραγματεία, business, business transaction.
πραγματεύομαι, I do business, I trade.
πραϋπάθεια, meekness (gentleness) of spirit.
πρεσβῦτις, an old woman.
πρηνής (a medical term, denoting a disease, and corresponding to πίμπρημι, which see), swollen up, inflamed.
πρίζω, I saw, I saw through.
προαιρέομαι, I choose deliberately.
προαιτιάομαι, I make a prior accusation.
προακούω, I hear beforehand.

words.g: a forecourt, a courtyard in the front part of a building
words.s: προαύλιον, a forecourt, a courtyard in the front part of a building.
προβατικός, connected with sheep: προβατική (sc. πύλη) the Sheep Gate of Jerusalem: if κολυμβήθρᾳ be read, προβατικῇ agrees with it.
προβιβάζω, I instruct.
προβλέπομαι, I provide; I resolve on.
προγίνομαι, I happen (come about) previously.
προδίδωμι, I give previously.
πρόδρομος, a forerunner.

words.g: I hope before another, I am the first to hope
words.s: προελπίζω, I hope before another, I am the first to hope.

words.g: I proclaim the good news beforehand
words.s: προευαγγελίζομαι, I proclaim the good news beforehand.
προέχω, I excel, surpass; pass. in Rom. iii 9.

words.g: I lead in front, I give a lead to
words.s: προηγέομαι, I lead in front, I give a lead to.

words.g: a term (or age, date) previously indicated
words.s: προθεσμία, a term (or age, date) previously indicated (fixed, laid down).
προθύμως, eagerly.
πρόϊμος (not πρώϊμος, but from πρό), early in the year (understand ὑετός or some other word meaning rain): reference is to that beginning in October: opposed to ὄψιμος.
προκαλέομαι, I call out, challenge.
προκαταρτίζω, I prepare (arrange) beforehand.
προκηρύσσω, I proclaim previously.
πρόκριμα, prejudgement (favourable or unfavourable).
προκυρόω, I make valid beforehand.
προμαρτύρομαι, I call (God) beforehand to witness.

words.g: I practise beforehand, I prepare, I get up
words.s: προμελετάω, I practise beforehand, I prepare, I get up.
προμεριμνάω, I am anxious beforehand.
προπάσχω, I suffer previously.
προπάτωρ, a forefather.
προσάββατον, the day before the Sabbath, i. e. from 6 p.m. on Thursday to 6 p.m. on Friday.

words.g: I designate as by addressing by a certain title
words.s: προσαγορεύω, I designate as by addressing by a certain title; I recognize as.

words.g: I beg, I am a beggar
words.s: προσαιτέω, I beg, I am a beggar.

words.g: I go up to, I come up to
words.s: προσαναβαίνω, I go up to, I come up to.
προσαναλίσκω, I spend in addition.

words.g: I add a threat (or threats) to the warning
words.s: προσαπειλέομαι, I add a threat (or threats) to the warning.
προσδαπανάω, I spend in addition.

words.g: I need (have need of) something additional
words.s: προσδέομαι, I need (have need of) something additional.

words.g: I permit to go straight onwards
words.s: προσεάω, I permit to go straight onwards.

words.g: I produce in addition, I gain
words.s: προσεργάζομαι, I produce in addition, I gain.
προσηλόω, I nail to.
προσκαρτέρησις, constant attendance, persistence, perseverance, constancy.
προσκεφάλαιον, a pillow or a cushion.
προσκληρόω, I allot (assign) to (as disciples), Ac. xvii 4, where, if the passive has a middle force, we may translate, threw in their lot with.
προσκλίνω, mid. I attach myself to, follow.
πρόσκλισις, inclination; possibly, taking sides, party spirit.
προσκοπή, causing of stumbling (met.).
προσκυνητής, a worshipper.
πρόσλημψις, taking to one's self; assumption into God's favour.
προσορμίζομαι, I anchor at a place.
προσοφείλω, I owe besides (in addition).

words.g: either inclined to hunger or very hungry
words.s: πρόσπεινος, either inclined to hunger or very hungry.
προσπήγνυμι, I fix to anything.
προσποιέομαι, I pretend.
προσπορεύομαι, I come to.
προστάτις (a development of the political sense of προστάτης [patronus], a political sponsor of resident aliens), protectress, patroness.

words.g: a relish, delicacy, or tit-bit eaten with bread
words.s: προσφάγιον, a relish, delicacy, or tit-bit eaten with bread (commonly it would be fish).

words.g: now for the first time made, new
words.s: πρόσφατος (from πρός and the root of φόνος, therefore originally newly slaughtered, fresh-killed), now for the first time made, new.
προσφάτως, freshly, recently.
προσφιλής, lovable, amiable.
πρόσχυσις, pouring upon the altar (as was done in later times, not in that of Moses).
προσψαύω, I touch, handle.
προσωπολημπτέω (from προσωπολήμπτης, Hebraistic, later than LXX), I favour specially.

words.g: a special favourer of one more than of another
words.s: προσωπολήμπτης (from πρόσωπον and λαμβάνειν, Hebraistic, later than LXX; see under the latter), a special favourer of one more than of another, a respecter of persons.

words.g: I stretch forward, I put into a tense posture
words.s: προτείνω, I stretch forward, I put into a tense posture.
προτρέπομαι, I encourage.

words.g: belonging to a προφήτης or to προφῆται, prophetic
words.s: προφητικός, belonging to a προφήτης or to προφῆται, prophetic.
προφθάνω, I anticipate, I forestall.
προχειροτονέω, I appoint beforehand.

words.g: Prochorus, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem
words.s: Πρόχορος, Prochorus, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem.

words.g: I hold the first (chief) place, I am the head
words.s: πρωτεύω, I hold the first (chief) place, I am the head.
πρῶτον (primum), in the first place, first: τὸ πρῶτον (primo), at first, at the beginning.

words.g: one who stands in the front rank
words.s: πρωτοστάτης, one who stands in the front rank, hence a leader, ringleader.
πρωτοτόκια (τά), one's rights as first-born.
πρώτως, for the first time (v. l.).
πτέρνα, heel.
πτηνός, winged; hence as substantive, a bird.
πτόησις, fear, terror (or other violent excitement).

words.g: Ptolemaïs, a coast city of Phoenicia
words.s: Πτολεμαΐς, Ptolemaïs, a coast city of Phoenicia, midway between Tyre and Caesarea.
πτύρω, I frighten, terrify.
πτύσμα, spittle.
πτύσσω, I roll up, close.

words.g: I live the life of a poor man
words.s: πτωχεύω, I live the life of a poor man.

πυγμή, the fist: meaning of Mk. vii 3 (v. l.) still uncertain (‘turning the closed fist of one hand about the hollow of the other’, or ‘as far as the elbow’, or paraphrased by ‘diligently’, ‘carefully’?).
πύθων, a ventriloquist (the utterance being supposed to be due to the presence of a familiar spirit [πύθων] within the body of the speaker).

words.g: I am a boxer, I box
words.s: πυκτεύω, I am a boxer, I box.
πύρινος, as of fire, that is, probably, fire-coloured.

words.g: Pyrrhus, father of the Christian Sopater of Beroea
words.s: Πύρρος, Pyrrhus, father of the Christian Sopater of Beroea.
Ῥαγαύ (Hebr.), Ragau, an ancestor of Jesus.
ῥᾳδιούργημα, a moral wrong, a crime.
ῥᾳδιουργία, (ease in working; so unscrupulousness: hence) fraud, wickedness.
ῥακά (or ῥαχά) (Aramaic), empty foolish.

words.g: Rama, a place in Ephraim, two hours north of Jerusalem
words.s: Ῥαμά; Rama, a place in Ephraim, two hours north of Jerusalem.

words.g: Rachel, younger wife of the patriarch Jacob
words.s: Ῥαχήλ (Hebr.), Rachel, younger wife of the patriarch Jacob.

words.g: Rebecca, wife of the patriarch Isaac
words.s: Ῥεβέκκα (Hebr.), Rebecca, wife of the patriarch Isaac.
ῥέδη (reda, a word of Keltic origin), a carriage.
ῥῆγμα, a breaking up, collapse.
Ῥησά (Hebr.), Resa, an ancestor of Jesus.

words.g: a rhetorician, a professional public speaker
words.s: ῥήτωρ, a rhetorician, a professional public speaker; hence, a barrister, acting as counsel for the prosecution.

words.g: in so many words, expressly, explicitly
words.s: ῥητῶς, in so many words, expressly, explicitly.

words.g: a glance (indicating instantaneousness), flash of an eye
words.s: ῥιπή, a glance (indicating instantaneousness), flash of an eye.
ῥιπίζω (from ῥιπίς, a fire-fan: hence, I fan either a fire or a person), I raise with the wind.

words.g: Rhoda, a maidservant in the house of John Mark's mother
words.s: Ῥόδη (lit. Rose), Rhoda, a maidservant in the house of John Mark's mother at Jerusalem.

words.g: Rhodes, an island in the Aegean sea
words.s: Ῥόδος, Rhodes, an island in the Aegean sea, SW. of Asia Minor.
ῥοιζηδόν (properly expressing the whizzing sound produced by rapid motion through the air), with thunderous crash (roar).

words.g: Reuben, eldest son of the patriarch Jacob
words.s: Ῥουβήν (Hebr.), Reuben, eldest son of the patriarch Jacob and founder of a tribe.

words.g: Ruth, wife of Boes (Boaz) and mother of Iobed (Obed)
words.s: Ῥούθ (Hebr.), Ruth, wife of Boes (Boaz) and mother of Iobed (Obed).
ῥυπαρεύομαι, I am filthy; hence (morally), I am stained with sin.
ῥυπαρία, defilement.
ῥύπος, filth, dirt.
ῥυτίς, a wrinkle of age.
Ῥωμαϊστί, in the Latin language.
ῥώννυμι, I make strong: perf. mid. imperative, a formula of correspondence, at the end of a letter, ἔρρωσο, ἔρρωσθε (uale, ualete), farewell.

words.g: a resting as on the sabbath
words.s: σαββατισμός, a resting as on the sabbath.
σαγήνη, a fishing-net.

words.g: I draw aside, allure from the right path
words.s: σαίνω (properly of dogs, I wag the tail, fawn: then met. I fawn upon, beguile), I draw aside, allure from the right path: perhaps the v. l. σιαίνεσθαι, to be disturbed (troubled), ought to be read.

words.g: Salamis, a city at the eastern end of Cyprus
words.s: Σαλαμίς, Salamis, a city at the eastern end of Cyprus.

words.g: Salim, a place eight Roman miles south of Scythopolis
words.s: Σαλείμ, Salim, a place eight Roman miles south of Scythopolis in the extreme north of Samaria.

words.g: Salmone, a promontory on the east of Crete
words.s: Σαλμώνη, Salmone, a promontory on the east of Crete.
σάλος, a rough sea, surf.
σαλπιστής, a bugler, trumpeter.

words.g: Samothrace, an island south of the province of Thrace
words.s: Σαμοθρᾴκη, Samothrace, an island south of the province of Thrace.

words.g: Samos, an island in the Aegean sea off the coast of Asia Minor
words.s: Σάμος, Samos, an island in the Aegean sea off the coast of Asia Minor, near Ephesus and Miletus.

words.g: Sampson, Samson, one of the Judges of Israel
words.s: Σαμψών (Hebr.), Sampson, Samson, one of the Judges of Israel.
σανίς, a plank, board.

words.g: Sapphira, wife of Ananias, an early Christian
words.s: Σάπφειρα (perhaps from an Aramaic word meaning beautiful), Sapphira, wife of Ananias, an early Christian.
σάπφειρος (Semitic), a sapphire; lapis lazuli.

words.g: a mat-basket, a large basket of flexible material
words.s: σαργάνη, a mat-basket, a large basket of flexible material closed by sewing and usually employed to hold slices of salt fish (raisins and figs are also mentioned).
σαρδόνυξ, sardonyx.

words.g: Sarepta, a town in the district of Sidon in Phoenicia
words.s: Σάρεπτα, Sarepta, a town in the district of Sidon in Phoenicia.

words.g: Sharon, the maritime plain between Carmel and Joppa
words.s: Σαρών, Sharon, the maritime plain between Carmel and Joppa.
σεβάζομαι, I reverence, worship.
σειρός (properly a pit, excavation for the storage of grain), a pit: v. l. σειρά, a chain, fetter.
Σέκουνδος (Latin), Secundus, a Christian of Thessalonica.
Σελεύκεια, Seleucia, on the Syrian coast, the harbour of Syrian Antioch.
Σεμεείν (Hebr.), Semein, an ancestor of Jesus.
σεμίδαλις, the finest wheaten meal.

words.g: Sergius, the middle (gentile) name of the proconsul of Cyprus
words.s: Σέργιος, Sergius, the middle (gentile) name of the proconsul of Cyprus.
Σερούχ (Hebr.), Seruch, an ancestor of Jesus.
Σήθ (Hebr.), Seth, third son of Adam.
Σήμ (Hebr.), Shem, a son of Noah.
σημειόομαι, I mark (notify) for myself; hence, with an idea of disapprobation added.
σήπω, tr. I cause to rot: 2 perf. σέσηπα, I have rotted, I am rotten.
σητόβρωτος, moth-eaten.
σθενόω, I strengthen.
σίδηρος, iron.
σικάριος (Latin, from sica, a stiletto), an assassin, a murderer; with reference to a fanatical Jewish political faction, accustomed to assassinate their opponents.

words.g: an intoxicating drink, a strong fruit-wine
words.s: σίκερα (Aramaic), an intoxicating drink, a strong fruit-wine.
σιμικίνθιον (Latin, semicinctium), an artisan’s working-apron.
σινιάζω, I sift, winnow.
σιρικός (an inexact spelling of σηρικός, adj. formed from Σῆρες, the Chinese, from whose country silk was obtained), silken; silk fabrics (or garments).
σιτίον, food made of corn, bread.

words.g: the same in meaning as the much commoner σιτευτός
words.s: σιτιστός, the same in meaning as the much commoner σιτευτός.

words.g: measure of corn, portion of corn, allowance of corn
words.s: σιτομέτριον, measure of corn, portion of corn, allowance of corn.
σκέπασμα, strictly roofing, shelter, but with special reference to clothing.
Σκευᾶς, Sceva, an inhabitant of Ephesus.
σκευή (a collective noun), tackle.

σκηνοπηγία, sometimes called ἑορτὴ [τῶν] σκηνῶν or ἑορτὴ [τῆς] σκηνοπηγίας, the Feast of Tabernacles (lit. of booth-building), the great festival of the Jews, held in October, originally the Feast of Ingathering.
σκηνοποιός, a tentmaker.
σκληρότης, obstinacy.
σκληροτράχηλος, stiff-necked, stubborn.
σκόλοψ, originally a stake; but commonly in N.T. times a thorn; a splinter: met. referring to some physical trouble.

words.g: a mark to be aimed at
words.s: σκοπός, a mark to be aimed at (e.g. by an archer).
σκύβαλον, sweepings, refuse, especially dirt, dung (popularly used of the human skeleton).

words.g: a Scythian, an uncivilized inhabitant of NE. Europe
words.s: Σκύθης, a Scythian, an uncivilized inhabitant of NE. Europe.
σκωληκόβρωτος, eaten by worms (the word scolex is still used for the tape-worm at one stage of its growth).
σμαράγδινος (ζμαράγδινος), of an emerald.
σμάραγδος (ζμάραγδος), an emerald.
σμυρνίζω, I spice with myrrh.
σορός, a bier.

words.g: Susannah, a woman of the retinue of Jesus
words.s: Σουσάννα, Susannah, a woman of the retinue of Jesus.
σπεκουλάτωρ (Latin), a scout; a courier: also an executioner.

words.g: used properly of a bird picking up seeds
words.s: σπερμολόγος (from σπέρμα and λέγω: a slang term in Ac.), used properly of a bird picking up seeds; hence a parasite, hanger on: also of one who picks up scraps of information and retails them at secondhand, an ignorant plagiarist.
σπιλάς, adjectivally used with ἄνεμος understood, a dirty, foul (lit.), miry wind, perhaps of its effect on the water.
σπορά, quasi-collective, seed.
στάμνος, an earthenware pot (jar).
στασιαστής, a revolutionary.
στατήρ, a stater, that is four drachmae (which see), temple-tax for two persons.
Στάχυς, a Christian man at Rome.
στέμμα (from στέφω, I wreathe), a garland.
στερέωμα (probably a military metaphor), firm foundation, bulwark.
στηριγμός, support.

words.g: a wisp (bundle) of brushwood, twigs or other light growth
words.s: στιβάς, a wisp (bundle) of brushwood, twigs or other light growth.

words.g: a brand burned into, or the mark of a cut made in, the skin of a slave
words.s: στίγμα, properly, a brand burned into, or the mark of a cut made in, the skin of a slave; in Gal. vi 17 τὰ στίγματα are the marks or scars, due to the lictor’s rods at Pisidian Antioch and the stones at Lystra, marking Paul as the slave of Jesus.
στιγμή (lit. a pricking), an instant, a moment.
στίλβω, I gleam, flash.
στόμαχος, the stomach.
στρατολογέω, tr., I enrol in the army.
στρατόπεδον, a camp.
στρεβλόω, (lit. I twist, warp, stretch on the rack, hence met.) I twist, strain.
στρῆνος, wantonness, luxury.
στυγητός, hated, hateful.
συγγενίς, a kinswoman.
συγκυρία, coincidence, chance.
σύγχυσις, confusion, disturbance.
συκάμινος (a Semitic word), the black mulberry tree.
συκομορέα, a sycamore tree.

words.g: I take away from as booty (plunder), I rob
words.s: συλαγωγέω, I take away from as booty (plunder), I rob.
συλάω, I rob.
συλλογίζομαι, I reason together with others.
σύμβουλος, an adviser.

words.g: I cause to share the form (see μορφή) of another
words.s: συμμορφίζω (συνμ.), lit. I cause to share the form (see μορφή) of another, hence in Phil. iii 10 συνμορφιζόμενος = being made to share the experience of.
συμπαθής, sharing the experiences of others.

words.g: a fellow tribesman, one of the same tribe
words.s: συμφυλέτης, a fellow tribesman, one of the same tribe, doubtless with reference to Jews in Thessalonica, all enrolled in one city-tribe.

words.g: grown along with, vitally one with, united with
words.s: σύμφυτος, grown along with, vitally one with, united with.
συμφώνησις, harmony, agreement.
συμφωνία, bagpipes (cf. Dan. iii 5), but perhaps music, symphony.
σύμφωνος, agreeing: ἐκ συμφώνου, by agreement.

words.g: I calculate together, I reckon up
words.s: συμψηφίζω, I calculate together, I reckon up.
συναγωνίζομαι, I struggle (contend) in company with.

words.g: I have table fellowship with, I share a common meal with
words.s: συνᾰλίζομαι (from σύν and ἅλς, ‘salt’), I have table fellowship with, I share a common meal with. (Others take as συνᾱλίζομαι (from σύν and ἁλής, ‘crowded’), I meet with, from time to time.)
συναλλάσσω, I attempt (seek) to reconcile.
συναναπαύομαι, I rest along with.

words.g: I lead away with, I carry along with
words.s: συναπάγω, I lead away with, I carry along with (in good or bad sense according to context): mid. c. dat., I condescend to, Rom. xii 16.
συναπόλλυμαι, I perish along with.

words.g: I send away in some one’s company
words.s: συναποστέλλω, I send away in some one’s company.
συνδοξάζω, I glorify along with.

words.g: a running together, a tumultuous concourse
words.s: συνδρομή, a running together, a tumultuous concourse.
συνεκλεκτός, fellow-chosen, fellow-elect, understand ἐκκλησία.

words.g: I add my testimony to that already given
words.s: συνεπιμαρτυρέω, I add my testimony to that already given.
συνεπιτίθεμαι (lit. I join in attacking), I join in the charge.
συνέπομαι, I accompany.

words.g: rose up together, set upon together
words.s: συνεφίστημι: 2 aor. intr. (the multitude) rose up together, set upon together.
συνζητητής, a discusser, debater.
σύνζυγος, yoke-fellow, companion, colleague (perhaps a proper name).
συνήδομαι, I delight in.
συνηλικιώτης, a contemporary.
συνθρύπτω (lit. I crush to pieces), I weaken thoroughly, unman.

words.g: I treat evilly (with hardship) along with
words.s: συνκακουχέω, I treat evilly (with hardship) along with.
συνκαλύπτω, I veil (cover) completely.

words.g: I bend low, I cause to stoop low
words.s: συνκάμπτω, I bend low, I cause to stoop low.
συνκαταβαίνω, I come down along with (together).
συνκατάθεσις, agreement, union.
συνκατατίθεμαι, I agree with.
συνκαταψηφίζω, I number (reckon) along with.
συνκινέω, I stir violently.

συνκομίζω, I carry (convey) together, i.e. to burial; or I take up for burial; hence I bury (cf. effero): perhaps, however, I get back, recover (the συν- expressing the collecting of the mangled remains).

words.g: I am bent double, bent in two, bowed down
words.s: συνκύπτω, I am bent double, bent in two, bowed down.
συνλυπέομαι, I am greatly pained (grieved).

words.g: a fellow disciple, a fellow scholar
words.s: συνμαθητής, a fellow disciple, a fellow scholar.
συνμερίζω, I cause to share with (in the sacrifices).

words.g: a joint imitator, an imitator along (together) with others
words.s: συνμιμητής, a joint imitator, an imitator along (together) with others.
συνοδεύω, I journey (travel) along with.
συνοδία, a travelling company, caravan.

words.g: I cohabit with, live in wedlock with
words.s: συνοικέω, I cohabit with, live in wedlock with.
συνοικοδομέω, met. I build together.
συνομιλέω, I talk with.

words.g: I am contiguous with, I am next door to
words.s: συνομορέω, I am contiguous with, I am next door to.
συνπαραγίνομαι, I arrive along with.
συνπαρακαλέω, I cheer (encourage) along with.
συνπάρειμι, I am present (here) along with.
συνπεριλαμβάνω, I embrace closely.
συνπίνω, I drink (wine) along with.

words.g: I fall together, I fall in, I collapse
words.s: συνπίπτω, I fall together, I fall in, I collapse.
συνπολίτης, a fellow-citizen.
συνπρεσβύτερος, a fellow-elder.
συνστενάζω, I groan together.
συνστοιχέω (properly a military term, I keep in line or file), I correspond exactly to.
σύνσωμος, sharing in a body: it has been taken as fellow-slave (see σῶμα).
συντέμνω, I cut down; hence I contract, limit, restrict the scope of.
σύντριμμα, destruction, ruin.
σύντροφος, foster-brother: such is the lit. rendering, but it would appear to be a court title, and might therefore be translated a courtier.

words.g: I encounter, come up with, come close to
words.s: συντυγχάνω, I encounter, come up with, come close to.

words.g: Syntyche, a woman member of the church at Philippi
words.s: Συντύχη, Syntyche, a woman member of the church at Philippi.
συνυποκρίνομαι, pass. I dissemble along with.

words.g: I co-operate in a subordinate capacity
words.s: συνυπουργέω, I co-operate in a subordinate capacity.

words.g: I have intercourse with, I associate with
words.s: συνχράομαι, I have intercourse with, I associate with.

words.g: I unite in suffering travail (birth pangs, severe pain)
words.s: συνωδίνω, I unite in suffering travail (birth pangs, severe pain).
συνωμοσία, a conspiracy, plot.
Συράκουσαι (plur. because originally, as in many similar cases, both a citadel and a settlement in the valley), Syracuse, in E. Sicily.
Σύρος, Syrian, belonging to Syria.
Συροφοινίκισσα, Syro-phoenician, i. e. Phoenician (of Syria, in contrast to Carthage and its territory in N. Africa).

words.g: Syrtis, a quicksand off the coast of N. Africa
words.s: Σύρτις, Syrtis, a quicksand off the coast of N. Africa.

words.g: a signal agreed upon between two parties
words.s: σύσσημον, a signal agreed upon between two parties.
συστατικός, recommending, introducing.
Συχάρ, Sychar, a ‘city’ of Samaria.
σφάγιον, a sacrifice (of an animal).
σφοδρῶς, exceedingly.
σφυδρόν, an ankle-bone.
σχολή, a school, or lecture-hall.
σωματικῶς, bodily, in a bodily way, almost = visibly.
Σώπατρος (a pet-form of Σωσίπατρος), Sopater, son of Pyrrhus, and a Christian of Beroea in Macedonia.
Σωσίπατρος, Sosipater, a Christian at Rome.
σωφρονίζω, (lit. I make σώφρων, hence) I admonish, warn.
σωφρονισμός, self-discipline.
σωφρόνως, sobermindedly.
τάγμα (a military term), rank; division.
τακτός, appointed, arranged.
ταλαιπωρέω, I am wretched (afflicted, in distress).

words.g: a talent in weight or size
words.s: ταλαντιαῖος, a talent in weight or size. (But ἀγῶνες ταλαντιαῖοι are games where the value of the prizes amounted to a talent.)
ταλειθά (Aramaic), maiden.
ταπεινόφρων, meek-minded; humble-minded.
ταρταρόω, I send to Tartarus (Tartarus being in the Greek view a place of punishment under the earth, to which, for example, the Titans were sent).
ταφή (sepultura), burial.
τεκμήριον, an infallible proof, a piece of certain (convincing) evidence.

words.g: to bear a child (children), to become a mother
words.s: τεκνογονεῖν, to bear a child (children), to become a mother.
τεκνογονία, child-bearing; motherhood.
τεκνοτροφέω, I bring up children.
τελείως, perfectly, absolutely, with νήφοντες, 1 Pet. i 13.
τελειωτής, a completer, perfecter.
τελεσφορέω, I bring (the fruit) to maturity.
τελευτή (lit. end), death.
Τέρτιος (Latin), Tertius, a Roman (?) Christian, who wrote the Epistle to the Romans at Paul’s dictation.
τεταρταῖος, of the fourth day (Greek idiom often personalises such adjectives), four days since he died.
τετράγωνος, with four corners, square.

words.g: a quaternion, a group of four soldiers
words.s: τετράδιον (quaternio), a quaternion, a group of four soldiers.
τετράμηνος, adj., of four months (understand χρόνος): hence, four months.
τετραπλόος (quadruplex, quadruplus), fourfold, four times as much.

words.g: I cover with, or I convert into, ashes
words.s: τεφρόω, I cover with, or I convert into, ashes.
τήκομαι, I melt (intr.).
τηλαυγῶς (so old MSS. [including W, the Washington (Freer) Gospels], clearly from afar, clearly: but others of equal age read δηλαυγῶς, which see).
Τιβέριος, Tiberius, the second Roman emperor (died A.D. 37).
τιμιότης, preciousness.

words.g: Timon, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem
words.s: Τίμων, Timon, one of the seven original ‘deacons’ at Jerusalem.
τιμωρία, (deserved) punishment.
τίνω, I pay.

words.g: of such character, to the following effect
words.s: τοιόσδε, of such character, to the following effect.
τοῖχος, a wall.
τολμηρῶς, courageously.
τολμητής, a shameless and headstrong man.
τομός, cutting, with cutting power.
τόξον, a bow (and arrows).
τοπάζιον, a topaz.
τοὔνομα (syncopated from τὸ ὄνομα), as adv., by name.
τραπεζίτης (from τράπεζα, money-changer’s table), a money-changer, a banker.
τραῦμα, a wound.

τραχηλίζω (from τράχηλος, ‘neck’, probably referring originally to the bending back of the head in sacrifice so as to expose the neck: but, whatever be the origin of the expression, the met. sense is clear): τετραχηλισμένα, open, manifest.
Τραχωνιτίς, Trachonitic, belonging to Trachon, adj. applied to a hilly region (inhabited by a nomad tribe), considerably to the south of Damascus, called also Ituraean.
τρῆμα, opening, hole; eye of needle (perhaps a favourite term of medical writers).

words.g: a period of three years, three years
words.s: τριετία, a period of three years, three years.
τρίζω, I grind, crunch.
τρίμηνος, lasting three months: acc. neut. as adv. three months.

words.g: having three roofs, with three floors (stories)
words.s: τρίστεγος, having three roofs, with three floors (stories): hence neut. as noun, the third floor, but it is uncertain whether the ground floor was counted or not in this enumeration; if so, we should have to translate, the second floor.
τρισχίλιοι, three thousand.
τρίτον, acc. neut. of adj., generally with definite article, as adv., the third time; third, in the third place, 1 Cor. xii 28.
τρίχινος, made of hair.

words.g: any change undergone by any object
words.s: τροπή, any change undergone by any object; hence referring to night and day, or the waxing and waning of the moon, the solstice, &c.
τροποφορέω, I bear (endure) the ways (disposition) of (v. l.).
τροφός, a nurse (and thus of a mother who suckles her own children).
τροχιά, (orbita [from orbis], a track; hence) a road.
τροχός, (a wheel; hence) the chariot-wheel of man as he advances on the way of life, following his appointed course.
τρυγών, a turtledove.
τρυμαλιά, an opening, hole; an eye of needle.
τρύπημα, a hole; an eye.
Τρύφαινα, Tryphaena, a woman-Christian in Rome.
τρυφάω, I live a luxurious life.
Τρυφῶσα, Tryphosa, a woman-Christian in Rome, perhaps a sister of Tryphaena.
τυμπανίζω (from τύμπανον, ‘drum’ used in worship, then ‘implement of torture’), I break on the wheel.

words.g: by way of example, or typically, prefiguratively
words.s: τυπικῶς, either by way of example, or typically, prefiguratively.
Τύραννος, Tyrannus an inhabitant of Ephesus, probably a rhetorician.

words.g: a Tyrian, an inhabitant of Tyre
words.s: Τύριος, a Tyrian, an inhabitant of Tyre.
τύφομαι, intr. I smoke.
τυφωνικός (from τυφώς, ‘a vehement wind’); ἄνεμος, a heavy eddying squall.

words.g: of the colour of the martagon lily
words.s: ὑακίνθινος, of the colour of the martagon lily, that is, of a dusky red colour.
ὑάκινθος, a sapphire of dusky red colour like the martagon lily.
ὑγρός, moist, full of sap.
ὑδροποτέω, I drink water (alone, not mixed with wine).
ὑδρωπικός, dropsical, afflicted with dropsy.
ὕλη, wood, timber, brushwood.

words.g: under the authority of a husband
words.s: ὕπανδρος, under the authority of a husband.
ὑπείκω, I yield, submit.
ὑπέρακμος, of doubtful meaning; probably of excessive sexual vigour (of the man), rather than past the bloom of youth (of the woman).
ὑπεραυξάνω, intr. I grow exceedingly.
ὑπερβαίνω, intr. I transgress.
ὑπερβαλλόντως, exceedingly.
ὑπερέκεινος, lit. beyond yonder: τὰ ὑπερέκεινα, the places beyond, c. gen.

words.g: I stretch beyond the measure assigned to me
words.s: ὑπερεκτείνω, tr. I stretch beyond the measure assigned to me.

words.g: I pour out so that it overflows
words.s: ὑπερεκχύννω, I pour out so that it overflows.
ὑπερεντυγχάνω, I supplicate on behalf of.
ὑπερηφανία, haughtiness, arrogance.
ὑπερνικάω, I score a heavy victory; I am more than a conqueror.
ὑπερπερισσῶς, most exceedingly.

words.g: I abound exceedingly, I am exceedingly abundant
words.s: ὑπερπλεονάζω, I abound exceedingly, I am exceedingly abundant.
ὑπερυψόω, I elevate greatly (exceedingly).
ὑπερφρονέω, I have high notions.
ὑπέχω, I undergo.
ὑποβάλλω, I suborn.
ὑπογραμμός, (properly a piece of calligraphy, a copy, for children to imitate; hence) a model, a type, which has to be followed.

words.g: liable to (brought under) the judgement of
words.s: ὑπόδικος (a forensic word), liable to (brought under) the judgement of, answerable to.
ὑποζώννυμι, I undergird, frap, that is, I fasten cables vertically round the hull of the ship to prevent the timbers from straining or giving way.
ὑποκρίνομαι, I act the part, pretend.
ὑπόλειμμα, a remnant.
ὑπολείπω, I leave behind.
ὑπολήνιον, a wine-press, probably the lower (ὑπο-) trough, smaller but deeper than the ληνός proper, both being cut out of the solid rock.
ὑπόνοια, a supposition, suspicion.
ὑποπνέω, I blow moderately (gently).
ὑποστολή, withdrawal; shrinking.
ὑποστρωννύω, tr. I spread underneath.

words.g: I run before a wind under the lee of
words.s: ὑποτρέχω, I run before a wind under the lee of.
ὗς, a sow.
ὑφαντός, woven.
ὑψηλοφρονέω, I am haughty (arrogant).

words.g: Phalek, son of Eber, and one of the ancestors of Jesus
words.s: Φάλεκ (Hebr.), Phalek, son of Eber, and one of the ancestors of Jesus.
φανός, (a light, a torch; then) a lantern.

words.g: Fanuhel, Phanuel, father of Anna the prophetess
words.s: Φανουήλ, Fanuhel, Phanuel, father of Anna the prophetess.
φαντάζω, I make to appear; τὸ φανταζόμενον, the appearance.
φαντασία, show, display.

words.g: a hollow place, a hollow, a valley
words.s: φάραγξ, a hollow place, a hollow, a valley.
φάρμακον, a drug; hence plur., of those used in sorcery, and thus sorcery, Rev. ix 21 (v. l.).
φάσις (from φαίνω), information.
φθινοπωρινός (derived from τὸ φθινόπωρον, which itself = φθίνουσα ὀπώρα, ‘the concluding portion of the ὀπώρα’), autumnal, in autumn, when fruit is expected.
φθονέω, I envy.
φιλάγαθος, loving what is good.
φιλάδελφος, loving one’s brothers (fellow-Christians).
φίλανδρος, loving one’s husband.
φιλανθρώπως, kindly.
φιλαργυρία, love of money.
φίλαυτος, loving self.
φιλήδονος, loving (sensuous) pleasure.

words.g: Philemon, a Christian man of Colossae
words.s: Φιλήμων, Philemon, a Christian man of Colossae.

words.g: Philetus, a backsliding Christian at Rome
words.s: Φίλητος, Philetus, a backsliding Christian at Rome.
φιλία, friendship.

words.g: a Philippian, an inhabitant of Philippi
words.s: Φιλιππήσιος (Latin [Philippensis], for the pure-Greek Φιλιππεύς, Φιλιππηνός), a Philippian, an inhabitant of Philippi.
φιλόθεος, loving God.
Φιλόλογος, Philologus, a Roman Christian.
φιλονεικία (see φιλόνεικος), emulation, rivalry.
φιλόνεικος (φίλος and νείκη [νίκη] ‘victory’), contentious.
φιλοπρωτεύω, I love the first (chief) place.
φιλοσοφία, philosophy, in a bad sense, and perhaps identified with ἀπάτη.
φιλόσοφος, a philosopher.
φιλόστοργος, loving warmly (strongly).
φιλότεκνος, loving one’s children.
φιλοφρόνως, with friendly thoughtfulness.
Φλέγων, Phlegon, a Roman Christian man.
φλυαρέω, c. acc. I chatter (gossip) against.
φλύαρος, chattering, gossiping.

words.g: an instrument of terror, an object of fear, a bugbear
words.s: φόβητρον (φόβηθρον, probably more Lukan), an instrument of terror, an object of fear, a bugbear.
Φοίβη, Phoebe, a leading Christian woman in the church at Cenchreae.
Φοῖνιξ, Phoenix (perhaps modern Lutro), a bay on the south coast of Crete.
Φόρον (Latin, Forum), Forum, Market, Market-Town.
Φορτουνᾶτος (Latin), Fortunatus, a Christian of Corinth.
φραγέλλιον (by dissimilation from Latin, flagellum), a lash.
φράζω, I explain, I interpret.
φρεναπατάω (lit. I deceive the mind), I deceive.
φρεναπάτης (see φρεναπατάω), a deceiver; deceiving.
φρίσσω (used properly of the standing of the hair on end with fear), I feel awe.
φρονίμως, wisely, sensibly, prudently.

words.g: I am careful, I take care
words.s: φροντίζω, I am careful, I take care.
φρυάσσω, (properly, of the snorting and neighing of a high-spirited horse; then) I roar, rage.
φρύγανον, brushwood, copse.

words.g: Phygelus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia
words.s: Φύγελος, Phygelus, a Christian of the Roman province Asia who deserted St. Paul.
φυγή, flight.

words.g: I put in prison, I imprison
words.s: φυλακίζω, I put in prison, I imprison.

φυλακτήριον, a phylactery, an amulet, a parchment capsule containing little parchment rolls with the Hebrew texts, Exod. xiii 1–10, 11–16, Deut. vi 4–9, xi 13–21, affixed to the left upper arm or the forehead of men at morning prayer, and regarded as a protection (hence the name) against evil spirits.
φυσικῶς, by instinct.
φυσίωσις, a puffing up (due to conceit).
φυτεία (lit. planting), a plant.
φωσφόρος (lit. light-bringing, lucifer), the day-star (the planet Venus, probably).

words.g: a Chaldaean, one living in southern Armenia
words.s: Χαλδαῖος, a Chaldaean, one living in southern Armenia.

words.g: a worker in bronze, a smith
words.s: χαλκεύς, a worker in bronze, a smith.

words.g: a chalcedony, a small stone of various colours
words.s: χαλκηδών, a chalcedony, a small stone of various colours.
χαλκίον, a bronze vessel.
Χαναναῖος, Canaanitish, Canaanite, a Biblical and archaic name for Phoenician.
χαρακτήρ, a representation.
χάραξ, a mound, rampart.
χάρτης, papyrus, paper.
χάσμα (from χαίνω, I yawn), an intervening space, a chasm.

words.g: I am in the grip of a storm
words.s: χειμάζομαι, I am in the grip of a storm.
χείμαρρος, a winter torrent.

words.g: one who leads a helpless person by the hand
words.s: χειραγωγός, one who leads a helpless person by the hand.
χειρόγραφον, properly, a signature, hence, as a term of a court of justice, (a) a bill, bond, certificate of debt, or (b) any written obligation or agreement.

words.g: cherubin, two golden figures of winged animals
words.s: χερουβείν (Aramaic, while -ειμ is Hebrew), cherubin, two golden figures of winged animals over the mercy-seat (and the ark) in the Jewish tabernacle.

words.g: Chios (modern Scio), an important island in the Aegean Sea
words.s: Χίος, Chios (modern Scio), an important island in the Aegean Sea, off the west central coast of Asia Minor.

words.g: I scoff by gesture and word
words.s: χλευάζω, I scoff by gesture and word.
χλιαρός, lukewarm, tepid.
Χλόη, Chloe, a woman, probably with business connexions either in Corinth or in Ephesus or in both.
χολάω, I am angry with.
χορός, dancing.
χόρτασμα, food, sustenance, corn for man as well as beast.

words.g: Chuza, a steward of Herod Antipas
words.s: Χουζᾶς, Chuza, a steward of Herod Antipas.
χρή, it is fitting, it is congruous to a law or rather standard; the word is somewhat vague.

words.g: a response of God (to an inquiry as to one’s duty)
words.s: χρηματισμός, a response of God (to an inquiry as to one’s duty), an oracle.
χρήσιμος, useful.

words.g: I play the part of a kind person (full of service to others)
words.s: χρηστεύομαι, I play the part of a kind person (full of service to others).

words.g: affectation of kind speech, with insinuating tone
words.s: χρηστολογία, affectation of kind speech, with insinuating tone.
χρονοτριβέω, I waste time.

words.g: with (wearing) a (one or more) gold ring(s) on the finger(s)
words.s: χρυσοδακτύλιος, with (wearing) a (one or more) gold ring(s) on the finger(s).

words.g: a sparkling gem, of gold-yellow colour
words.s: χρυσόλιθος, a sparkling gem, of gold-yellow colour, possibly our topaz, almost certainly not our chrysolite.

words.g: a precious stone of leek-green colour
words.s: χρυσόπρασος, a precious stone of leek-green colour, which sparkled golden-yellow, from India, perhaps fluor-spar, certainly not chrysoprase.
χρώς, skin.
χῶρος (Latin, caurus, corus), the north-west wind, and so, the quarter of the sky from which it comes, north-west.
ψευδαπόστολος, a false apostle, i.e. one who has received no commission from Jesus to preach the Gospel, though he pretends to have received it.
ψευδοδιδάσκαλος, a teacher of false things.
ψευδολόγος, speaking false things, lying; a liar.
ψευδώνυμος, falsely named.
ψεῦσμα, a lie.
ψιθυρισμός, whispering, especially of secret attacks on a person’s character.
ψιθυριστής, a whisperer (cf. ψιθυρισμός).
ψύχομαι, I become cold, met.
ψώχω, I rub.
ὠνέομαι, I buy.
ᾠόν (ouom), an egg.
ὠρύομαι, I roar.
Ὡσηέ (Hebr.), Hosea, the Old Testament prophet.
ὡσπερεί (= ὥσπερ εἰ), even as if, as if.
